<!-- conjecture-1: body_md -->
\label{Mann_conjecture}
    Let $D\colon\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})\to\mathrm{Cat}$ be a $3$-functor formalism. Let ${I},{P}\subset{E}$ denote the wide subcategories of $D$-\'etale and $D$-proper morphisms in ${E}$, respectively. Then $D$ extends uniquely to a lax symmetric monoidal $2$-functor of $(\infty,2)$-categories
    \[
    \mathbf{Span}^2({C},{E})^{{P}}_{{I}}\to{\mathbf{Cat}}.
    \]
<!-- end conjecture-1 -->
<!-- main-1: body_md -->
\label{main_theorem:free_adjointed_2_cat}
    Let ${C}$ be an $\infty$-category, and let ${P},{I}\subset{E}\subset{C}$ be wide subcategories stable under base change in ${C}$. Assume that ${P}$ and ${I}$ are left cancellable and that their morphisms are truncated. Then the canonical functor
    \[
    F\colon\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})\to\mathbf{Span}^2({C},{E})^{{P}}_{{I}}
    \]
    is the free ${I}$-left adjointed and ${P}$-right adjointed functor. That is, for any $(\infty,2)$-category $\mathbb{K}$, the restriction functor
    \[
    \mathrm{Fun}(\mathbf{Span}^2({C},{E})^{{P}}_{{I}},\mathbb{K})
    \to
    \mathrm{Fun}(\mathrm{Span}({C},{E}),\mathbb{K})
    \]
    is fully faithful, and its essential image is spanned by the ${I}$-left adjointed and ${P}$-right adjointed functors.
<!-- end main-1 -->
<!-- main-2: body_md -->
\label{main_theorem:lax_monoidal_free_adjointed_2_cat}
    Let ${C}$ be an $\infty$-category with finite products, and let ${P},{I}\subset{E}\subset{C}$ be wide subcategories stable under base change in ${C}$. Assume that ${P}$ and ${I}$ are left cancellable and that their morphisms are truncated. Then the canonical functor
    \[
    F\colon\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})\to\mathbf{Span}^2({C},{E})^{{P}}_{{I}}
    \]
    is the free lax symmetric monoidal ${I}$-left adjointed and ${P}$-right adjointed functor. That is, for any symmetric monoidal $(\infty,2)$-category $\mathbb{K}$, the restriction functor
    \[
    \mathrm{Fun}^{\operatorname{lax}-\otimes}(\mathbf{Span}^2({C},{E})^{{P}}_{{I}},\mathbb{K})
    \to
    \mathrm{Fun}^{\operatorname{lax}-\otimes}(\mathrm{Span}({C},{E}),\mathbb{K})
    \]
    is fully faithful, and its essential image is spanned by the ${I}$-left adjointed and ${P}$-right adjointed lax symmetric monoidal functors.
<!-- end main-2 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:equiv_between_2ff_and_E_monoidal_intro}
    There is an equivalence of $\infty$-categories
    \[
    \mathrm{Fun}(\mathrm{Span}({C},{E}),\mathrm{Cat})
    \simeq
    {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat}_{\mathcal{C}})(*)
    \]
    between the $\infty$-category of $2$-functor formalisms and the $\infty$-category of $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{C}$-categories.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- main-3: body_md -->
\label{main_theorem:free_E_monoidal_semiadditive}
    ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})[A]$ is the free $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathsf{I}$-cocartesian $\mathsf{P}$-cartesian category generated by $A\in\mathcal{B}$.

    That is, for any $\mathsf{P}$-cartesian, $\mathsf{I}$-cocartesian $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal category $\mathsf{D}$, the canonical functor
    \[
    \underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{E}-\otimes}({\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})[A],\mathsf{D})
    \xrightarrow{\sim}
    \mathsf{D}^A
    \]
    is an equivalence of $\mathcal{B}$-categories.
<!-- end main-3 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
The category ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})$ is an idempotent algebra in ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})(*)$. Moreover, the modules over ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})$ are the $\mathsf{P}$-cartesian and $\mathsf{I}$-cocartesian $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal categories.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- para-1: body_md -->
{\bf Setup}
    \begin{mylist}
        \item Let ${C}$ be an $\infty$-category.
        \item Let ${I},{P},{E}$ be wide sub-$\infty$-categories of ${C}$ that are stable under base change in ${C}$. Here, a wide sub-$\infty$-category ${D}\subset{C}$ is stable under base change in ${C}$ if pullbacks of morphisms in ${D}$ along arbitrary morphisms in ${C}$ exist and again belong to ${D}$.
        \item Assume that ${I},{P}$ are left cancellable and that every morphism in ${I}$ and ${P}$ is truncated.
        \item Assume that ${I},{P}\subset{E}$.
        \item Let $\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})$ be the span $\infty$-category.
        \item For a functor $F:\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})\to\mathbb{K}$ to an $(\infty,2)$-category and a map $f$ in ${C}$, we denote its left-pointing image by $f^*$ and, if $f\in{E}$, its right-pointing image by $f_!$.
    \end{mylist}
<!-- end para-1 -->
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
Let $F:\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})\to \mathbb{K}$ be a functor to an $(\infty,2)$-category. It is called ${I}$-naively left adjointable if $i^*$ has a left adjoint $i_\sharp$ for every map $i$ in ${I}$. It is called ${P}$-naively right adjointable if $p^*$ has a right adjoint $p_*$ for every map $p$ in ${P}$.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
One can compare this with the definition in \cite{CLLuniv}, where a functor ${C}^{\mathrm{op}}\to \mathbb{K}$ is defined to be adjointable if it is naively adjointable and also satisfies some Beck--Chevalley conditions. We circumvent the need to consider the Beck--Chevalley conditions by considering functors from $\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})$ together with an adjointedness property that will be defined below.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
{\bf Adjointed functors}\label{def:adjointed_functors}
    \begin{mylist}
        \item Let $F:\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})\to \mathbb{K}$ be a functor to an $(\infty,2)$-category $\mathbb{K}$.
        \item We say that this functor is ${P}^{(-2)}$-right adjointed if it is ${P}$-naively right adjointable.
        \item Let $F$ be a ${P}^{(n)}$-right adjointed functor. Let $p$ be an $(n+1)$-truncated map in ${P}$. We define a morphism $N_p:p_{!}\to p_*$ from the right-pointing image of $p$ to the right adjoint of the left-pointing image of $p$. We then define a ${P}^{(n+1)}$-right adjointed functor to be a ${P}^{(n)}$-right adjointed functor for which these maps are isomorphisms.
        \item If $F$ is a ${P}^{(n)}$-right adjointed functor and $p$ is in ${P}^{(n)}$, then we have an adjunction $p^*\dashv p_!$ coming from the identification $N_p:p_!\simeq p_*$.
        \item Let $F$ be a ${P}^{(n)}$-right adjointed functor, and let $p:A\to B$ be an $(n+1)$-truncated morphism in ${P}$. Consider the diagram:
        \[
        \begin{tikzcd}
            A \\
            & {A\times_BA} & A \\
            & A & B.
            \arrow["\Delta"', from=1-1, to=2-2]
            \arrow[curve={height=-6pt}, equal, from=1-1, to=2-3]
            \arrow[curve={height=6pt}, equal, from=1-1, to=3-2]
            \arrow["{\pi_2}", from=2-2, to=2-3]
            \arrow["{\pi_1}"', from=2-2, to=3-2]
            \arrow["p", from=2-3, to=3-3]
            \arrow["p"', from=3-2, to=3-3]
        \end{tikzcd}
        \]
        Notice that $\Delta$ is an $n$-truncated map in ${P}$, and so by induction $\Delta_{!}$ is the right adjoint of $\Delta^*$.

        Consider now the following map:
        \[
        p^*p_!\simeq\pi_{1!}\pi_2^*
        \to\pi_{1!}\Delta_!\Delta^*\pi_2^*
        \simeq\mathrm{id}_!\mathrm{id}^*=\mathrm{id}.
        \]
        The first map is part of the functoriality of $F$.
        The second map is given by the unit of the adjunction $\Delta^*\dashv \Delta_!$. This gives the mate $N_p^F:p_{!}\to p_{*}$ as desired. We call this map the norm map of $p$. If $F$ is clear from the context, we write $N_p:=N_p^F$.
        \item We say that $F$ is ${P}$-right adjointed if it is ${P}^{(n)}$-right adjointed for all $n$.
        \item We say that $F$ is ${I}^{(n)}$-left adjointed (resp. ${I}$-left adjointed) if the corresponding functor $F^{\mathrm{co}}:\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})\to\mathbb{K}^{\mathrm{co}}$ is ${I}^{(n)}$-right adjointed (resp. ${I}$-right adjointed).
    \end{mylist}
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- notation-1: body_md -->
By $\operatorname{2Cat}$ we denote the $\infty$-category of $(\infty,2)$-categories. We let $\operatorname{2Cat}_{\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})/}$ be the slice in which we view the $\infty$-category $\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})$ as an $(\infty,2)$-category via the canonical embedding $\mathrm{Cat}\hookrightarrow\operatorname{2Cat}$.
<!-- end notation-1 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
We define the $\infty$-category of $({P},{I})$-adjointed functors to be the full sub-$\infty$-category of $\operatorname{2Cat}_{\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})/}$ spanned by functors which are ${I}$-left adjointed and ${P}$-right adjointed, and denote it by $\operatorname{2Cat}_{\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})/}^{({P},{I}){\operatorname{-adjointed}}}$.
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
In \cite[Definition 2.4]{CLLuniv}, natural transformations between functors ${C}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbb{K}$ are called $({P},{I})$-adjointable if they satisfy a suitable Beck--Chevalley condition.
    The commuting squares arising from those conditions are subsumed in the fact that we care about functors from $\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})$.
    In fact, one can show that the commutative squares arising from the functoriality of $F$ agree with the ones provided by the Beck--Chevalley transformation.
    However, we do not need this in our paper.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:nat_of_norms}
    Let $F:\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})\to\mathbb{K}$ be a functor, and let $G:\mathbb{K}\to\mathbb{K}'$ be a $2$-functor of $(\infty,2)$-categories. Suppose that both $F$ and $G\circ F$ are ${P}^{(n)}$-right adjointed. Let $p$ be an $(n+1)$-truncated map in ${P}$.

    Then we have a canonical homotopy $G(N_p^F)\simeq N_p^{G\circ F}$ of $2$-morphisms in $\mathbb{K}'$.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
We argue by induction on $n$. For $n=-2$, there is nothing to prove.

    Suppose that we know the result for $n$. Let $p_!^F,p_F^*$ denote the $1$-morphisms arising as the images of morphisms in $\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})$ under the functor $F$.
    Let $p_*^F$ denote the right adjoint of $p_F^*$.
    Use analogous notation for $G\circ F$.

    $2$-functors preserve the formation of mates.
    Thus, to show that $G$ sends $N_p^F$ to $N_p^{G\circ F}$, it is enough to show that it sends the mate of $N_p^F$,
    \[
    p_F^*p_!^F\to\mathrm{id},
    \]
    to the mate of $N_p^{G\circ F}$,
    \[
    p_{G\circ F}^*p_!^{G\circ F}\to\mathrm{id}.
    \]

    The mate $p_F^*p_!^F\to\mathrm{id}$ is defined as the following composition of $2$-morphisms:
    \[
    p_F^*p_!^F
    \simeq(\pi_1)_!^F(\pi_2)_F^*
    \xrightarrow{\eta}(\pi_1)_!^F\Delta_*^F\Delta_F^*(\pi_2)_F^*
    \xrightarrow{(N_{\Delta_p}^F)^{-1}}(\pi_1)_!^F\Delta_!^F\Delta_F^*(\pi_2)_F^*
    \simeq\mathrm{id}.
    \]
    The first isomorphism comes from a $2$-isomorphism in $\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})$. The second morphism is a unit of an adjunction in $\mathbb{K}$. The third is the inverse of $N_{\Delta_p}^F$. The fourth comes from a $2$-isomorphism in $\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})$.

    Any $2$-isomorphism from $\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})$ is sent by $G$ to a $2$-isomorphism defined in the same way in $\mathbb{K}'$. Units of adjunctions are preserved by $2$-functors. By the induction hypothesis, $(N_{\Delta_p}^F)^{-1}$ is sent to $(N_{\Delta_p}^{G\circ F})^{-1}$. Thus $G$ sends the mate of $N_p^F$ to the mate of $N_p^{G\circ F}$.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:upward_close_lemma}
    Let $F:\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})\to\mathbb{K}$ be a $({P},{I})$-adjointed functor, and let $G:\mathbb{K}\to\mathbb{K}'$ be a $2$-functor of $(\infty,2)$-categories. Then $G\circ F$ is also $({P},{I})$-adjointed.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
This follows from the naturality of the norm maps and the fact that $2$-functors send invertible $2$-morphisms to invertible $2$-morphisms.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:adjtd_preserves_nonempty_colimits}
    The inclusion
    \[
    \operatorname{2Cat}_{\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})/}^{({P},{I}){\operatorname{-adjointed}}}
    \subset
    \operatorname{2Cat}_{\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})/}
    \]
    preserves nonempty colimits.
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
Let $D:{K}\to\operatorname{2Cat}_{\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})/}^{({P},{I}){\operatorname{-adjointed}}}$ be a diagram indexed by a nonempty $\infty$-category ${K}$, and let $\mathbb{M}$ be its colimit in $\operatorname{2Cat}_{\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})/}$. For some $k\in{K}$, which exists by assumption, we have a factorization
    \[
    \mathrm{Span}({C},{E})\to D(k)\to\mathbb{M}.
    \]
    Since $D(k)$ is $({P},{I})$-adjointed, \crtCref{cor:upward_close_lemma} shows that $\mathbb{M}$ is also $({P},{I})$-adjointed.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- remark-3: body_md -->
Notice that the condition that the colimit be nonempty is vital. The inclusion does not preserve the empty colimit unless ${P},{I}$ consist only of isomorphisms. Indeed, preservation would imply, by \crtCref{cor:upward_close_lemma}, that every $(\infty,2)$-category equipped with a functor from $\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})$ is adjointed, which is false.
<!-- end remark-3 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:adj_closed_under_limits}
    Let $D:{K}\to\operatorname{2Cat}$ be a diagram indexed by an $\infty$-category ${K}$. Suppose that we have a cone $D':{K}^{\triangleleft}\to\operatorname{2Cat}$ such that $D'(-\infty)=\Delta^1$ and, for each $k\in{K}$, the functor $\Delta^1\to D'(k)$ picks a left adjoint in $D'(k)$. Then the functor $\Delta^1\to\lim_{{K}}D$ picks a left adjoint in $\lim_{{K}}D$.
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
Let $\mathbb{D}$ be an $(\infty,2)$-category.
    Let $\mathbf{Adj}$ be the initial $(\infty,2)$-category with adjoint $1$-morphisms $L\dashv R$. There is a canonical functor $\Delta^1\to\mathbf{Adj}$ picking $L$.

    Recall that a $1$-morphism corresponding to a functor $\Delta^1\to\mathbb{D}$ is a left adjoint in $\mathbb{D}$ if and only if there exists a necessarily unique lift
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        \Delta^1\ar[r]\ar[d]
        &\mathbb{D}\\
        \mathbf{Adj}.\ar[ur, dotted]
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    Thus, since $2$-functors preserve adjunctions, the cone from $\Delta^1$ to $D$ factors through a cone from $\mathbf{Adj}$.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\label{cor:naively_adjbl_functors_are_closed_under_limits}
    $\operatorname{2Cat}_{\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})/}^{({P},{I})^{(-2)}{\operatorname{-adjointed}}}$ is closed under limits.
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
This is immediate from \crtCref{lem:adj_closed_under_limits}.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:2_isos_closed_under_limits}
    Let $D:{K}\to\operatorname{2Cat}$ be a diagram indexed by an $\infty$-category ${K}$. Suppose that we have a cone $D':{K}^{\triangleleft}\to\operatorname{2Cat}$ such that $D'(-\infty)=\mathbf{O}^{\operatorname{lax}}$ and, for each $k\in{K}$, the functor $\mathbf{O}^{\operatorname{lax}}\to D'(k)$ picks a $2$-isomorphism in $D'(k)$. Then the corresponding functor $\mathbf{O}^{\operatorname{lax}}\to\lim_{{K}}D$ picks a $2$-isomorphism in $\lim_{{K}}D$.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
The proof is identical to the proof of \crtCref{lem:adj_closed_under_limits}.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:adjtd_preserves_limits}
    The inclusion
    \[
    \operatorname{2Cat}_{\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})/}^{({P},{I}){\operatorname{-adjointed}}}
    \subset
    \operatorname{2Cat}_{\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})/}
    \]
    preserves all limits.
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
We will prove by induction that each full sub-$\infty$-category
    \[
    \operatorname{2Cat}_{\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})/}^{({P},{I})^{(n)}{\operatorname{-adjointed}}}
    \subset
    \operatorname{2Cat}_{\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})/}^{({P},{I})^{(n-1)}{\operatorname{-adjointed}}}
    \]
    is closed under limits, and that $\operatorname{2Cat}_{\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})/}^{({P},{I})^{(-2)}{\operatorname{-adjointed}}}$ is closed under limits in $\operatorname{2Cat}_{\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})/}$.

    \crtCref{cor:naively_adjbl_functors_are_closed_under_limits} provides the base of the induction.

    Now consider a diagram $D:{K}\to\operatorname{2Cat}_{\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})/}^{({P},{I})^{(n)}{\operatorname{-adjointed}}}$. By induction, its limit in $\operatorname{2Cat}_{\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})/}$ belongs to $\operatorname{2Cat}_{\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})/}^{({P},{I})^{(n-1)}{\operatorname{-adjointed}}}$. For all objects of this full sub-$\infty$-category, we have naturally defined norm maps $i_\sharp\to i_!$ and $p_!\to p_*$ (see \crtCref{lem:nat_of_norms}). Thus, for each $i\in{I}^{(n)}$ or $p\in{P}^{(n)}$, we get a cone $D':{K}^{\triangleleft}\to\operatorname{2Cat}$ such that $D'(-\infty)=\mathbf{O}^{\operatorname{lax}}$ and the components $\mathbf{O}^{\operatorname{lax}}\to D'(k)$ for $k\in{K}$ classify the norm maps of $i$ or $p$.

    By \crtCref{lem:2_isos_closed_under_limits}, the limit $\lim_{{K}}D$ belongs to $\operatorname{2Cat}_{\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})/}^{({P},{I})^{(n)}{\operatorname{-adjointed}}}$.

    We have proved that a limit in $\operatorname{2Cat}_{\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})/}^{({P},{I})^{(n-1)}{\operatorname{-adjointed}}}$ of objects in $\operatorname{2Cat}_{\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})/}^{({P},{I})^{(n)}{\operatorname{-adjointed}}}$ belongs to $\operatorname{2Cat}_{\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})/}^{({P},{I})^{(n)}{\operatorname{-adjointed}}}$, and we are done.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{prop:adjointed_reflection}
    The inclusion
    \[
    \operatorname{2Cat}_{\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})/}^{({P},{I}){\operatorname{-adjointed}}}
    \hookrightarrow
    \operatorname{2Cat}_{\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})/}
    \]
    has a left adjoint $L_{\operatorname{adjointed}}$.
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
By the reflection theorem of Ragimov and Schlank \cite{shauly_reflection} and the adjoint functor theorem, it suffices to show that the inclusion preserves all limits and is accessible.

    Note that filtered $\infty$-categories are nonempty, for example because their geometric realizations are contractible. Hence we are done by \crtCref{prop:adjtd_preserves_nonempty_colimits,prop:adjtd_preserves_limits}.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- corollary-3: body_md -->
\label{cor:existence_of_universal_adjointed_functor}
    There exists a $({P},{I})$-adjointed functor $F:\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})\to\mathbb{U}$ such that precomposition with $F$ gives an equivalence of $\infty$-categories
    \[
    (-)\circ F\colon
    \operatorname{2Cat}_{\mathbb{U}/}
    \to
    \operatorname{2Cat}_{\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})/}^{({P},{I}){\operatorname{-adjointed}}}.
    \]

    Equivalently, $F$ is a universal $({P},{I})$-adjointed functor, in the sense that for any $({P},{I})$-adjointed functor $G:\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})\to\mathbb{K}$, there is a unique functor $H:\mathbb{U}\to\mathbb{K}$ factoring $G$.
<!-- end corollary-3 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
We take $\mathbb{U}:=L_{\operatorname{adjointed}}(\mathrm{Span}({C},{E}))$.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
\label{prop:enriched_universal_property}
    For any object $F:\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})\to\mathbb{G}$ of $\mathbf{2Cat}_{\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})/}^{({P},{I}){\operatorname{-adjointed}}}$, we have an equivalence of $\infty$-categories
    \[
    \mathrm{Fun}(\mathbb{U},\mathbb{G})\simeq *,
    \]
    where $\mathrm{Fun}(\mathbb{U},\mathbb{G})$ denotes the mapping $\infty$-category in $\mathbf{2Cat}_{\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})/}^{({P},{I}){\operatorname{-adjointed}}}$.
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
The $\infty$-category $\operatorname{2Cat}_{\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})/}^{({P},{I}){\operatorname{-adjointed}}}$ can be endowed with the structure of a $\mathrm{Cat}$-module in $\mathrm{Pr}^{\mathrm{L}}$. Thus it is both enriched and cotensored over $\mathrm{Cat}$.

    It is enough to show that, for every $\infty$-category ${T}$, the anima
    \[
    \operatorname{Map}({T},\mathrm{Fun}(\mathbb{U},\mathbb{G}))
    \]
    is contractible.

    Let $\mathbf{Fun}({T},\mathbb{G})$ denote the $(\infty,2)$-category of functors from ${T}$ to $\mathbb{G}$.

    Consider the functor $\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})\to\mathbf{Fun}({T},\mathbb{G})$ given by the composition of $F$ with the diagonal functor $\mathbb{G}\to\mathbf{Fun}({T},\mathbb{G})$.

    We have
    \[
    \operatorname{Map}({T},\mathrm{Fun}(\mathbb{U},\mathbb{G}))
    \simeq
    \operatorname{Map}(\mathbb{U},\mathbf{Fun}({T},\mathbb{G})).
    \]
    The right-hand side is contractible by the universality of $\mathbb{U}$ in the $\infty$-category $\operatorname{2Cat}_{\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})/}^{({P},{I}){\operatorname{-adjointed}}}$.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- definition-4: body_md -->
\label{def:free_adjointed_functor_on_an_object}
    Let $a\in{C}$ be an object. A pair consisting of a $({P},{I})$-adjointed functor $F\colon\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})\to\mathrm{Cat}$ and an object $1_a\in F(a)$ is called the free $({P},{I})$-adjointed functor on $a$ if, for every $({P},{I})$-adjointed functor $G\colon\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})\to\mathrm{Cat}$, the functor given by evaluation at $1_a$ is an equivalence of $\infty$-categories:
    \[
    \mathrm{Fun}_{\mathbf{Fun}(\mathrm{Span}({C},{E}),{\mathbf{Cat}})}(F,G)\to G(a).
    \]

    When $a$ is clear, we might say that $F$ is a free $({P},{I})$-adjointed functor on $1_a$ instead.
<!-- end definition-4 -->
<!-- notation-2: body_md -->
For an $(\infty,2)$-category $\mathbb{V}$, we denote by $\text{\usefont{U}{dmjhira}{m}{n}\symbol{"48}}_{\mathbb{V}}$ the $\mathrm{Cat}$-enriched Yoneda functor, i.e. the $2$-functor
    \[
    \text{\usefont{U}{dmjhira}{m}{n}\symbol{"48}}_{\mathbb{V}}\colon\mathbb{V}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Fun}(\mathbb{V},{\mathbf{Cat}}).
    \]
    In particular, for $a\in\mathbb{V}$, $\text{\usefont{U}{dmjhira}{m}{n}\symbol{"48}}_{\mathbb{V}}(a)$ is a $2$-functor $\mathbb{V}\to{\mathbf{Cat}}$ sending $b$ to $\mathrm{Fun}_{\mathbb{V}}(a,b)$.
<!-- end notation-2 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{recognition_principle}
    Let $h\colon\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})\to\mathbb{V}$ be a $({P},{I})$-adjointed functor to an $(\infty,2)$-category $\mathbb{V}$. Then it is the free $({P},{I})$-adjointed functor if and only if the following two conditions hold.
    \begin{itemize}
        \item $h$ is essentially surjective.
        \item For every object $a\in{C}$, $\text{\usefont{U}{dmjhira}{m}{n}\symbol{"48}}_{\mathbb{V}}(h(a))\circ h\colon\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})\to\mathrm{Cat}$ is a free $({P},{I})$-adjointed functor on $\mathrm{id}_{h(a)}$.
    \end{itemize}
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:universal_adjointed_representables_are_free}
    If $F\colon\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})\to\mathbb{U}$ is the free $({P},{I})$-adjointed functor, then, for every $a\in\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})$, $\text{\usefont{U}{dmjhira}{m}{n}\symbol{"48}}_{\mathbb{U}}(F(a))\circ F$ is a free $({P},{I})$-adjointed functor on $\mathrm{id}_{F(a)}$.
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
By the universal property of $F$, any $({P},{I})$-adjointed functor $G\colon\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})\to\mathrm{Cat}$ can be lifted uniquely to a $2$-functor $\tilde{G}\colon\mathbb{U}\to{\mathbf{Cat}}$, and we have:
    \begin{align*}
        \mathrm{Fun}_{\mathbf{Fun}(\mathrm{Span}({C},{E}),{\mathbf{Cat}})}(\text{\usefont{U}{dmjhira}{m}{n}\symbol{"48}}_{\mathbb{U}}(F(a))\circ F,G)
        &\simeq\mathrm{Fun}_{\mathbf{Fun}(\mathbb{U},{\mathbf{Cat}})}(\text{\usefont{U}{dmjhira}{m}{n}\symbol{"48}}_{\mathbb{U}}(F(a)),\tilde{G})\\
        &\simeq\tilde{G}(F(a))\\
        &\simeq G(a).
    \end{align*}

    It is standard to check that this equivalence comes from evaluation at $\mathrm{id}_{F(a)}$, and so we are done.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{lem:universal_adjointed_essentially_surjective}
    If $F\colon\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})\to\mathbb{U}$ is the free $({P},{I})$-adjointed functor, then it is essentially surjective.
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
Let $\mathbb{U}'\subseteq\mathbb{U}$ be the full sub-$(\infty,2)$-category given by the essential image of $F$. It is clear that $F$, regarded as a functor to $\mathbb{U}'$, is still $({P},{I})$-adjointed. Therefore there is a $2$-functor $\phi\colon\mathbb{U}\to\mathbb{U}'$ over $\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})$. Composing with the inclusion, we get a self-map of $\mathbb{U}$. Since $\mathbb{U}$ is universal, this self-map must be equivalent to the identity. This implies that the inclusion is essentially surjective, so $\mathbb{U}'\simeq\mathbb{U}$ and $F$ is essentially surjective.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
In one direction, we already showed in \crtCref{lem:universal_adjointed_representables_are_free,lem:universal_adjointed_essentially_surjective} that the free $({P},{I})$-adjointed functor satisfies the conditions.

    To see the other direction, let $h\colon\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})\to\mathbb{V}$ be a $({P},{I})$-adjointed functor satisfying the conditions. That is, $h$ is essentially surjective and, for every $a\in{C}$, $\text{\usefont{U}{dmjhira}{m}{n}\symbol{"48}}_{\mathbb{V}}(h(a))\circ h$ is the free $({P},{I})$-adjointed functor on $\mathrm{id}_{h(a)}$. Let $F\colon\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})\to\mathbb{U}$ be the free $({P},{I})$-adjointed functor.

    By the universal property of $\mathbb{U}$, we have a $2$-functor $\bar{F}\colon\mathbb{U}\to\mathbb{V}$ satisfying $\bar{F}\circ F\simeq h$. Since $h$ is essentially surjective, so is $\bar{F}$. It remains to show that it is fully faithful.

    We wish to show that, for every pair of objects $X,Y\in\mathbb{U}$, we have an equivalence of $\infty$-categories:
    \[
    \mathrm{Fun}_{\mathbb{U}}(X,Y)\simeq\mathrm{Fun}_{\mathbb{V}}(\bar{F}(X),\bar{F}(Y)).
    \]
    Since $F$ is essentially surjective, this is the same as showing that, for every $x\in{C}$,
    \[
    \mathrm{Fun}_{\mathbb{U}}(F(x),F(-))\simeq\mathrm{Fun}_{\mathbb{V}}(h(x),h(-))
    \]
    as functors $\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})\to\mathrm{Cat}$. However, these are simply $\text{\usefont{U}{dmjhira}{m}{n}\symbol{"48}}_{\mathbb{U}}(F(x))\circ F$ and $\text{\usefont{U}{dmjhira}{m}{n}\symbol{"48}}_{\mathbb{V}}(h(x))\circ h$, respectively. By \crtCref{lem:universal_adjointed_representables_are_free} and the assumption, they are free on the respective identities. Since the map between them takes $\mathrm{id}_{F(x)}$ to $\mathrm{id}_{h(x)}$, it must be an equivalence, and we are done.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- definition-5: body_md -->
For $a,b\in{C}$, the $\infty$-category ${E}[a](b)$ is the mapping $\infty$-category from $a$ to $b$ in the $(\infty,2)$-category ${\mathbf{Span}^{1.5}}({C},{E})^{{E}}$. Objects of ${E}[a](b)$ are of the form $a\leftarrow x\to b$, where the right arrow is in ${E}$. A morphism from $a\leftarrow x\to b$ to $a\leftarrow y\to b$ is a morphism $x\to y$ in ${E}$ together with the commutation data over $a$ and $b$.

    Let ${I}\subset{E}$ be a wide sub-$\infty$-category. We let ${E}^{{I}}[a](b)$ denote the wide sub-$\infty$-category of ${E}[a](b)$ where we allow morphisms between $x$ and $y$ which are in ${I}$.
<!-- end definition-5 -->
<!-- remark-4: body_md -->
Since ${E}[a](b)$ was defined as a mapping $\infty$-category, it can be regarded as a functor in both $a$ and $b$ (contravariantly in $a$ and covariantly in $b$).
<!-- end remark-4 -->
<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
Let ${P},{I}$ be as before. Then $({E}[a](b),{E}^{{P}}[a](b),{E}^{{I}}[a](b))$ is an adequate triplet which is functorial in $a$ and $b$.
<!-- end proposition-5 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
It is clear that pullbacks in ${E}[a](b)$ are computed in ${C}$. Thus $({E}[a](b),{E}^{{P}}[a](b),{E}^{{I}}[a](b))$ is an adequate triplet. Functoriality follows immediately from the functoriality of ${E}[a](b)$.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{thm:red_of_main}
    Let ${C}$ be an $\infty$-category, and let ${E},{I},{P}\subset{C}$ be wide sub-$\infty$-categories that are stable under base change in ${C}$. Assume that ${I},{P}\subset{E}$ are left cancellable and that every morphism in ${I}$ and ${P}$ is truncated. Let $a\in{C}$. Let $F\colon\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})\to\mathrm{Cat}$ denote the functor given by
    \[
    F(b):=\mathrm{Span}({E}[a](b),{P},{I}),
    \]
    obtained by composing the functor $b\mapsto({E}[a](b),{P},{I})$ with $\mathrm{Span}$. Then $F$ is the free $({P},{I})$-adjointed functor on $\mathrm{id}_a\in F(a)$.
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- proposition-6: body_md -->
\label{prop:reduction_of_main_theorem}
    \crtCref{thm:red_of_main} implies \crtCref{main_theorem:free_adjointed_2_cat}.
<!-- end proposition-6 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
Let
    \[
    h\colon\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})\to\mathbf{Span}^2({C},{E})^{{P}}_{{I}}
    \]
    denote the canonical functor. Since $h$ is clearly essentially surjective, \crtCref{recognition_principle} shows that \crtCref{main_theorem:free_adjointed_2_cat} is equivalent to the restricted Yoneda functor $\text{\usefont{U}{dmjhira}{m}{n}\symbol{"48}}_{\mathbf{Span}^2({C},{E})^{{P}}_{{I}}}(a)\circ h$ being the free $({P},{I})$-adjointed functor on $\mathrm{id}_a$ for every $a\in{C}$. This functor sends
    \[
    b\mapsto\mathrm{Fun}_{\mathbf{Span}^2({C},{E})^{{P}}_{{I}}}(a,b).
    \]
    By the description of the mapping $\infty$-categories in \cite[proof of Theorem 4.20]{CLLuniv}, we have a natural equivalence
    \[
    \mathrm{Fun}_{\mathbf{Span}^2({C},{E})^{{P}}_{{I}}}(a,b)
    \simeq\mathrm{Span}({E}[a](b),{P},{I}).
    \]
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- definition-6: body_md -->
An adequate triplet $({C},{C}_L,{C}_R)$ is an $\infty$-category ${C}$ with two wide subcategories ${C}_L,{C}_R\subset{C}$, called the left-pointing and right-pointing maps, respectively, such that for every $Y\to W$ in ${C}_R$ and $Z\to W$ in ${C}_L$, the pullback
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:pullback_square_of_left_along_right}
    \begin{tikzcd}
        Z\times_W Y \ar[r]\ar[d]\arrow[rd, "\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none] & Z\ar[d]\\
        Y\ar[r] & W
    \end{tikzcd}
    \end{equation}
    exists, and the upper and left morphisms belong to ${C}_R$ and ${C}_L$, respectively.
<!-- end definition-6 -->
<!-- definition-7: body_md -->
A functor of adequate triplets $({C},{C}_L,{C}_R)\to({D},{D}_L,{D}_R)$ is a functor $F:{C}\to{D}$ satisfying the following conditions.
    \begin{mylist}
        \item If $f$ belongs to ${C}_L$, then $F(f)$ belongs to ${D}_L$. If $g$ belongs to ${C}_R$, then $F(g)$ belongs to ${D}_R$.
        \item $F$ preserves pullbacks of right-pointing maps along left-pointing maps, as in \crtCref{eq:pullback_square_of_left_along_right}.
    \end{mylist}
    We denote by $\operatorname{AdTrip}$ the $\infty$-category of adequate triplets and functors of adequate triplets.
<!-- end definition-7 -->
<!-- definition-8: body_md -->
Let $F,G:({C},{C}_L,{C}_R)\to({D},{D}_L,{D}_R)$ be functors of adequate triplets.

    A right-pointing natural transformation of functors of adequate triplets is a natural transformation $\theta:F\Rightarrow G$ such that each component $\theta_X:F(X)\to G(X)$ belongs to ${D}_R$ and, for every morphism $f:X\to Y$ in ${C}_L$, the naturality square
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        F(X)\arrow[rd, "\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none]\ar[r, "F(f)"]\ar[d,"\theta_X"'] & F(Y)\ar[d,"\theta_Y"]\\
        G(X)\ar[r, "G(f)"'] & G(Y)
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    is cartesian in ${D}$.

    A left-pointing natural transformation of functors of adequate triplets is a natural transformation $\theta:F\Rightarrow G$ such that each component $\theta_X:F(X)\to G(X)$ belongs to ${D}_L$ and, for every morphism $f:X\to Y$ in ${C}_R$, the naturality square
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        F(X)\arrow[rd, "\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none]\ar[r, "F(f)"]\ar[d,"\theta_X"'] & F(Y)\ar[d,"\theta_Y"]\\
        G(X)\ar[r, "G(f)"'] & G(Y)
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    is cartesian in ${D}$.

    We denote by $\mathbf{AdTrip}^R$ the $(\infty,2)$-category of adequate triplets, functors of adequate triplets, and right-pointing natural transformations. Likewise, we denote by $\mathbf{AdTrip}^L$ the $(\infty,2)$-category defined using left-pointing natural transformations.
<!-- end definition-8 -->
<!-- definition-9: body_md -->
A span pair is an adequate triplet with ${C}_L={C}$. Equivalently, it is an $\infty$-category ${C}$ with a wide subcategory ${C}_R\subset{C}$ that is stable under base change in ${C}$.

    We denote by $\operatorname{SpanPairs}\subset\operatorname{AdTrip}$ the full subcategory spanned by span pairs.
<!-- end definition-9 -->
<!-- construction-1: body_md -->
\begin{mylist}
        \item For an adequate triplet $({C},{C}_L,{C}_R)$, there is an $\infty$-category $\mathrm{Span}({C},{C}_L,{C}_R)$ with the same space of objects as ${C}$, morphisms given by correspondences, and composition given by pullbacks. We refer to \cite[\S 2]{HHLNSpansDef} for a precise treatment.
        \item The span construction assembles into a limit-preserving functor
        \[
        \mathrm{Span}:\operatorname{AdTrip}\to\mathrm{Cat}.
        \]
        This functor admits two enhancements to a $2$-functor of $(\infty,2)$-categories:
        \[
        \mathrm{Span}:\mathbf{AdTrip}^R\to{\mathbf{Cat}},
        \qquad
        \mathrm{Span}:(\mathbf{AdTrip}^L)^{\mathrm{co}}\to{\mathbf{Cat}}
        \]
        (see \cite[Proposition C.20]{BHNormsInMotivic}).
        \item\label{def:catsofspans:adjuncions}
        Adjunctions in $\mathbf{AdTrip}^R$ are adjunctions $F:{C}\leftrightarrows{D}:G$ in which $F$ and $G$ are functors of adequate triplets and the unit and counit are right-pointing natural transformations. Since $\mathrm{Span}:\mathbf{AdTrip}^R\to{\mathbf{Cat}}$ is a $2$-functor, it sends such adjunctions to adjunctions of $\infty$-categories.

        Adjunctions in $\mathbf{AdTrip}^L$ are defined similarly using left-pointing natural transformations. The $2$-functor $\mathrm{Span}:(\mathbf{AdTrip}^L)^{\mathrm{co}}\to{\mathbf{Cat}}$ also sends these to adjunctions of $\infty$-categories, with the direction of the adjunction reversed because of the $\mathrm{co}$.
    \end{mylist}
<!-- end construction-1 -->
<!-- construction-2: body_md -->
\label{const:unfurling}
    Following \cite[Definition 3.12(2) and Theorem 3.13(2)]{CLRUniversalityOfUnferling}, let $({C},{C}_R)$ be a span pair.
    \begin{mylist}
        \item Let $F:{C}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Cat}$ be a functor. We say that $F$ is \emph{left $R$-adjointable} if it sends morphisms in ${C}_R^{\mathrm{op}}$ to functors admitting left adjoints and sends every base change square
        \[
        \begin{tikzcd}
            Z\times_W Y\ar[r,"{C}_R"]\ar[d]\arrow[rd, "\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none] & Z\ar[d]\\
            Y\ar[r,"{C}_R"'] & W
        \end{tikzcd}
        \]
        of a morphism in ${C}_R$ to a horizontally left adjointable square
        \[
        \begin{tikzcd}
            F(W)\ar[r]\ar[d] & F(Y)\ar[d]\\
            F(Z)\ar[r] & F(Z\times_W Y).
        \end{tikzcd}
        \]
        That is, the horizontal functors admit left adjoints and the square satisfies the Beck--Chevalley condition.
        \item A \emph{morphism of left $R$-adjointable functors} is a natural transformation $\eta:F\Rightarrow G$ such that, for every morphism $f:X\to Y$ in ${C}_R$, the naturality square
        \[
        \begin{tikzcd}
            F(Y)\ar[r,"F(f)"]\ar[d,"\eta_Y"'] & F(X)\ar[d,"\eta_X"]\\
            G(Y)\ar[r,"G(f)"'] & G(X)
        \end{tikzcd}
        \]
        satisfies the Beck--Chevalley condition. We denote by
        \[
        \mathrm{Fun}^{R\operatorname{-adjointable}}({C}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathrm{Cat})
        \subset\mathrm{Fun}({C}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathrm{Cat})
        \]
        the $\infty$-subcategory of left $R$-adjointable functors and their morphisms.
        \item Let $F:{C}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Cat}$ be left $R$-adjointable, and let $p:{E}\to{C}$ be its cartesian unstraightening. Let ${E}^{p{\operatorname{-cart}}}$ be the wide subcategory of ${E}$ spanned by $p$-cartesian morphisms, and let ${E}_R\subset{E}$ be the wide subcategory of morphisms lying over ${C}_R$. Then $({E},{E}^{p{\operatorname{-cart}}},{E}_R)$ is an adequate triplet, and $p$ induces a functor of adequate triplets
        \[
        ({E},{E}^{p{\operatorname{-cart}}},{E}_R)
        \to({C},{C},{C}_R).
        \]
        Applying the span construction gives a functor
        \[
        \mathrm{Span}(p):\mathrm{Span}({E},{E}^{p{\operatorname{-cart}}},{E}_R)
        \to\mathrm{Span}({C},{C},{C}_R).
        \]
        \item The functor $\mathrm{Span}(p)$ is a cocartesian fibration classifying a functor
        \[
        \widetilde{F}:\mathrm{Span}({C},{C}_R)\to\mathrm{Cat},
        \]
        called the \emph{unfurling} of $F$. It extends $F$, and for every $f:Y\to W$ in ${C}_R$, the functor $\widetilde{F}(Y=Y\xrightarrow{f}W)$ is left adjoint to $F(f)=\widetilde{F}(W\xleftarrow{f}Y=Y)$.
    \end{mylist}
<!-- end construction-2 -->
<!-- definition-10: body_md -->
\label{def:internal_ad_triplet}
    Following \cite[Definition 4.3]{CLLambi}, an adequate triplet of $\mathcal{B}$-categories is a triplet $(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_L,\mathsf{C}_R)$ consisting of a $\mathcal{B}$-category $\mathsf{C}$ and two wide $\mathcal{B}$-subcategories $\mathsf{C}_L,\mathsf{C}_R\subset\mathsf{C}$ such that, for every $A\in\mathcal{B}$, the triplet $(\mathsf{C}(A),\mathsf{C}_L(A),\mathsf{C}_R(A))$ is adequate and, for every morphism $p:B\to A$ in $\mathcal{B}$, the restriction functor $p^*:\mathsf{C}(A)\to\mathsf{C}(B)$ is a functor of adequate triplets.
<!-- end definition-10 -->
<!-- definition-11: body_md -->
The span $\mathcal{B}$-category ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_L,\mathsf{C}_R)$ is the composite
    \[
    \mathcal{B}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{AdTrip}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{Span}}\mathrm{Cat}.
    \]
    This defines a $\mathcal{B}$-functor
    \[
    {\mathsf{Span}}:\mathsf{AdTrip}\to\mathsf{Cat}.
    \]
<!-- end definition-11 -->
<!-- proposition-7: body_md -->
Let $F:\mathsf{C}\to\mathsf{D}$ be a $\mathcal{B}$-functor. The condition that $F|_{\mathcal{B}_{/A}}$ is a left adjoint is local in $A$: for every effective epimorphism $A'\to A$, the functor $F|_{\mathcal{B}_{/A}}$ is a left adjoint if and only if $F|_{\mathcal{B}_{/A'}}$ is a left adjoint.
<!-- end proposition-7 -->
<!-- construction-3: body_md -->
\label{const:internal_unfurling}
    Let $(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_R)$ be a $\mathcal{B}$-span pair.
    \begin{mylist}
        \item Let $F:\mathsf{C}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{Cat}$ be a $\mathcal{B}$-functor. We say that $F$ is \emph{left $R$-adjointable} if it sends morphisms in $\mathsf{C}_R^{\mathrm{op}}$ to internal right adjoints and, for every context $A$, sends each base change square in $\mathsf{C}(A)$
        \[
        \begin{tikzcd}
            Z\times_W Y\ar[r,"\mathsf{C}_R"]\ar[d]\arrow[rd, "\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none] & Z\ar[d]\\
            Y\ar[r,"\mathsf{C}_R"'] & W
        \end{tikzcd}
        \]
        of a morphism in $\mathsf{C}_R(A)$ to a horizontally left adjointable square
        \[
        \begin{tikzcd}
            F(W)\ar[r]\ar[d] & F(Y)\ar[d]\\
            F(Z)\ar[r] & F(Z\times_W Y)
        \end{tikzcd}
        \]
        in the $(\infty,2)$-category ${\mathbf{Cat}}(\mathcal{B}_{/A})$. That is, the horizontal functors admit internal left adjoints and the square satisfies the Beck--Chevalley condition in every context.
        \item A \emph{morphism of internally left $R$-adjointable functors} is a natural transformation $\eta:F\Rightarrow G$ such that, for every context $A$ and every morphism $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathsf{C}_R(A)$, the naturality square
        \[
        \begin{tikzcd}
            F(Y)\ar[r,"F(f)"]\ar[d,"\eta_Y"'] & F(X)\ar[d,"\eta_X"]\\
            G(Y)\ar[r,"G(f)"'] & G(X)
        \end{tikzcd}
        \]
        satisfies the Beck--Chevalley condition in ${\mathbf{Cat}}(\mathcal{B}_{/A})$. We denote by
        \[
        \underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{R\operatorname{-adjointable}}(\mathsf{C}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathsf{Cat})
        \subset\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}(\mathsf{C}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathsf{Cat})
        \]
        the $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory of left $R$-adjointable functors and their morphisms. This is a $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory by locality of adjunctions.
        \item\label{const:unst_of_unf}
        Let $F:\mathsf{C}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{Cat}$ be left $R$-adjointable, and let $p:\mathsf{P}\to\mathsf{C}$ be its cartesian unstraightening. Let $\mathsf{P}^{p{\operatorname{-cart}}}$ be the wide $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory of $\mathsf{P}$ spanned by $p$-cartesian morphisms, and let $\mathsf{P}_R$ be the wide $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory of morphisms lying over $\mathsf{C}_R$. Then $(\mathsf{P},\mathsf{P}^{p{\operatorname{-cart}}},\mathsf{P}_R)$ is an internal adequate triplet, and $p$ induces a functor of internal adequate triplets
        \[
        (\mathsf{P},\mathsf{P}^{p{\operatorname{-cart}}},\mathsf{P}_R)
        \to(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_R).
        \]
        Applying the internal span construction gives a $\mathcal{B}$-functor
        \[
        {\mathsf{Span}}(p):{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{P},\mathsf{P}^{p{\operatorname{-cart}}},\mathsf{P}_R)
        \to{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_R).
        \]
    \end{mylist}
<!-- end construction-3 -->
<!-- proposition-8: body_md -->
Let $F:\mathsf{C}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{Cat}$ be a left $R$-adjointable $\mathcal{B}$-functor. The $\mathcal{B}$-functor
    \[
    {\mathsf{Span}}(p):{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{P},\mathsf{P}^{p{\operatorname{-cart}}},\mathsf{P}_R)
    \to{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_R)
    \]
    of \crtCref{const:unst_of_unf} is a cocartesian fibration classifying a $\mathcal{B}$-functor
    \[
    \widetilde{F}:{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_R)\to\mathsf{Cat},
    \]
    called the \emph{unfurling} of $F$. It extends $F$, and for every context $A$ and every $f:Y\to W$ in $\mathsf{C}_R(A)$, the functor $\widetilde{F}(Y=Y\xrightarrow{f}W)$ is internally left adjoint to $F(f)=\widetilde{F}(W\xleftarrow{f}Y=Y)$.
<!-- end proposition-8 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
The only nontrivial assertion is that ${\mathsf{Span}}(p)$ is a cocartesian fibration. By \cite[Proposition 3.1.7]{MInternalStraightenning}, it suffices to check that ${\mathsf{Span}}(p)(A)$ is a cocartesian fibration of $\infty$-categories for every $A\in\mathcal{B}$ and that, for every morphism $q:B\to A$ in $\mathcal{B}$, the square
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{P},\mathsf{P}^{p{\operatorname{-cart}}},\mathsf{P}_R)(A)\ar[d,"q^*"]\ar[rr,"{\mathsf{Span}}(p)(A)"]
        &&{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_R)(A)\ar[d,"q^*"]\\
        {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{P},\mathsf{P}^{p{\operatorname{-cart}}},\mathsf{P}_R)(B)\ar[rr,"{\mathsf{Span}}(p)(B)"]
        &&{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_R)(B)
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    is a morphism of cocartesian fibrations.

    In each context $A$, the functor ${\mathsf{Span}}(p)(A)$ is obtained by applying \crtCref{const:unfurling} to the composite
    \[
    \mathsf{C}^{\mathrm{op}}(A)\xrightarrow{F(A)}\mathsf{Cat}(A)\xrightarrow{\Gamma_A}\mathrm{Cat}.
    \]
    Thus it is a cocartesian fibration by the construction for $\infty$-categories.

    Functoriality of unfurling shows that the square induced by $q^*$ is a morphism of cocartesian fibrations. Here we use the Beck--Chevalley conditions for adjunctions of $\mathcal{B}$-categories.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
\label{thm:uniqueness_of_unfurling}
    Restriction along the natural inclusion ${C}^{\mathrm{op}}\hookrightarrow\mathrm{Span}({C},{C}_R)$ defines a natural transformation between functors $(\operatorname{SpanPairs}')^{\mathrm{op}}\to\widehat{\mathrm{Cat}}$:
    \[
    \theta:\mathrm{Fun}^{R{\operatorname{-adjointed}}}(\mathrm{Span}({C},{C}_R),\mathrm{Cat})
    \to\mathrm{Fun}^{R\operatorname{-adjointable}}({C}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathrm{Cat}).
    \]
    The unfurling construction assembles into a section of $\theta$. For every $({C},{C}_R)\in\operatorname{SpanPairs}'$, this section is an equivalence of $\infty$-categories.
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
The assertion that $\theta$ is an equivalence under the truncation and left cancellation assumptions is a special case of \cite[Theorem 3.3]{uniqueness_of_6ff}. Since unfurling gives a section of $\theta$, it also gives its inverse.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- definition-12: body_md -->
Let $\mathsf{D}$ be a $\mathcal{B}$-category, and let $f:x\to y$ be a morphism of $\mathsf{D}$ in context $A$. We say that $f$ is \emph{locally truncated} if there exists a cover $(p_i:U_i\to A)_i$ such that each $p_i^*(f)$ is truncated in $\mathsf{D}(U_i)$.

    We say that $\mathsf{D}$ is \emph{truncated} if every morphism of $\mathsf{D}$ is locally truncated.
<!-- end definition-12 -->
<!-- definition-13: body_md -->
Let $(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_R)$ be a $\mathcal{B}$-span pair, with $\mathsf{C}_R$ left cancellable and truncated. For each $A\in\mathcal{B}$, we write
    \[
    \mathsf{C}_R(A)^t\subset\mathsf{C}_R(A)
    \]
    for the wide subcategory spanned by truncated morphisms.
<!-- end definition-13 -->
<!-- proposition-9: body_md -->
Let $(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_R)$ be a $\mathcal{B}$-span pair, with $\mathsf{C}_R$ left cancellable and truncated. For every context $A\in\mathcal{B}$, the pair $(\mathsf{C}(A),\mathsf{C}_R(A)^t)$ is a span pair. Moreover, the inclusion
    \[
    (\mathsf{C}(A),\mathsf{C}_R(A)^t)
    \to(\mathsf{C}(A),\mathsf{C}_R(A))
    \]
    is a morphism of span pairs.
<!-- end proposition-9 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
This follows because truncated morphisms are stable under base change.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- definition-14: body_md -->
Let $(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_R)$ be a $\mathcal{B}$-span pair, with $\mathsf{C}_R$ left cancellable and truncated. A $\mathcal{B}$-functor
    \[
    F:{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_R)\to\mathsf{Cat}
    \]
    is \emph{$R$-adjointed} if, for every context $A\in\mathcal{B}$, the composite
    \[
    \mathrm{Span}(\mathsf{C}(A),\mathsf{C}_R(A)^t)
    \hookrightarrow{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_R)(A)
    \xrightarrow{F(A)}\mathsf{Cat}(A)
    \simeq\mathrm{Cat}(\mathcal{B}_{/A}),
    \]
    viewed as a functor into ${\mathbf{Cat}}(\mathcal{B}_{/A})$, is $\mathsf{C}_R(A)^t$-left adjointed in the sense of \crtCref{def:adjointed_functors}.
<!-- end definition-14 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\label{lem:truncated_sheafify_to_locally_trancated}
    The inclusion of $\mathcal{P}$-categories
    \[
    {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_R^t)
    \hookrightarrow i_*{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_R)
    \]
    is adjoint to an equivalence of $\mathcal{B}$-categories
    \[
    i^*{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_R^t)
    \simeq{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_R).
    \]
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
Recall that an internal category $\mathsf{C}$ is a simplicial object in the corresponding $\infty$-topos:
    \[
    \mathsf{C}_0
    \;\substack{
    \longleftarrow\\[-0.2em]
    \longrightarrow\\[-0.2em]
    \longleftarrow
    }\;
    \mathsf{C}_1
    \;\substack{
    \longleftarrow\\[-0.2em]
    \longrightarrow\\[-0.2em]
    \longleftarrow\\[-0.2em]
    \longrightarrow\\[-0.2em]
    \longleftarrow
    }\;
    \mathsf{C}_2
    \;\cdots.
    \]
    Both $i^*$ and $i_*$ are computed levelwise on this simplicial object.

    The morphism
    \[
    {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_R^t)_0
    \to i_*{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_R)_0
    \]
    is an equivalence because the inclusion in the statement is wide. The morphism
    \[
    {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_R^t)_1
    \to i_*{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_R)_1
    \]
    is a monomorphism in $\mathcal{P}$. Since $i^*$ is left exact, it preserves monomorphisms. By local truncation, the induced morphism
    \[
    i^*{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_R^t)_1
    \to{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_R)_1
    \]
    is also an effective epimorphism, hence an equivalence. The Segal conditions then give an equivalence in every degree.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
\label{thm:internal_uniqueness_of_unfurling}
    Let $(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_R)$ be a $\mathcal{B}$-span pair, with $\mathsf{C}_R$ left cancellable and truncated. The internal unfurling construction defines an equivalence of $\mathcal{B}$-categories
    \[
    \underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{R\operatorname{-adjointable}}(\mathsf{C}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathsf{Cat})
    \simeq\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{R{\operatorname{-adjointed}}}({\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_R),\mathsf{Cat}).
    \]
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
Let $x:{X}\to\operatorname{SpanPairs}'$ be the cartesian unstraightening of the functor $(\operatorname{SpanPairs}')^{\mathrm{op}}\to\widehat{\mathrm{Cat}}$ given by
    \[
    ({C},{C}_R)
    \mapsto\mathrm{Fun}^{R\operatorname{-adjointable}}({C}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathrm{Cat}).
    \]
    Similarly, let $y:{Y}\to\operatorname{SpanPairs}'$ be the cartesian unstraightening of the functor $(\operatorname{SpanPairs}')^{\mathrm{op}}\to\widehat{\mathrm{Cat}}$ given by
    \[
    ({C},{C}_R)
    \mapsto\mathrm{Fun}^{R{\operatorname{-adjointed}}}(\mathrm{Span}({C},{C}_R),\mathrm{Cat}).
    \]

    Left $R$-adjointable $\mathcal{B}$-functors $\mathsf{C}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{Cat}$ correspond to $\mathcal{B}$-sheaves in ${X}$, while $R$-adjointed $\mathcal{B}$-functors ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_R)\to\mathsf{Cat}$ correspond to $\mathcal{B}$-sheaves in ${Y}$. By \crtCref{thm:uniqueness_of_unfurling}, restriction defines an equivalence ${Y}\simeq{X}$ over $\operatorname{SpanPairs}'$.

    By \crtCref{lem:truncated_sheafify_to_locally_trancated}, it suffices to consider the case in which $\mathcal{B}=\mathcal{P}=\operatorname{PSh}(S)$ is a presheaf $\infty$-topos and the corresponding functor $S^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{SpanPairs}$ takes values in $\operatorname{SpanPairs}'$. In this case, the result follows from the equivalence ${Y}\simeq{X}$.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- proposition-10: body_md -->
\label{prop:cov_unfurling}
    Let $(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_L)$ be a $\mathcal{B}$-span pair, and let $F:\mathsf{C}\to\mathsf{Cat}$ be a right $L$-adjointable $\mathcal{B}$-functor. Let $p:\mathsf{P}\to\mathsf{C}$ be its cocartesian unstraightening, and let $\mathsf{P}^{L{\operatorname{-cart}}}$ be the wide $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory of $\mathsf{P}$ spanned by cartesian lifts of morphisms in $\mathsf{C}_L$. Then
    \[
    {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{P},\mathsf{P}^{L{\operatorname{-cart}}},\mathsf{P})
    \to{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_L,\mathsf{C})
    \]
    is a cocartesian fibration classifying an extension
    \[
    \widetilde{F}:{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_L,\mathsf{C})
    \to\mathsf{Cat}
    \]
    of $F$. This extension sends left-pointing maps to the right adjoints of the corresponding right-pointing maps.

    If $\mathsf{C}_L$ is left cancellable and truncated, there is also a canonical equivalence of $\mathcal{B}$-categories
    \[
    \underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{L\operatorname{-adjointable}}(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{Cat})
    \simeq\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{L{\operatorname{-adjointed}}}({\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_L,\mathsf{C}),\mathsf{Cat}).
    \]
<!-- end proposition-10 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
It suffices to verify the corresponding statement for $\infty$-categories and then internalize the construction as above. The covariant unfurling construction is given in \cite[Theorem 3.13(1)]{CLRUniversalityOfUnferling}. The uniqueness statement follows by the same argument as in the contravariant case.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- definition-15: body_md -->
\label{def:storngly_regular_universe}
    A context-free subuniverse is a $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory $\mathsf{E}\subset\mathsf{\Omega}$ satisfying the following conditions.
    \begin{mylist}
        \item\label[condition]{cond:srs_is_kappa_small} (Smallness) $\mathsf{E}$ is a small $\mathcal{B}$-category.
        \item\label[condition]{cond:srs_has_iso} (Pointedness) $\mathsf{E}$ is closed under empty limits in $\mathsf{\Omega}$. That is, in every context $A\in\mathcal{B}$, the terminal object $[\mathrm{id}:A\to A]\in\mathsf{\Omega}(A)$ belongs to $\mathsf{E}(A)$.
        \item\label[condition]{cond:idependent_of_context} (Independence of context) Let $B\in\mathsf{E}(A)$. A morphism $p:C\to B$ in $\mathsf{\Omega}(A)$ belongs to $\mathsf{E}(A)$ if and only if the corresponding object $[p:C\to B]\in\mathsf{\Omega}(B)$ belongs to $\mathsf{E}(B)$.
    \end{mylist}

    A context-free subuniverse $\mathsf{E}$ is \emph{full} if $\mathsf{E}\subset\mathsf{\Omega}$ is a full $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory.

    It is \emph{truncated} if, for every context $A$ and every object $[B\to A]\in\mathsf{E}(A)$, there exists a cover $(U_\alpha\to A)_\alpha$ such that $[B\times_A U_\alpha\to U_\alpha]$ is a truncated object of $\mathsf{\Omega}(U_\alpha)$ for every $\alpha$.

    A context-free subuniverse $\mathsf{I}$ is \emph{inductible} if it is full and truncated.
<!-- end definition-15 -->
<!-- warning-1: body_md -->
One can instead take the full $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory of $\mathsf{\Omega}$ spanned by the morphisms in $E$, as in \cite[beginning of page 9]{MWPresentabilityAndTopoi}. Our construction also restricts the morphisms between these objects. We discuss the full subcategory below.
<!-- end warning-1 -->
<!-- proposition-11: body_md -->
\label{prop:from_local_class_to_subuniverse}
    Let $E$ be a local class of morphisms in $\mathcal{B}$ that is closed under composition and contains equivalences. If the associated $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory $\mathsf{E}$ is small, then it is a context-free subuniverse.

    Moreover, $E$ is left cancellable if and only if $\mathsf{E}$ is full, and every morphism in $E$ is locally truncated if and only if $\mathsf{E}$ is truncated.
<!-- end proposition-11 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
Independence of context (\crtCref{cond:idependent_of_context}) follows directly from the construction. Smallness (\crtCref{cond:srs_is_kappa_small}) holds by assumption, and pointedness (\crtCref{cond:srs_has_iso}) follows because $E$ contains equivalences.

    Suppose that $E$ is left cancellable, and consider a commutative triangle
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        C\ar[rd,"g"']\ar[rr,"f"]&&D\ar[ld,"h"]\\
        &A.
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    If $g,h\in E$, then $f\in E$ by left cancellation. Thus every morphism in $\mathsf{\Omega}(A)$ between objects of $\mathsf{E}(A)$ belongs to $\mathsf{E}(A)$, so $\mathsf{E}$ is full. Conversely, fullness applied to such a triangle shows that $E$ is left cancellable.

    Finally, a morphism $f:B\to A$ in $\mathcal{B}$ is truncated if and only if $[f:B\to A]$ is a truncated object of $\mathcal{B}_{/A}\simeq\mathsf{\Omega}(A)$. Locality on the target corresponds to locality in the context, proving the last assertion.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- remark-5: body_md -->
This construction gives a one-to-one correspondence between context-free subuniverses and local classes that are closed under composition, contain equivalences, and have small associated $\mathcal{B}$-subcategories of $\mathsf{\Omega}$.
<!-- end remark-5 -->
<!-- example-1: body_md -->
\label{example:Fin_in_Ani}
    Let $\mathcal{B}=\mathrm{Ani}$ be the $\infty$-category of anima, and let $\mathsf{Fin}\subset\mathsf{\Omega}$ correspond to the local class of finite covering maps. By \crtCref{prop:from_local_class_to_subuniverse}, $\mathsf{Fin}$ is inductible: finite covering maps are $0$-truncated and satisfy left cancellation.
<!-- end example-1 -->
<!-- example-2: body_md -->
For any $\infty$-topos $\mathcal{B}$, the smallest context-free subuniverse is $\left\{*\right\}\subset\mathsf{\Omega}$, corresponding to the local class of equivalences.
<!-- end example-2 -->
<!-- remark-6: body_md -->
A context-free subuniverse $\mathsf{E}$ is full if and only if $\mathsf{E}=\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$.
<!-- end remark-6 -->
<!-- remark-7: body_md -->
The full $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$ need not be a context-free subuniverse. It is context-free precisely when $\mathsf{E}=\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$.
<!-- end remark-7 -->
<!-- proposition-12: body_md -->
Let $\mathsf{E}$ be a context-free subuniverse. Then $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$ is right regular. That is, $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$ is $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$ cocomplete and the inclusion  $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}\hookrightarrow \mathsf{\Omega}$  is $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-cocontinuous.
<!-- end proposition-12 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
Let $[B\to A]\in\mathsf{E}(A)$, and let $c:B\to\pi_A^*\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$ be a $B$-shaped diagram in context $A$. Such a diagram corresponds to an object $[C\to B]\in\mathsf{E}(B)$. Its colimit in $\mathsf{\Omega}(A)$ is the composite $C\to B\to A$, which belongs to $\mathsf{E}(A)$ by independence of context.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- corollary-4: body_md -->
\label{prop:S_is_free_with_S_colmitis}
    Let $\mathsf{E}$ be a context-free subuniverse. Then $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$ is the free $\mathsf{E}$-cocompletion, equivalently the free $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-cocompletion, of the point. Thus, for every $\mathsf{E}$-cocomplete $\mathcal{B}$-category $\mathsf{C}$, restriction to the point induces an equivalence of $\mathcal{B}$-categories
    \[
    \underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{E}\text{-}\sqcup}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{C})
    \simeq\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}(*,\mathsf{C})\simeq\mathsf{C},
    \]
    where the left-hand side denotes the $\mathcal{B}$-category of $\mathsf{E}$-cocontinuous functors.
<!-- end corollary-4 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
By \cite[Theorem 7.1.13]{MWcocomplete}, the free $\mathsf{E}$-cocompletion of $*$ is the full $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory of $\mathsf{PSh}(*)\simeq\mathsf{\Omega}$ generated by $*$ under $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-colimits. This is $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$: right regularity gives closure under these colimits, and every object of $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$ is the colimit of the constant point indexed by itself.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- proposition-13: body_md -->
Let $\mathsf{E}$ be a context-free subuniverse. Then $(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})$ is a $\mathcal{B}$-span pair.
<!-- end proposition-13 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
We must show that $\mathsf{E}(A)$ is stable under base change in $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}(A)$ for every context $A$, and that restriction functors preserve these pullbacks.

    Let $f:C\to D$ belong to $\mathsf{E}(A)$, and let $g:B\to D$ belong to $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}(A)$. By independence of context, $[f:C\to D]$ is an object of $\mathsf{E}(D)$. Hence
    \[
    [C\times_D B\to B]\simeq g^*([f:C\to D])\in\mathsf{E}(B).
    \]
    Applying independence of context again shows that $C\times_D B\to B$ belongs to $\mathsf{E}(A)$.

    For a morphism $p:B\to A$ in $\mathcal{B}$, the restriction functor $p^*:\mathsf{\Omega}(A)\to\mathsf{\Omega}(B)$ preserves pullbacks. Its restriction to $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$ therefore preserves the pullbacks in question.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- proposition-14: body_md -->
\label{prop:limits_in_span_E}
    Let $\mathsf{E}$ be a context-free subuniverse. The $\mathcal{B}$-category ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})$ is $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-complete, and the inclusion
    \[
    (\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}})^{\mathrm{op}}\hookrightarrow{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})
    \]
    is $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-continuous.
<!-- end proposition-14 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
We argue as in \cite[Proposition 4.5]{CLLambi}. For $[p:B\to A]\in\mathsf{E}(A)$, we verify that the adjunction
    \[
    p_\sharp:\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}(B)\leftrightarrows\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}(A):p^*
    \]
    is an adjunction in $\mathbf{AdTrip}^L$ (see \crtCref{def:catsofspans:adjuncions}). The restriction functor $p^*$ is already a functor of adequate triplets. We must check this for $p_\sharp$ and verify that the unit and counit are left-pointing natural transformations of functors of adequate triplets.

    By independence of context, $p_\sharp$ restricts to a functor $\mathsf{E}(B)\to\mathsf{E}(A)$. Moreover, $p_\sharp:\mathsf{\Omega}(B)\to\mathsf{\Omega}(A)$ preserves pullbacks, since it is the forgetful functor between slice $\infty$-categories. Thus $p_\sharp$ is a functor of adequate triplets.

    All morphisms in $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$ are left-pointing, so the components of the unit and counit are left-pointing. To check the remaining condition, we show that their naturality squares are cartesian. In fact, this holds for all morphisms $C\to C'$ in $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}(A)$ and $D\to D'$ in $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}(B)$:
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        p_\sharp p^*C\ar[r]\ar[d] & C\ar[d]
        &D\ar[r]\ar[d] & p^*p_\sharp D\ar[d]\\
        p_\sharp p^*C'\ar[r] & C'
        &D'\ar[r] & p^*p_\sharp D'.
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    We check the counit square; the unit square is analogous. Under the inclusion into $\mathsf{\Omega}(A)\simeq\mathcal{B}_{/A}$, the identification
    \[
    p_\sharp p^*[C\to A]\simeq[B\times_A C\to A]
    \]
    identifies it with the cartesian square
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        B\times_A C\ar[r]\ar[d] & C\ar[d]\\
        B\times_A C'\ar[r] & C'.
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    For the unit square, one similarly uses $p^*p_\sharp[D\to B]\simeq[B\times_A D\to B]$.

    The span construction reverses this adjunction, making $\mathrm{Span}(p_\sharp)$ right adjoint to restriction. Its restriction to $(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}})^{\mathrm{op}}$ is the corresponding limit functor, proving both assertions.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- warning-2: body_md -->
If $\mathsf{E}$ is not full, ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})$ need not be $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-cocomplete. The preceding adjunction need not lie in $\mathbf{AdTrip}^R$: the unit maps $D\to p^*p_\sharp D$ need not belong to $\mathsf{E}$.
<!-- end warning-2 -->
<!-- proposition-15: body_md -->
\label{prop:limits_in_span_E_are_computed_in_E_op}
    Let $\mathsf{E}$ be a context-free subuniverse, and let $\mathsf{C}$ be an $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-complete $\mathcal{B}$-category. A $\mathcal{B}$-functor $F:{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\to\mathsf{C}$ is $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-continuous if and only if the composite
    \[
    (\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}})^{\mathrm{op}}\hookrightarrow{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\xrightarrow{F}\mathsf{C}
    \]
    is $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-continuous.
<!-- end proposition-15 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
The forward implication follows from \crtCref{prop:limits_in_span_E}.

    Conversely, suppose that the composite is $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-continuous. Let $B\in\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}(A)$, and let $d:B\to\pi_A^*{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})$ be a diagram in context $A$. The inclusion $(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}})^{\mathrm{op}}\hookrightarrow{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})$ is an equivalence on underlying $\mathcal{B}$-groupoids, so $d$ lifts to a diagram
    \[
    \widetilde{d}:B\to\pi_A^*(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}})^{\mathrm{op}}.
    \]
    Both the inclusion and its composite with $F$ preserve the limit of $\widetilde{d}$. Hence $F$ preserves the limit of $d$.
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- definition-16: body_md -->
\label{def:E_monoids}
    Let $\mathsf{C}$ be an $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-complete $\mathcal{B}$-category. An \emph{$\mathsf{E}$-monoid} in $\mathsf{C}$ in context $A$ is an $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-continuous $\mathcal{B}$-functor
    \[
    {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\to\mathsf{C}
    \]
    defined in context $A$.

    The $\infty$-category of $\mathsf{E}$-monoids in $\mathsf{C}$ is
    \[
    \mathrm{CMon}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{C})
    :=\mathrm{Fun}^{\mathsf{E}\text{-}\sqcap}({\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}),\mathsf{C}),
    \]
    and the $\mathcal{B}$-category of $\mathsf{E}$-monoids in $\mathsf{C}$ is
    \[
    {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{C})
    :=\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{E}\text{-}\sqcap}({\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}),\mathsf{C}).
    \]
    Thus an object of ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{C})(A)$ is an $\mathsf{E}$-monoid in context $A$.

    When $\mathsf{C}$ is omitted, it is understood to be $\mathsf{\Omega}$. When the context is omitted, it is understood to be $A=*$.
<!-- end definition-16 -->
<!-- example-3: body_md -->
\label{example:Fin_monoids}
    Let $\mathcal{B}=\mathrm{Ani}$, and let $\mathsf{Fin}\subset\mathsf{\Omega}$ be the context-free subuniverse of finite covering maps from \crtCref{example:Fin_in_Ani}. A $\mathsf{Fin}$-monoid in $\mathsf{C}$ is the same as a commutative monoid in $\mathsf{C}(*)$. Indeed, global sections identify the $\infty$-category of $\mathrm{Ani}$-categories with $\mathrm{Cat}$.
<!-- end example-3 -->
<!-- proposition-16: body_md -->
\label{example:free_E_monoid}
    The $\mathcal{B}$-groupoid $\mathsf{E}^{\simeq}$ carries a natural $\mathsf{E}$-monoid structure. With this structure, it is the free $\mathsf{E}$-monoid on one generator: it corepresents the forgetful $\mathcal{B}$-functor ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{\Omega})\to\mathsf{\Omega}$.
<!-- end proposition-16 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
The representable $\mathcal{B}$-functor
    \[
    {\mathsf{map}}(*,-):{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\to\mathsf{\Omega}
    \]
    preserves limits and hence defines an $\mathsf{E}$-monoid. Its underlying object is ${\mathsf{map}}(*,*)\simeq\mathsf{E}^{\simeq}$.

    By the internal Yoneda lemma, for every $\mathcal{B}$-functor $F:{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\to\mathsf{\Omega}$, there is a natural equivalence of $\mathcal{B}$-anima
    \[
    {\mathsf{map}}({\mathsf{map}}(*,-),F)\simeq F(*).
    \]
    Since ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{\Omega})$ is a full $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory of $\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}({\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}),\mathsf{\Omega})$, this proves the universal property.
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- proposition-17: body_md -->
\label{prop:cmon_is_presentable}
    The $\mathcal{B}$-category ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{\Omega})$ is $\mathcal{B}$-presentable.
<!-- end proposition-17 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
We show that
    \[
    {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{\Omega})\subset\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}({\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}),\mathsf{\Omega})
    \]
    is a Bousfield localization at a small $\mathcal{B}$-category of morphisms. This suffices by \cite[Corollary 2.4.2.9 and Theorem 2.4.2.5]{MWPresentabilityAndTopoi}.

    Let $F:{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\to\mathsf{\Omega}$ be a $\mathcal{B}$-functor. Choose $[C\to B]\in\mathsf{E}(B)$ and $[p:B\to A]\in\mathsf{E}(A)$, and let $x$ denote $[C\to B]$, viewed as a $B$-shaped diagram in ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})$ in context $A$. By \crtCref{prop:limits_in_span_E}, its limit $p_*x$ is $[C\to A]$.

    Write
    \[
    \text{\usefont{U}{dmjhira}{m}{n}\symbol{"48}}(A):{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})^{\mathrm{op}}(A)\hookrightarrow\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}({\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}),\mathsf{\Omega})(A)
    \]
    for the internal Yoneda embedding in context $A$. Thus $\text{\usefont{U}{dmjhira}{m}{n}\symbol{"48}}(A)(D)$ is the internally representable functor associated to $D\in{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})(A)$. By the internal Yoneda lemma and the adjunction for $p_\sharp$, we have
    \[
    F(p_*x)\simeq{\mathsf{map}}(\text{\usefont{U}{dmjhira}{m}{n}\symbol{"48}}(A)(p_*x),F),
    \qquad
    p_*F(x)\simeq{\mathsf{map}}(p_\sharp\text{\usefont{U}{dmjhira}{m}{n}\symbol{"48}}(B)(x),F),
    \]
    where the mapping anima are formed in context $A$. The comparison map $F(p_*x)\to p_*F(x)$ is obtained by applying ${\mathsf{map}}(-,F)$ to the canonical morphism
    \[
    p_\sharp\text{\usefont{U}{dmjhira}{m}{n}\symbol{"48}}(B)(x)\to\text{\usefont{U}{dmjhira}{m}{n}\symbol{"48}}(A)(p_*x).
    \]

    Consequently, ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{\Omega})$ is the full $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory of objects that are Bousfield local with respect to these morphisms. They generate a small $\mathcal{B}$-category: they lie in the small $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory generated from representables under $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-colimits.
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- definition-17: body_md -->
Let $\mathsf{E}$ be a context-free subuniverse. Define $\mathsf{\Omega}_{\mathsf{E}}\subset\mathsf{\Omega}$ to be the wide $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory whose morphisms in context $A$ are maps $C\to B$ over $A$ such that $[C\to B]\in\mathsf{E}(B)$.
<!-- end definition-17 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
\label{prop:groupoid_limits_span_universe_E}
    The pair $(\mathsf{\Omega},\mathsf{\Omega}_{\mathsf{E}})$ is a $\mathcal{B}$-span pair. The $\mathcal{B}$-category ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{\Omega},\mathsf{\Omega}_{\mathsf{E}})$ is $\mathsf{\Omega}$-complete, and the inclusion
    \[
    \mathsf{\Omega}^{\mathrm{op}}\hookrightarrow{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{\Omega},\mathsf{\Omega}_{\mathsf{E}})
    \]
    is $\mathsf{\Omega}$-continuous.

    Moreover, for a $\mathcal{B}$-category $\mathsf{C}$, a $\mathcal{B}$-functor $F:{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{\Omega},\mathsf{\Omega}_{\mathsf{E}})\to\mathsf{C}$ is $\mathsf{\Omega}$-continuous if and only if the composite
    \[
    \mathsf{\Omega}^{\mathrm{op}}\hookrightarrow{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{\Omega},\mathsf{\Omega}_{\mathsf{E}})\xrightarrow{F}\mathsf{C}
    \]
    is $\mathsf{\Omega}$-continuous.
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
The argument is the same as in \crtCref{prop:limits_in_span_E,prop:limits_in_span_E_are_computed_in_E_op}.
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- proposition-18: body_md -->
\label{prop:extra_back_functoriality_for_E_monoidal_cats}
    Let $\mathsf{C}$ be a complete $\mathcal{B}$-category. Restriction induces an equivalence of $\mathcal{B}$-categories
    \[
    \underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{\Omega}\text{-}\sqcap}({\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{\Omega},\mathsf{\Omega}_{\mathsf{E}}),\mathsf{C})
    \simeq\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{E}\text{-}\sqcap}({\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}),\mathsf{C})
    ={\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{C}),
    \]
    with inverse given by right Kan extension.
<!-- end proposition-18 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
We follow the proof of \cite[Lemma 5.21]{CLLambi}. Restriction along the fully faithful inclusion ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\hookrightarrow{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{\Omega},\mathsf{\Omega}_{\mathsf{E}})$ gives a $\mathcal{B}$-functor
    \[
    F:\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}({\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{\Omega},\mathsf{\Omega}_{\mathsf{E}}),\mathsf{C})
    \to\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}({\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}),\mathsf{C}).
    \]
    By \crtCref{prop:limits_in_span_E_are_computed_in_E_op,prop:groupoid_limits_span_universe_E}, this restricts to
    \[
    G:\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{\Omega}\text{-}\sqcap}({\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{\Omega},\mathsf{\Omega}_{\mathsf{E}}),\mathsf{C})
    \to\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{E}\text{-}\sqcap}({\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}),\mathsf{C}).
    \]
    Indeed, a $\mathcal{B}$-functor out of ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{\Omega},\mathsf{\Omega}_{\mathsf{E}})$ is $\mathsf{\Omega}$-continuous if and only if its restriction to $\mathsf{\Omega}^{\mathrm{op}}$ is right Kan extended from the point. Its restriction to $(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}})^{\mathrm{op}}$ is then also right Kan extended from the point.

    To show that $G$ is an equivalence, we apply \cite[Proposition 5.18]{CLLambi}. Both span categories have factorization systems given by backward-facing and forward-facing morphisms, as discussed after \cite[Convention 5.19]{CLLambi}. Their inclusion is compatible with these factorization systems. Moreover, if $X\in{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})(A)$ and $Y\to X$ is a forward-facing morphism in ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{\Omega},\mathsf{\Omega}_{\mathsf{E}})(A)$, then $Y$ also belongs to ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})(A)$. Thus
    \[
    {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})^{\mathrm{op}}\hookrightarrow{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{\Omega},\mathsf{\Omega}_{\mathsf{E}})^{\mathrm{op}}
    \]
    is a good inclusion in the sense of \cite[Definition 5.10]{CLLambi}, by \cite[Example 5.8]{CLLambi}. Proposition 5.18 of that work therefore identifies $G$ as an equivalence, with inverse given by right Kan extension.
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- definition-18: body_md -->
\label{def:free_on_A_with_E_colimits}
    For $A\in\mathcal{B}$, let $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}[A]$ denote the full $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory of $\mathsf{PSh}(A)$ generated by the image of the Yoneda embedding under $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-colimits.
<!-- end definition-18 -->
<!-- remark-8: body_md -->
When $\mathcal{B}=\mathrm{Ani}$ and $\mathsf{E}=\mathsf{Fin}$, the underlying groupoid of $\mathsf{Fin}[A](*)$ is the anima of maps from finite sets to $A$. Thus it is equivalent to
    \[
    \coprod_{n\in\mathbb{N}}(A^n)//\Sigma_n,
    \]
    as above.
<!-- end remark-8 -->
<!-- proposition-19: body_md -->
\label{prop:free_on_A_with_E_colimits}
    Let $A\in\mathcal{B}$, and let $\mathsf{C}$ be an $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-cocomplete $\mathcal{B}$-category. Restriction along the Yoneda embedding induces an equivalence of $\mathcal{B}$-categories
    \[
    \underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{E}\text{-}\sqcup}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}[A],\mathsf{C})
    \simeq\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}(A,\mathsf{C}).
    \]
<!-- end proposition-19 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
This is an application of \cite[Theorem 7.1.13]{MWcocomplete}.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- proposition-20: body_md -->
\label{prop:the_underlying_groupoid_of_the_free_cat_with_colims_on_E}
    For $A\in\mathcal{B}$, there is a natural equivalence of $\mathcal{B}$-anima
    \[
    {\mathsf{map}}_{{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{\Omega},\mathsf{\Omega}_{\mathsf{E}})}(A,*)
    \simeq\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}[A]^{\simeq}.
    \]
    Thus $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}[A]^{\simeq}$ is the underlying object of the $\mathsf{E}$-monoid obtained by restricting the representable functor ${\mathsf{map}}_{{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{\Omega},\mathsf{\Omega}_{\mathsf{E}})}(A,-)$.
<!-- end proposition-20 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
In context $B$, a morphism from $A$ to $*$ in ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{\Omega},\mathsf{\Omega}_{\mathsf{E}})$ is a span over $B$
    \[
    A\times B\longleftarrow X\longrightarrow B
    \]
    such that $[X\to B]\in\mathsf{E}(B)$. The anima of these spans is the core of the full subcategory of $\mathcal{B}_{/A\times B}$ on objects whose projection to $B$ belongs to $\mathsf{E}(B)$. By the description above, this is $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}[A](B)^{\simeq}$. These equivalences are compatible with pullback in $B$, and hence give the asserted equivalence of $\mathcal{B}$-anima.
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- proposition-21: body_md -->
\label{prop:free_E_monoid_on_A}
    Let $A\in\mathcal{B}$, and let $\mathsf{M}$ be an $\mathsf{E}$-monoid. There is a natural equivalence of $\mathcal{B}$-anima
    \[
    {\mathsf{map}}_{{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{\Omega})}(\mathsf{E}^{\simeq}[A],\mathsf{M})
    \simeq{\mathsf{map}}(A,\mathsf{M}(*)),
    \]
    where $\mathsf{M}(*)$ is the underlying object of $\mathsf{M}$.
<!-- end proposition-21 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
By \crtCref{prop:extra_back_functoriality_for_E_monoidal_cats}, $\mathsf{M}$ extends to a $\mathsf{\Omega}$-continuous $\mathcal{B}$-functor
    \[
    \widetilde{\mathsf{M}}:{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{\Omega},\mathsf{\Omega}_{\mathsf{E}})\to\mathsf{\Omega}.
    \]
    By \crtCref{prop:the_underlying_groupoid_of_the_free_cat_with_colims_on_E} and the internal Yoneda lemma, the mapping $\mathcal{B}$-anima on the left is equivalent to $\widetilde{\mathsf{M}}(A)$. Since $\widetilde{\mathsf{M}}$ is $\mathsf{\Omega}$-continuous, this is ${\mathsf{map}}(A,\mathsf{M}(*))$, as required. This is the same argument as in \crtCref{example:free_E_monoid}.
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- example-4: body_md -->
The $\mathcal{B}$-category $\mathsf{Cat}$ is $\mathcal{B}$-presentable and hence admits all $\mathcal{B}$-limits and colimits. An \emph{$\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category} is an $\mathsf{E}$-monoid in $\mathsf{Cat}$. The $\mathcal{B}$-category of these objects is ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})$.
<!-- end example-4 -->
<!-- definition-19: body_md -->
Let $F:{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\to\mathsf{Cat}$ be an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category. Its \emph{underlying $\mathcal{B}$-category} is $\mathsf{C}:=F(*)$, obtained by restriction along $\left\{*\right\}\hookrightarrow{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})$. We will often say that $\mathsf{C}$ is $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal or that it is equipped with an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal structure.
<!-- end definition-19 -->
<!-- proposition-22: body_md -->
\label{prop:values_of_E_monoidal_categories}
    Let $F:{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\to\mathsf{Cat}$ be an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category with underlying category $\mathsf{C}$. For every context $A\in\mathcal{B}$ and every $[s:B\to A]\in\mathsf{E}(A)$, there are canonical equivalences of $\mathcal{B}_{/A}$-categories
    \[
    F(B)\simeq s_*s^*\mathsf{C}
    \simeq\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}_{\mathcal{B}_{/A}}(B,\mathsf{C}),
    \]
    where $\mathsf{C}$ on the right is restricted to context $A$.
<!-- end proposition-22 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
The limit functor $s_*:{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})(B)\to{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})(A)$ sends $[\mathrm{id}:B\to B]$ to $[s:B\to A]$. Since $F$ is $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-continuous, this gives the first equivalence. The second is the formula for this limit in $\mathsf{Cat}(A)$.
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- notation-3: body_md -->
\label{notation:exponent_and_lower_otimes}
    Let $F:{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\to\mathsf{Cat}$ be an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category with underlying category $\mathsf{C}$. For $[B\to A]\in\mathsf{E}(A)$, write
    \[
    \mathsf{C}^{B}:=F(B\to A)
    \simeq\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}_{\mathcal{B}_{/A}}(B,\mathsf{C})
    \in\mathsf{Cat}(A).
    \]
    For a morphism $s:C\to B$ in $\mathsf{E}(A)$, the span $C=C\xrightarrow{s}B$ induces a $\mathcal{B}_{/A}$-functor
    \[
