    s_\otimes:\mathsf{C}^{C}\to\mathsf{C}^{B}.
    \]
    Evaluating in context $A$ gives a functor of $\infty$-categories, denoted by the same symbol:
    \[
    s_\otimes:\mathsf{C}(C)
    \simeq(\mathsf{C}^{C})(A)
    \to(\mathsf{C}^{B})(A)
    \simeq\mathsf{C}(B).
    \]

    More generally, a span $B\xleftarrow{t}X\xrightarrow{s}C$ in ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})(A)$ induces the $\mathcal{B}_{/A}$-functor
    \[
    s_\otimes t^*:\mathsf{C}^{B}\to\mathsf{C}^{C}.
    \]
    Its evaluation in context $A$ is the functor
    \[
    s_\otimes t^*:\mathsf{C}(B)\to\mathsf{C}(C).
    \]
<!-- end notation-3 -->
<!-- proposition-23: body_md -->
\label{prop:cmon_is_cat_module_in_prl}
    The $\mathcal{B}$-category ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})$ is a module over $\mathsf{Cat}$ in $\mathrm{Pr}^{\mathrm{L}}(\mathcal{B})$.
<!-- end proposition-23 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
There are equivalences
    \begin{align*}
        \underline{\mathsf{Fun}}({\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}),\mathsf{Cat})
        &\simeq\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^R(\mathsf{PSh}({\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})^{\mathrm{op}})^{\mathrm{op}},\mathsf{Cat})\\
        &\simeq\mathsf{PSh}({\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})^{\mathrm{op}})\otimes\mathsf{Cat}
    \end{align*}
    in $\mathrm{Pr}^{\mathrm{L}}(\mathcal{B})$, where $\otimes$ is the multilinear tensor product of presentable $\mathcal{B}$-categories developed in \cite[\S 2.6]{MWPresentabilityAndTopoi}. By the universal property of the Bousfield localization from \crtCref{prop:cmon_is_presentable}, the $\mathcal{B}$-category
    \[
    \underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^R({\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{\Omega})^{\mathrm{op}},\mathsf{Cat})
    \]
    corresponds compatibly to the $\mathsf{E}$-continuous functors. Thus
    \[
    {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})
    \simeq{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{\Omega})\otimes\mathsf{Cat},
    \]
    which gives the asserted module structure.
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- corollary-5: body_md -->
\label{cor:cmon_is_tensored_and_powered_by_cat}
    There are $\mathcal{B}$-functors
    \[
    \underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{E}\text{-}\otimes}(-,-):
    {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})^{\mathrm{op}}\times{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})
    \to\mathsf{Cat}
    \]
    and
    \[
    (-)^{(-)}:{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})\times\mathsf{Cat}^{\mathrm{op}}
    \to{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat}),
    \]
    each preserving limits separately in both variables. There is also a bilinear $\mathcal{B}$-functor
    \[
    -\otimes-:{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})\times\mathsf{Cat}
    \to{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat}).
    \]
    For every $\mathcal{B}$-category $\mathsf{C}$, there is a canonical equivalence of $\mathcal{B}$-categories, natural in both remaining variables,
    \[
    \underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{E}\text{-}\otimes}(-\otimes\mathsf{C},-)
    \simeq\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{E}\text{-}\otimes}(-,(-)^{\mathsf{C}}).
    \]
    Moreover, taking the underlying groupoid of the mapping category recovers the mapping $\mathcal{B}$-anima:
    \[
    \underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{E}\text{-}\otimes}(-,-)^{\simeq}
    \simeq{\mathsf{map}}_{{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})}(-,-).
    \]
<!-- end corollary-5 -->
<!-- proposition-24: body_md -->
\label{example:free_E_monoidal_cat}
    Let $A\in\mathcal{B}$, and let $\mathsf{C}$ be an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category. There is a natural equivalence of $\mathcal{B}$-categories
    \[
    \underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{E}\text{-}\otimes}(\mathsf{E}^{\simeq}[A],\mathsf{C})
    \simeq\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}(A,\mathsf{C}).
    \]
<!-- end proposition-24 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
This follows from \crtCref{prop:free_E_monoid_on_A,prop:cmon_is_cat_module_in_prl}.
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- definition-20: body_md -->
Let $\mathsf{C}$ be an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category. A $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory $\mathsf{D}\subset\mathsf{C}$ is an \emph{$\mathsf{E}$-monoidal subcategory} if, for every $[s:B\to A]\in\mathsf{E}(A)$ and every morphism $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathsf{D}(B)$, the morphism
    \[
    s_\otimes(f):s_\otimes(X)\to s_\otimes(Y)
    \]
    belongs to $\mathsf{D}(A)$.
<!-- end definition-20 -->
<!-- proposition-25: body_md -->
\label{prop:monoidal_subcategories_are_monoidal}
    Let $F:{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\to\mathsf{Cat}$ be an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category with underlying category $\mathsf{C}$, and let $\mathsf{D}\subset\mathsf{C}$ be an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal subcategory. There is a subfunctor $G\hookrightarrow F$ that equips $\mathsf{D}$ with an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal structure.

    Moreover, $G\to F$ is terminal among $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functors $T\to F$ whose underlying functor $T(*)\to\mathsf{C}$ factors through $\mathsf{D}$.
<!-- end proposition-25 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
In context $A$, define
    \[
    G(B):=\mathsf{D}^B\subset\mathsf{C}^B\simeq F(B).
    \]
    To obtain a subfunctor, it suffices to check compatibility with restriction along morphisms in $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}(A)$ and tensor products along morphisms in $\mathsf{E}(A)$. Restriction preserves $\mathsf{D}$ because it is a $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory of $\mathsf{C}$. The tensor functors preserve $\mathsf{D}$ by assumption. The formula $G(B)=\mathsf{D}^B$ also shows that $G$ is $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-continuous, so it defines an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal structure on $\mathsf{D}$.

    The inclusion $G\hookrightarrow F$ is a monomorphism in $\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}({\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}),\mathsf{Cat})$. For an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functor $T\to F$, the underlying functor $T(*)\to\mathsf{C}$ factors through $\mathsf{D}$ if and only if, in every context $A$ and for every $B\in{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})(A)$, the functor $T(B)\to F(B)$ factors through $\mathsf{D}^B=G(B)$. This proves the universal property.
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- theorem-7: body_md -->
\label{thm:monoidal_localization}
    Let $F:{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\to\mathsf{Cat}$ be an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category with underlying category $\mathsf{C}$. Let $i:\mathsf{D}\hookrightarrow\mathsf{C}$ be a reflective (respectively, coreflective) $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory, with reflection (respectively, coreflection) $L:\mathsf{C}\to\mathsf{D}$. Let
    \[
    \mathsf{S}:=L^{-1}(\mathsf{D}^{\simeq})\subset\mathsf{C}
    \]
    be the wide $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory of morphisms inverted by $L$. Suppose that $\mathsf{S}$ is an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal subcategory. Then $\mathsf{D}$ carries a canonical $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal structure for which $L$ is $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal.

    Moreover, for every $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category $\mathsf{T}$, precomposition with $L$ defines a fully faithful $\mathcal{B}$-functor
    \[
    \underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{E}\text{-}\otimes}(\mathsf{D},\mathsf{T})
    \to\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{E}\text{-}\otimes}(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{T}),
    \]
    whose essential image consists of the functors that send every morphism in $\mathsf{S}$ to an equivalence.
<!-- end theorem-7 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
Apply \crtCref{prop:monoidal_subcategories_are_monoidal} to $\mathsf{S}\subset\mathsf{C}$ to obtain a subfunctor $G\hookrightarrow F$. Define $H:{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\to\mathsf{Cat}$ by the pointwise pushout
    \[
    H(-):=G(-)^{\operatorname{gpd}}\coprod_{G(-)}F(-).
    \]
    For $[B\to A]\in{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})(A)$, we claim that
    \[
    H(B)\simeq(\mathsf{S}^B)^{\operatorname{gpd}}
    \coprod_{\mathsf{S}^B}\mathsf{C}^B
    \simeq\mathsf{D}^B.
    \]
    Indeed, $\mathsf{S}^B$ is the wide subcategory of morphisms inverted by $L^B:\mathsf{C}^B\to\mathsf{D}^B$, so this is the pushout description of localization in \cite[Proposition 3.4.6]{MWcocomplete}.

    The identification $H(B)\simeq\mathsf{D}^B$ shows that $H$ is $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-continuous. Thus $H$ equips $\mathsf{D}$ with an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal structure, and the natural transformation $F\to H$ equips $L$ with an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal structure. The universal property follows from that of the pushout.
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- proposition-26: body_md -->
\label{prop:categories_with_E_colimits_have_E_monoidal_structure}
    Let $\mathsf{C}$ be an $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-cocomplete $\mathcal{B}$-category. There is an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category $\operatorname{Equip}^{\operatorname{cc}}(\mathsf{C})$ with underlying category $\mathsf{C}$ such that, for every $[p:B\to A]\in\mathsf{E}(A)$,
    \[
    p_\otimes\simeq p_\sharp:\mathsf{C}(B)\to\mathsf{C}(A).
    \]
    This construction is functorial in $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-cocontinuous $\mathcal{B}$-functors.
<!-- end proposition-26 -->
<!-- proof-40: body_md -->
Recall that $\mathsf{Cat}^{\mathsf{E}\text{-}\sqcup}$ denotes the $\mathcal{B}$-category of $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-cocomplete $\mathcal{B}$-categories and $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-cocontinuous $\mathcal{B}$-functors. It is closed under all $\mathcal{B}$-limits in $\mathsf{Cat}$. By the dual of \crtCref{prop:S_is_free_with_S_colmitis}, there are equivalences of $\mathcal{B}$-categories
    \[
    \mathsf{Cat}^{\mathsf{E}\text{-}\sqcup}
    \simeq\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}(*,\mathsf{Cat}^{\mathsf{E}\text{-}\sqcup})
    \simeq\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{E}\text{-}\sqcap}
    ((\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}})^{\mathrm{op}},\mathsf{Cat}^{\mathsf{E}\text{-}\sqcup}).
    \]

    Let $F:(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}})^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{Cat}^{\mathsf{E}\text{-}\sqcup}$ correspond to $\mathsf{C}$ under this equivalence. We claim that its underlying $\mathcal{B}$-functor to $\mathsf{Cat}$ is left $\mathsf{E}$-adjointable in the sense of \crtCref{const:internal_unfurling}. In each context, $F$ sends a morphism $p:B\to A$ in $\mathsf{E}$ to the restriction functor
    \[
    p^*:\mathsf{C}^{A}\to\mathsf{C}^{B}.
    \]
    Since $\mathsf{C}$ is $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-cocomplete, this functor admits an internal left adjoint $p_\sharp$. The required Beck--Chevalley conditions are those for indexed colimits in $\mathsf{C}$. Moreover, $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-cocontinuous functors commute with these indexed colimits and therefore induce morphisms of left $\mathsf{E}$-adjointable functors.

    Internal unfurling thus gives a $\mathcal{B}$-functor
    \[
    \underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{E}\text{-}\sqcap}
    ((\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}})^{\mathrm{op}},\mathsf{Cat}^{\mathsf{E}\text{-}\sqcup})
    \to\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}({\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}),\mathsf{Cat}).
    \]
    The unfurled functor still takes values in $\mathsf{Cat}^{\mathsf{E}\text{-}\sqcup}$: the original restriction functors preserve these colimits, and so do the added left adjoints $p_\sharp$. By \crtCref{prop:limits_in_span_E_are_computed_in_E_op}, it is $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-continuous because its restriction to $(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}})^{\mathrm{op}}$ is. It therefore defines an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal structure on $\mathsf{C}$, with $p_\otimes\simeq p_\sharp$ by the construction of unfurling. Functoriality follows from functoriality of unfurling.
<!-- end proof-40 -->
<!-- remark-9: body_md -->
When the cocartesian structure is understood, we will sometimes omit $\operatorname{Equip}^{\operatorname{cc}}$ from the notation.
<!-- end remark-9 -->
<!-- proposition-27: body_md -->
\label{prop:categories_with_E_limits_have_E_monoidal_structure}
    Let $\mathsf{C}$ be an $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-complete $\mathcal{B}$-category. There is an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category $\operatorname{Equip}^{\operatorname{ct}}(\mathsf{C})$ with underlying category $\mathsf{C}$ such that, for every $[p:B\to A]\in\mathsf{E}(A)$,
    \[
    p_\otimes\simeq p_*:\mathsf{C}(B)\to\mathsf{C}(A).
    \]
    This construction is functorial in $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-continuous $\mathcal{B}$-functors.
<!-- end proposition-27 -->
<!-- proof-41: body_md -->
Apply \crtCref{prop:categories_with_E_colimits_have_E_monoidal_structure} to $\mathsf{C}^{\mathrm{op}}$ and then take opposites of the resulting categories. The indexed colimit functors for $\mathsf{C}^{\mathrm{op}}$ become the indexed limit functors for $\mathsf{C}$.
<!-- end proof-41 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
\label{lem:every_morphism_in_I_is_locally_truncated_on_the_target}
    Let $f:C\to B$ be a morphism in $\mathsf{I}(A)$. There is a cover $(s_i:A_i\to A)_i$ such that each $s_i^*f$ is truncated.
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- proof-42: body_md -->
By assumption, $B$ and $C$ are locally truncated. After taking a common refinement of the corresponding covers of $A$, the morphism $f$ is a morphism between truncated objects and hence is truncated.
<!-- end proof-42 -->
<!-- theorem-8: body_md -->
\label{thm:uniqueness_of_cartesian_structures}
    Let $\mathsf{I}$ be an inductible context-free subuniverse. The $\mathcal{B}$-functor
    \[
    \operatorname{Equip}^{\operatorname{cc}}:\mathsf{Cat}^{\mathsf{I}\text{-}\sqcup}
    \to{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{Cat})
    \]
    is fully faithful.
<!-- end theorem-8 -->
<!-- proof-43: body_md -->
By \crtCref{lem:every_morphism_in_I_is_locally_truncated_on_the_target}, the hypotheses of \crtCref{thm:internal_uniqueness_of_unfurling} hold. Thus internal unfurling gives an equivalence of $\mathcal{B}$-categories
    \[
    \underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{I}\text{-adjointable}}(\mathsf{I}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathsf{Cat})
    \simeq
    \underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{I}\text{-adjointed}}({\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{I}),\mathsf{Cat}).
    \]
    By \crtCref{prop:limits_in_span_E_are_computed_in_E_op}, it restricts to an equivalence
    \[
    \underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{I}\text{-}\sqcap,\mathsf{I}\text{-adjointable}}
    (\mathsf{I}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathsf{Cat})
    \simeq
    \underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{I}\text{-}\sqcap,\mathsf{I}\text{-adjointed}}
    ({\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{I}),\mathsf{Cat}).
    \]
    The right-hand side is a full $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory of ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{Cat})$.

    On the left, the equivalence
    \[
    \underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{I}\text{-}\sqcap}(\mathsf{I}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathsf{Cat})
    \simeq\mathsf{Cat}
    \]
    coming from \crtCref{prop:S_is_free_with_S_colmitis} identifies adjointable functors with $\mathsf{I}$-cocomplete $\mathcal{B}$-categories and adjointable natural transformations with $\mathsf{I}$-cocontinuous $\mathcal{B}$-functors. It therefore restricts to
    \[
    \underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{I}\text{-}\sqcap,\mathsf{I}\text{-adjointable}}
    (\mathsf{I}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathsf{Cat})
    \simeq\mathsf{Cat}^{\mathsf{I}\text{-}\sqcup}.
    \]
    Under these identifications, unfurling is precisely $\operatorname{Equip}^{\operatorname{cc}}$. Hence $\operatorname{Equip}^{\operatorname{cc}}$ identifies its source with the full $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory of $\mathsf{I}$-adjointed objects in ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{Cat})$.
<!-- end proof-43 -->
<!-- definition-21: body_md -->
\label{def:cartesian_S_monoidal_category}
    Let $\mathsf{I}$ be an inductible context-free subuniverse, and let $\mathsf{C}$ be an $\mathsf{I}$-complete $\mathsf{I}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category.
    \begin{mylist}
        \item For a $(-2)$-truncated morphism $s:A\to B$ in $\mathsf{I}$, that is, an equivalence, there is a canonical equivalence
        \[
        N_s:s_\otimes\to s_*.
        \]
        We call this the $s$-norm. Every such $\mathsf{C}$ is declared to be $(-2)$-cartesian.
        \item Suppose that $\mathsf{C}$ is $n$-cartesian. For an $(n+1)$-truncated morphism $s:A\to B$ in $\mathsf{I}$, define the $s$-norm $N_s:s_\otimes\to s_*$ to be the mate of the composite
        \[
        \begin{aligned}
        s^*s_\otimes
        &\simeq(\pi_1)_\otimes\pi_2^*
        \to(\pi_1)_\otimes\Delta_*\Delta^*\pi_2^*\\
        &\xrightarrow{N_\Delta^{-1}}
        (\pi_1)_\otimes\Delta_\otimes\Delta^*\pi_2^*
        \simeq\mathrm{id}_\otimes\mathrm{id}^*=\mathrm{id},
        \end{aligned}
        \]
        where the maps are given by the diagram
        \[
        \begin{tikzcd}
            A\\
            &{A\times_B A}\arrow[rd,"\lrcorner"{anchor=center,pos=0.125},draw=none]&A\\
            &A&B.
            \arrow["\Delta"',from=1-1,to=2-2]
            \arrow[curve={height=-6pt},equal,from=1-1,to=2-3]
            \arrow[curve={height=6pt},equal,from=1-1,to=3-2]
            \arrow["\pi_2",from=2-2,to=2-3]
            \arrow["\pi_1"',from=2-2,to=3-2]
            \arrow["s",from=2-3,to=3-3]
            \arrow["s"',from=3-2,to=3-3]
        \end{tikzcd}
        \]
        The inverse of $N_\Delta$ exists because $\Delta$ is $n$-truncated and $\mathsf{C}$ is $n$-cartesian.
        \item We say that $\mathsf{C}$ is $(n+1)$-cartesian if it is $n$-cartesian and $N_s$ is an equivalence for every $(n+1)$-truncated morphism $s$ in $\mathsf{I}$.
    \end{mylist}
    We say that $\mathsf{C}$ is \emph{inductively cartesian} if it is $\mathsf{I}$-complete and is $n$-cartesian for every $n\geq-2$.
<!-- end definition-21 -->
<!-- proposition-28: body_md -->
An $\mathsf{I}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category is cartesian if and only if it is inductively cartesian.
<!-- end proposition-28 -->
<!-- proof-44: body_md -->
This follows from \crtCref{thm:internal_uniqueness_of_unfurling} applied to the opposite $\mathsf{I}$-monoidal structure.
<!-- end proof-44 -->
<!-- para-2: body_md -->
\begin{mylist}
        \item Let $\mathsf{I}$ be an inductible context-free subuniverse.
        \item\label{prop:op_is_also_monoidal} If $\mathsf{C}$ is an $\mathsf{I}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category, then $\mathsf{C}^{\mathrm{op}}$ carries the opposite $\mathsf{I}$-monoidal structure, defined by the composite
        \[
        {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{I})\to\mathsf{Cat}
        \xrightarrow{(-)^{\mathrm{op}}}\mathsf{Cat}.
        \]
        \item We say that $\mathsf{C}$ is $m$-cocartesian if $\mathsf{C}^{\mathrm{op}}$ is $m$-cartesian, and that $\mathsf{C}$ is cocartesian if $\mathsf{C}^{\mathrm{op}}$ is cartesian.
        \item By \crtCref{thm:uniqueness_of_cartesian_structures}, forgetting the cocartesian structure induces an equivalence of $\mathcal{B}$-categories
        \[
        {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{Cat})^{\text{cocart}}
        \simeq\mathsf{Cat}^{\mathsf{I}\text{-}\sqcup}.
        \]
    \end{mylist}
<!-- end para-2 -->
<!-- proposition-29: body_md -->
\label{prop:C_is_cartesian_iff_tensor_preserves_limits}
    Let $\mathsf{I}$ be an inductible context-free subuniverse, and let $\mathsf{C}$ be an $\mathsf{I}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category. Then $\mathsf{C}$ is $\mathsf{I}$-(co)cartesian if and only if, for every context $A$ and every morphism $p:C\to B$ in $\mathsf{I}(A)$, the functor
    \[
    p_\otimes:\mathsf{C}^{C}\to\mathsf{C}^{B}
    \]
    is $\mathsf{I}$-(co)continuous.
<!-- end proposition-29 -->
<!-- proof-45: body_md -->
The argument is the same as in \cite[Proposition 3.44]{CLLambi}.
<!-- end proof-45 -->
<!-- theorem-9: body_md -->
\label{Thm:CLL_amby}
    Let $\mathsf{C}$ be an $\mathsf{I}$-cartesian $\mathcal{B}$-category. The forgetful functor
    \[
    {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{C})\to\mathsf{C},
    \qquad M\mapsto M(*),
    \]
    is terminal among $\mathsf{I}$-cartesian $\mathcal{B}$-categories over $\mathsf{C}$ that are also cocartesian.
<!-- end theorem-9 -->
<!-- corollary-6: body_md -->
\label{cor:doubling}
    The forgetful $\mathcal{B}$-functor
    \[
    {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}({\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{Cat}))
    \to{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{Cat})
    \]
    is an equivalence. Its inverse $\delta$ sends an $\mathsf{I}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category $F:{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{I})\to\mathsf{Cat}$ to
    \[
    \delta(F):{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{I})\to{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{Cat}).
    \]
    The underlying functor with values in $\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}({\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{I}),\mathsf{Cat})$ is obtained by currying the composite
    \[
    {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{I})\times{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{I})
    \xrightarrow{\times}{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{I})\xrightarrow{F}\mathsf{Cat}.
    \]
<!-- end corollary-6 -->
<!-- definition-22: body_md -->
Following \cite{CLLambi}, an $\mathsf{I}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category is \emph{$\mathsf{I}$-ambidextrous} if it is both $\mathsf{I}$-cartesian and $\mathsf{I}$-cocartesian. We write $\mathsf{Cat}^{\mathsf{I}\text{-}\oplus}$ for the $\mathcal{B}$-category of $\mathsf{I}$-ambidextrous categories.
<!-- end definition-22 -->
<!-- remark-10: body_md -->
Equivalently, \crtCref{Thm:CLL_amby} states that ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}$ is right adjoint to the inclusion
    \[
    \mathsf{Cat}^{\mathsf{I}\text{-}\oplus}
    \hookrightarrow\mathsf{Cat}^{\mathsf{I}\text{-}\sqcap}.
    \]
<!-- end remark-10 -->
<!-- corollary-7: body_md -->
\label{lem:no_endomorphisms_of_CMon}
    Let $\mathsf{C}$ be an $\mathsf{I}$-cartesian $\mathcal{B}$-category. There is an equivalence of $\mathcal{B}$-categories
    \[
    \underline{\mathsf{Fun}}_{/\mathsf{C}}({\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{C}),{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{C}))
    \simeq *.
    \]
<!-- end corollary-7 -->
<!-- proof-46: body_md -->
The forgetful functor ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{C})\to\mathsf{C}$ is $\mathsf{I}$-continuous and conservative. Hence every endofunctor over $\mathsf{C}$ is $\mathsf{I}$-continuous. The result now follows from the universal property in \crtCref{Thm:CLL_amby}.
<!-- end proof-46 -->
<!-- question-1: body_md -->
\label{question:no_endomorphism_of_cmon_without_iductiblity}
    For $\mathsf{C}=\mathsf{Cat}$, does \crtCref{lem:no_endomorphisms_of_CMon} hold without assuming that the context-free subuniverse $\mathsf{E}$ is inductible? We expect that it does, but do not know a proof or a counterexample.
<!-- end question-1 -->
<!-- proposition-30: body_md -->
The $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory $\mathsf{E}\subset\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$ is an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal subcategory of $\operatorname{Equip}^{\operatorname{cc}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}})$.
<!-- end proposition-30 -->
<!-- proof-47: body_md -->
We must check that morphisms in $\mathsf{E}$ are closed under the indexed tensor products in $\operatorname{Equip}^{\operatorname{cc}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}})$. These tensor products are $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-indexed colimits, computed by forgetting context. Membership in $\mathsf{E}$ is independent of context, so the result follows.
<!-- end proof-47 -->
<!-- definition-23: body_md -->
\label{def:E_algebras_and_coalgebras}
    Let $\mathsf{C}$ be an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category. An \emph{$\mathsf{E}$-commutative coalgebra} in $\mathsf{C}$ is an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functor $\mathsf{E}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{C}$. The $\mathcal{B}$-category of these coalgebras is
    \[
    {\mathsf{coCAlg}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{C})
    :=\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{E}\text{-}\otimes}(\mathsf{E}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathsf{C}).
    \]
    Similarly, an \emph{$\mathsf{E}$-commutative algebra} in $\mathsf{C}$ is an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functor $\mathsf{E}\to\mathsf{C}$, and we write
    \[
    {\mathsf{CAlg}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{C})
    :=\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{E}\text{-}\otimes}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{C}).
    \]
    The underlying object of an algebra or coalgebra $F$ is $F(*)$. We will sometimes refer to this object as the algebra or coalgebra itself.
<!-- end definition-23 -->
<!-- corollary-8: body_md -->
\label{cor:cmon_is_self_enriched_if_inductible}
    Let $\mathsf{I}$ be an inductible context-free subuniverse. The $\mathcal{B}$-functor
    \[
    \underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{I}\text{-}\otimes}:
    {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{Cat})^{\mathrm{op}}\times{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{Cat})
    \to\mathsf{Cat}
    \]
    lifts canonically to a $\mathcal{B}$-functor
    \[
    \underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{I}\text{-}\otimes}:
    {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{Cat})^{\mathrm{op}}\times{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{Cat})
    \to{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{Cat}).
    \]
<!-- end corollary-8 -->
<!-- proof-48: body_md -->
Apply \crtCref{Thm:CLL_amby} in the second variable. The $\mathcal{B}$-category ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{Cat})$ is both $\mathsf{I}$-cartesian and $\mathsf{I}$-cocartesian, and $\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{I}\text{-}\otimes}(\mathsf{C},-)$ preserves $\mathsf{I}$-limits. The canonical lift is also functorial in $\mathsf{C}$.
<!-- end proof-48 -->
<!-- example-5: body_md -->
By \crtCref{example:free_E_monoidal_cat}, there is a natural equivalence
    \[
    \underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{I}\text{-}\otimes}(\mathsf{I}^{\simeq},\mathsf{C})
    \simeq\mathsf{C}.
    \]
    More generally, for $A\in\mathcal{B}$, both endofunctors
    \[
    (-)^A,\qquad
    \underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{I}\text{-}\otimes}(\mathsf{I}^{\simeq}[A],-)
    \]
    of ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{Cat})$ lift the composite
    \[
    {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{Cat})\to\mathsf{Cat}
    \xrightarrow{(-)^A}\mathsf{Cat}.
    \]
    By \crtCref{lem:no_endomorphisms_of_CMon}, these lifts are canonically equivalent.
<!-- end example-5 -->
<!-- proposition-31: body_md -->
\label{prop:evaluation_is_I_monoidal}
    Let $\mathsf{C}$ and $\mathsf{D}$ be $\mathsf{I}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-categories, and let $x:A\to\mathsf{C}$ be an object in context $A$. The evaluation functor
    \[
    \operatorname{ev}_x:
    \underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{I}\text{-}\otimes}(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{D})
    \to\mathsf{D}^A
    \]
    is canonically $\mathsf{I}$-monoidal.
<!-- end proposition-31 -->
<!-- proof-49: body_md -->
Under the preceding identification, evaluation is precomposition with the $\mathsf{I}$-monoidal functor $\mathsf{I}^{\simeq}[A]\to\mathsf{C}$ corresponding to $x$.
<!-- end proof-49 -->
<!-- definition-24: body_md -->
In view of \crtCref{prop:evaluation_is_I_monoidal}, we call the structure on $\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{I}\text{-}\otimes}(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{D})$ supplied by \crtCref{cor:cmon_is_self_enriched_if_inductible} the \emph{pointwise $\mathsf{I}$-monoidal structure}.
<!-- end definition-24 -->
<!-- proposition-32: body_md -->
For an $\mathsf{I}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category $\mathsf{C}$, the pointwise structure makes
    \[
    {\mathsf{CAlg}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{C})
    =\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{I}\text{-}\otimes}(\mathsf{I},\mathsf{C})
    \]
    an $\mathsf{I}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category.
<!-- end proposition-32 -->
<!-- proof-50: body_md -->
Apply \crtCref{cor:cmon_is_self_enriched_if_inductible} with first variable $\mathsf{I}$.
<!-- end proof-50 -->
<!-- proposition-33: body_md -->
\label{prop:forgetful_from_calg_is_internally_representable}
    The forgetful functor ${\mathsf{CAlg}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{C})\to\mathsf{C}$ is internally represented in ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{Cat})$ by the canonical $\mathsf{I}$-monoidal inclusion
    \[
    \mathsf{I}^{\simeq}\hookrightarrow\mathsf{I}.
    \]
    More explicitly, it is the functor induced by precomposition,
    \[
    \underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{I}\text{-}\otimes}(\mathsf{I},\mathsf{C})
    \to\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{I}\text{-}\otimes}(\mathsf{I}^{\simeq},\mathsf{C})
    \simeq\mathsf{C}.
    \]
<!-- end proposition-33 -->
<!-- proof-51: body_md -->
The universal property of $\mathsf{I}^{\simeq}$ identifies the last equivalence with evaluation at the point. Thus the displayed composite sends an algebra $F$ to $F(*)$, as required.
<!-- end proof-51 -->
<!-- proposition-34: body_md -->
\label{prop:calg_has_E_colimits}
    Let $\mathsf{I}$ be an inductible context-free subuniverse, and let $\mathsf{C}$ be an $\mathsf{I}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category. The pointwise $\mathsf{I}$-monoidal structure on
    \[
    {\mathsf{CAlg}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{C})
    \simeq\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{I}\text{-}\otimes}(\mathsf{I},\mathsf{C})
    \]
    is cocartesian.
<!-- end proposition-34 -->
<!-- proof-52: body_md -->
Let $[s:B\to A]\in\mathsf{I}(A)$. We construct a unit and counit for $s_\otimes\dashv s^*$. Write $*_A=[\mathrm{id}:A\to A]\in\mathsf{I}(A)$ and similarly for $*_B$.

    Consider the counit morphism
    \[
    \mu_s:s_\sharp s^* *_A\to *_A
    \]
    in $\mathsf{I}(A)$, which we call the \emph{universal multiplication}. It is canonically a morphism of $\mathsf{I}$-algebras, using the equivalences
    \[
    \begin{aligned}
    {\mathsf{CAlg}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{I})
    &=\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{I}\text{-}\otimes}(\mathsf{I},\mathsf{I})\\
    &\simeq\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{I}\text{-}\sqcup}(\mathsf{I},\mathsf{I})
    \simeq\mathsf{I}.
    \end{aligned}
    \]

    For $R\in{\mathsf{CAlg}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{C})(A)$, there is an identification
    \[
    (s_\otimes s^*R)(*_A)\simeq R(s_\sharp s^* *_A).
    \]
    Applying $R$ to the universal multiplication therefore gives a natural morphism whose underlying map is
    \[
    (s_\otimes s^*R)(*_A)
    \simeq R(s_\sharp s^* *_A)
    \xrightarrow{R(\mu_s)}R(*_A).
    \]
    Since $\mathsf{I}$-monoidal functors preserve $\mathsf{I}$-algebras, this is a morphism of algebras
    \[
    \mu_s^R:s_\otimes s^*R\to R.
    \]

    We next construct the unit for an arbitrary algebra $Q\in{\mathsf{CAlg}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{C})(B)$. Consider the diagram
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        B\\
        &{B\times_A B}\arrow[rd,"\lrcorner"{anchor=center,pos=0.125},draw=none]&B\\
        &B&A.
        \arrow["\Delta"',from=1-1,to=2-2]
        \arrow[curve={height=-6pt},equal,from=1-1,to=2-3]
        \arrow[curve={height=6pt},equal,from=1-1,to=3-2]
        \arrow["\pi_2",from=2-2,to=2-3]
        \arrow["\pi_1"',from=2-2,to=3-2]
        \arrow["s",from=2-3,to=3-3]
        \arrow["s"',from=3-2,to=3-3]
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    It gives a morphism in ${\mathsf{CAlg}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{C})(B)$:
    \[
    \begin{aligned}
    \upsilon_s^Q:Q
    &\simeq(\pi_1)_\otimes\Delta_\otimes\Delta^*\pi_2^*Q\\
    &\xrightarrow{(\pi_1)_\otimes\mu_\Delta^{\pi_2^*Q}}
    (\pi_1)_\otimes\pi_2^*Q
    \simeq s^*s_\otimes Q.
    \end{aligned}
    \]

    In $\mathsf{I}(B)$, write
    \[
    \upsilon_s:=\upsilon_s^{*_B}:*_B\to s^*s_\sharp *_B.
    \]
    We call this the \emph{universal split unit}. It identifies with the unit of the adjunction
    \[
    s_\sharp:\mathsf{I}(B)\leftrightarrows\mathsf{I}(A):s^*.
    \]
    We say that $Q$ \emph{splits} if $Q\simeq s^*R$ for some $R\in{\mathsf{CAlg}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{C})(A)$.

    If $Q$ splits, then $\pi_1^*Q\simeq\pi_2^*Q$, and hence
    \[
    Q(\upsilon_s)
    \simeq(\pi_1)_\otimes\mu_\Delta^{\pi_1^*Q}
    \simeq(\pi_1)_\otimes\mu_\Delta^{\pi_2^*Q}
    =\upsilon_s^Q.
    \]
    The first equivalence follows from functoriality of $Q$ and naturality of $\upsilon$ in ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{I})$. The second uses the splitting, and the last equality is the definition of $\upsilon_s^Q$.

    For arbitrary $Q$, the corresponding comparison holds after applying $s_\otimes$:
    \[
    \begin{aligned}
    s_\otimes\upsilon_s^Q
    &=s_\otimes(\pi_1)_\otimes\mu_\Delta^{\pi_2^*Q}\\
    &\simeq s_\otimes(\pi_2)_\otimes\mu_\Delta^{\pi_2^*Q}
    \simeq s_\otimes Q(\upsilon_s).
    \end{aligned}
    \]
    Here the first equality and the last equivalence are as above, while the middle equivalence uses $s\pi_1=s\pi_2$.

    These natural maps satisfy the triangle identities: the preceding comparisons reduce them to the identities for the universal algebra $*_-$. The Beck--Chevalley conditions hold as well. Thus $s_\otimes$ computes the indexed colimit along $s$, proving the proposition.
<!-- end proof-52 -->
<!-- remark-11: body_md -->
We expect this proposition to hold for every full context-free subuniverse $\mathsf{E}$, but to fail in general when $\mathsf{E}$ is not full.
<!-- end remark-11 -->
<!-- proposition-35: body_md -->
\label{prop:cocalg_has_E_limits}
    Let $\mathsf{I}$ be an inductible context-free subuniverse, and let $\mathsf{C}$ be an $\mathsf{I}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category. The pointwise $\mathsf{I}$-monoidal structure on
    \[
    {\mathsf{coCAlg}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{C})
    \simeq\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{I}\text{-}\otimes}(\mathsf{I}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathsf{C})
    \]
    is cartesian.
<!-- end proposition-35 -->
<!-- proof-53: body_md -->
Apply \crtCref{prop:calg_has_E_colimits} to $\mathsf{C}^{\mathrm{op}}$ and take opposites.
<!-- end proof-53 -->
<!-- proposition-36: body_md -->
\label{prop:calg_has_E_colimits_coherence}
    Let $\mathsf{I}$ be an inductible context-free subuniverse, and let $F:{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{I})\to\mathsf{Cat}$ be an $\mathsf{I}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category with underlying category $\mathsf{C}=F(*)$. The composite
    \[
    D:{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{I})\xrightarrow{\delta(F)}{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{Cat})
    \xrightarrow{{\mathsf{CAlg}}^{\mathsf{I}}}\mathsf{Cat}
    \]
    identifies with $\operatorname{Equip}^{\operatorname{cc}}({\mathsf{CAlg}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{C}))$.
<!-- end proposition-36 -->
<!-- proof-54: body_md -->
Both constructions lift the limit-preserving $\mathcal{B}$-functor
    \[
    {\mathsf{CAlg}}^{\mathsf{I}}:{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{Cat})\to\mathsf{Cat}.
    \]
    They are therefore equivalent by \crtCref{Thm:CLL_amby}.
<!-- end proof-54 -->
<!-- proposition-37: body_md -->
\label{prop:canonical_Calg_structure_for_cocartesian_categories}
    Let $\mathsf{C}$ be an $\mathsf{I}$-cocomplete $\mathcal{B}$-category. The composite
    \[
    \begin{aligned}
    \mathsf{C}
    &\simeq\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}(*,\mathsf{C})
    \simeq\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{I}\text{-}\sqcup}(\mathsf{I},\mathsf{C})\\
    &\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Equip}^{\operatorname{cc}}}
    \underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{I}\text{-}\otimes}
    (\operatorname{Equip}^{\operatorname{cc}}(\mathsf{I}),\operatorname{Equip}^{\operatorname{cc}}(\mathsf{C}))
    ={\mathsf{CAlg}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\operatorname{Equip}^{\operatorname{cc}}(\mathsf{C}))
    \end{aligned}
    \]
    is $\mathsf{I}$-cocontinuous and natural in $\mathsf{C}$.
<!-- end proposition-37 -->
<!-- proof-55: body_md -->
By \crtCref{prop:calg_has_E_colimits}, colimits in the target are given by its pointwise tensor products. These are induced by the tensor products in $\operatorname{Equip}^{\operatorname{cc}}(\mathsf{C})$, which are the indexed colimits in $\mathsf{C}$ by \crtCref{prop:categories_with_E_colimits_have_E_monoidal_structure}. Thus the displayed functor is $\mathsf{I}$-cocontinuous.

    Naturality of the free cocontinuous extension follows from naturality of left Kan extension. The final functor is natural by functoriality of $\operatorname{Equip}^{\operatorname{cc}}$.
<!-- end proof-55 -->
<!-- proposition-38: body_md -->
\label{prop:forgetful_from_calg_is_monoidal}
    Let $\mathsf{C}$ be an $\mathsf{I}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category. The forgetful functor
    \[
    {\mathsf{CAlg}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{C})\to\mathsf{C},
    \qquad F\mapsto F(*),
    \]
    lifts to a natural $\mathsf{I}$-monoidal functor
    \[
    \operatorname{Equip}^{\operatorname{cc}}({\mathsf{CAlg}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{C}))\to\mathsf{C}.
    \]
<!-- end proposition-38 -->
<!-- proof-56: body_md -->
This follows from \crtCref{prop:forgetful_from_calg_is_internally_representable}, together with the identification of the pointwise structure as cocartesian in \crtCref{prop:calg_has_E_colimits}.
<!-- end proof-56 -->
<!-- theorem-10: body_md -->
\label{thm:calg_is_right_adjoint}
    Let $\mathsf{I}$ be an inductible context-free subuniverse. There is an adjunction of $\mathcal{B}$-categories
    \[
    \operatorname{Equip}^{\operatorname{cc}}:\mathsf{Cat}^{\mathsf{I}\text{-}\sqcup}
    \leftrightarrows{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{Cat}):{\mathsf{CAlg}}^{\mathsf{I}},
    \]
    with $\operatorname{Equip}^{\operatorname{cc}}$ as the left adjoint.
<!-- end theorem-10 -->
<!-- proof-57: body_md -->
The unit is given by \crtCref{prop:canonical_Calg_structure_for_cocartesian_categories}, and the counit by \crtCref{prop:forgetful_from_calg_is_monoidal}. We verify the triangle identities.

    For an $\mathsf{I}$-cocomplete $\mathcal{B}$-category $\mathsf{C}$, the composite
    \[
    \operatorname{Equip}^{\operatorname{cc}}(\mathsf{C})
    \to\operatorname{Equip}^{\operatorname{cc}}({\mathsf{CAlg}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\operatorname{Equip}^{\operatorname{cc}}(\mathsf{C})))
    \to\operatorname{Equip}^{\operatorname{cc}}(\mathsf{C})
    \]
    first extends a functor $*\to\mathsf{C}$ cocontinuously to $\mathsf{I}$ and then evaluates at the point. It is therefore canonically equivalent to the identity.

    Now let $\mathsf{C}$ be an $\mathsf{I}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category. We must identify
    \[
    {\mathsf{CAlg}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{C})
    \to{\mathsf{CAlg}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\operatorname{Equip}^{\operatorname{cc}}({\mathsf{CAlg}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{C})))
    \to{\mathsf{CAlg}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{C})
    \]
    with the identity. Let $F:\mathsf{I}\to\mathsf{C}$ be an algebra in context $A$, with underlying object $F(*_A)$. The first arrow assigns to $F$ the $\mathsf{I}$-cocontinuous extension
    \[
    G:\mathsf{I}\to{\mathsf{CAlg}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{C})
    \]
    of the point selecting $F$, equipped with its induced monoidal structure. The second arrow postcomposes with the forgetful functor. It remains to identify the composite
    \[
    \mathsf{I}\xrightarrow{G}{\mathsf{CAlg}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{C})\to\mathsf{C}
    \]
    with $F$.

    For $[p:B\to A]\in\mathsf{I}(A)$, the value of $G$ is $p_\sharp p^*F$. Its underlying object is $p_\otimes p^*F(*_A)\simeq F([p:B\to A])$. On morphisms, $G$ is given by the corresponding counits. By their construction in \crtCref{prop:calg_has_E_colimits}, these are the multiplication morphisms of $F$. Thus the composite recovers $F$, naturally in $F$, proving the second triangle identity.
<!-- end proof-57 -->
<!-- remark-12: body_md -->
We expect this adjunction to exist for every full context-free subuniverse. We do not expect $\operatorname{Equip}^{\operatorname{cc}}$ to remain fully faithful in that generality, as it is in \crtCref{thm:uniqueness_of_cartesian_structures}.
<!-- end remark-12 -->
<!-- theorem-11: body_md -->
\label{thm:in_cocart_everything_is_alg}
    An $\mathsf{I}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category $\mathsf{C}$ is cocartesian if and only if the forgetful functor
    \[
    {\mathsf{CAlg}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{C})\to\mathsf{C},
    \qquad R\mapsto R(*),
    \]
    is an equivalence of $\mathcal{B}$-categories.
<!-- end theorem-11 -->
<!-- proof-58: body_md -->
This is the underlying functor of the counit in \crtCref{thm:calg_is_right_adjoint}. The left adjoint is fully faithful by \crtCref{thm:uniqueness_of_cartesian_structures}. Hence the counit is an equivalence precisely on its essential image, namely the cocartesian $\mathsf{I}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-categories.
<!-- end proof-58 -->
<!-- theorem-12: body_md -->
\label{thm:cocart_cats_are_localization_of_monoidal}
    Let $\mathsf{I}$ be an inductible context-free subuniverse. The fully faithful $\mathcal{B}$-functor
    \[
    \operatorname{Equip}^{\operatorname{cc}}:\mathsf{Cat}^{\mathsf{I}\text{-}\sqcup}
    \hookrightarrow{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{Cat})
    \]
    also admits a left adjoint $L_{\sqcup}$. Moreover, $\mathsf{Cat}^{\mathsf{I}\text{-}\sqcup}$ is $\mathcal{B}$-presentable.
<!-- end theorem-12 -->
<!-- proof-59: body_md -->
By \crtCref{thm:in_cocart_everything_is_alg,prop:forgetful_from_calg_is_internally_representable}, an $\mathsf{I}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category is cocartesian if and only if it is internally local with respect to the $\mathsf{I}$-monoidal inclusion $\mathsf{I}^{\simeq}\hookrightarrow\mathsf{I}$. By \crtCref{cor:cmon_is_tensored_and_powered_by_cat}, this is equivalent to locality with respect to the functors
    \[
    \mathsf{I}^{\simeq}\otimes\Delta^n
    \to\mathsf{I}\otimes\Delta^n,
    \qquad n\in\mathbb{N}.
    \]
    Since ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{Cat})$ is $\mathcal{B}$-presentable by \crtCref{prop:cmon_is_cat_module_in_prl}, these local objects form an accessible localization. This gives $L_{\sqcup}$ and the asserted presentability.
<!-- end proof-59 -->
<!-- corollary-9: body_md -->
\label{cor:Icocart_iff_forgetful_colocal}
    An $\mathsf{I}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category $\mathsf{C}$ is cocartesian if and only if, for every $\mathsf{I}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category $\mathsf{T}$, the canonical morphism
    \[
    {\mathsf{map}}(\mathsf{C},{\mathsf{CAlg}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{T}))
    \to{\mathsf{map}}(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{T})
    \]
    is an equivalence of $\mathcal{B}$-anima. Here the mapping objects are taken in ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{Cat})$, with the cocartesian structure on ${\mathsf{CAlg}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{T})$.
<!-- end corollary-9 -->
<!-- proof-60: body_md -->
If $\mathsf{C}$ is cocartesian, the equivalence is the adjunction of \crtCref{thm:calg_is_right_adjoint}.

    Conversely, the two adjunctions identify the mapping functor represented by $\mathsf{C}$ with that represented by $\operatorname{Equip}^{\operatorname{cc}}(L_{\sqcup}\mathsf{C})$. The internal Yoneda lemma gives $\mathsf{C}\simeq\operatorname{Equip}^{\operatorname{cc}}(L_{\sqcup}\mathsf{C})$, so $\mathsf{C}$ is cocartesian.
<!-- end proof-60 -->
<!-- definition-25: body_md -->
Let $\mathsf{C}$ be a $\mathcal{B}$-category. We write
    \[
    \mathsf{Cocart}_{\mathsf{C}}\hookrightarrow\mathsf{Cat}_{/\mathsf{C}}
    \]
    for the $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory whose objects are cocartesian fibrations over $\mathsf{C}$ and whose morphisms are functors over $\mathsf{C}$ that preserve cocartesian lifts.
<!-- end definition-25 -->
<!-- definition-26: body_md -->
\label{def:E_preoperads}
    The $\mathcal{B}$-category $\mathsf{preOp}$ of \emph{$\mathsf{E}$-preoperads} is the $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory of $\mathsf{Cat}_{/{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})}$ defined as follows. Its objects in context $A$ are functors of $\mathcal{B}_{/A}$-categories
    \[
    \mathsf{O}^{\otimes}\to\pi_A^*{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})
    \]
    admitting cocartesian lifts of left-pointing arrows. Its morphisms are functors over $\pi_A^*{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})$ that preserve these cocartesian lifts.
<!-- end definition-26 -->
<!-- warning-3: body_md -->
This condition is stronger than requiring the restriction
    \[
    \mathsf{O}^{\otimes}\times_{\pi_A^*{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})}
    \pi_A^*(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}})^{\mathrm{op}}
    \to\pi_A^*(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}})^{\mathrm{op}}
    \]
    to be a cocartesian fibration. A lift must be cocartesian over the entire span category, so its universal property must hold against all morphisms, including those that are not left-pointing.
<!-- end warning-3 -->
<!-- definition-27: body_md -->
Consider the composite
    \[
    (-)^\otimes:\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}({\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}),\mathsf{Cat})
    \xrightarrow{\sim}\mathsf{Cocart}_{{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})}\hookrightarrow\mathsf{preOp}.
    \]
    We call $F^\otimes$ the \emph{associated preoperad} of $F$. If $F$ defines an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category $\mathsf{C}$, we also write $\mathsf{C}^{\otimes}:=F^\otimes$.
<!-- end definition-27 -->
<!-- definition-28: body_md -->
\label{def:E_full_1}
    Let $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full},(1)}\subset(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}})^{\Delta^1}$ be the full $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory spanned by arrows in $\mathsf{E}$. Thus a morphism in $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full},(1)}(A)$ is a commutative square in $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}(A)$ of the form
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        C'\ar[r]\ar[d,tail]&B'\ar[d,tail]\\
        C\ar[r]&B,
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    where the tailed arrows lie in $\mathsf{E}$.

    Let $\mathsf{E}^{(1)}\subset\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full},(1)}$ be the wide $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory whose morphisms have the form
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        C'\ar[r]\ar[d,tail]&B'\ar[d,tail]\\
        C\ar[r,tail]&B,
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    again with the tailed arrows in $\mathsf{E}$. Finally, let $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full},(1)}_{\operatorname{cart}}$ be the wide $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory whose morphisms are cartesian squares.
<!-- end definition-28 -->
<!-- proposition-39: body_md -->
The triplet
    \[
    (\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full},(1)},\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full},(1)}_{\operatorname{cart}},\mathsf{E}^{(1)})
    \]
    is adequate. The target functor $t:\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full},(1)}\to\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$ defines a morphism of adequate triplets
    \[
    (\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full},(1)},\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full},(1)}_{\operatorname{cart}},\mathsf{E}^{(1)})
    \to(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}).
    \]
<!-- end proposition-39 -->
<!-- proof-61: body_md -->
We check that the required pullbacks exist and are preserved by change of context. Consider a morphism in $\mathsf{E}^{(1)}(A)$ and a morphism in $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full},(1)}_{\operatorname{cart}}(A)$ with the same target:
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        D'\ar[r]\ar[d,tail]&B'\ar[d,tail]\\
        D\ar[r,tail]&B
    \end{tikzcd}
    \qquad
    \begin{tikzcd}
        C'\ar[r]\ar[d,tail]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]&B'\ar[d,tail]\\
        C\ar[r]&B.
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    Their pullback is computed at the source and target. At the target, $C\times_B D$ exists because $D\to B$ lies in $\mathsf{E}$. At the source, the pullback exists by the identification
    \[
    C'\times_{B'}D'\simeq(C\times_B D)\times_D D',
    \]
    where we use $C'\simeq C\times_B B'$. The induced arrow
    \[
    C'\times_{B'}D'\to C\times_B D
    \]
    lies in $\mathsf{E}$ by base change. The resulting square over $D'\to D$ is cartesian, and the morphism to $C'\to C$ lies in $\mathsf{E}^{(1)}$ because $C\times_B D\to C$ lies in $\mathsf{E}$.

    These pullbacks are preserved by change of context, since pullbacks in $\mathsf{\Omega}$ are preserved by change of context. The same description shows that $t$ preserves the required pullbacks and the two distinguished classes of morphisms.
<!-- end proof-61 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
\label{lem:descript_of_E_tensor}
    There is a canonical equivalence
    \[
    {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full},(1)},\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full},(1)}_{\operatorname{cart}},\mathsf{E}^{(1)})
    \simeq(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}})^{\otimes}.
    \]
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- proof-62: body_md -->
The target functor $t:\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full},(1)}\to\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$ is a cartesian fibration: arrows in $\mathsf{E}$ admit pullbacks and are stable under base change in $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$. For $B\in\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}(A)$, its fibre is the full $\mathcal{B}_{/A}$-subcategory
    \[
    (\pi_A^*\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}})_{\mathsf{E}/B}
    \subset(\pi_A^*\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}})_{/B}
    \]
    spanned by objects whose structure morphism to $B$ lies in $\mathsf{E}$.

    Straightening identifies this fibre with $(\pi_A^*\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}})^B$. Thus $t$ classifies the $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-continuous functor
    \[
    (\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}})^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{Cat}
    \]
    determined by $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$. The $t$-cartesian arrows are precisely the morphisms in $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full},(1)}_{\operatorname{cart}}$. The displayed span category is therefore the unfurling defining $(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}})^\otimes$.
<!-- end proof-62 -->
<!-- corollary-10: body_md -->
\label{cor:description_of_the_env_of_triv}
    The triplet
    \[
    (\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full},(1)},\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full},(1)}_{\operatorname{cart}},\mathsf{E}^{\Delta^1})
    \]
    is adequate, and there is a canonical equivalence
    \[
    {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full},(1)},\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full},(1)}_{\operatorname{cart}},\mathsf{E}^{\Delta^1})
    \simeq\mathsf{E}^{\otimes}.
    \]
<!-- end corollary-10 -->
<!-- proposition-40: body_md -->
\label{prop:source_target_identity_adjunctions}
    The source and target functors
    \[
    s,t:\mathsf{E}^\otimes\to{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}),
    \]
    induced by $\delta_1,\delta_0:\Delta^0\to\Delta^1$, fit into adjunctions
    \[
    t\dashv r\dashv s,
    \]
    where $r:{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\to\mathsf{E}^\otimes$ is the fully faithful functor induced by $\sigma:\Delta^1\to\Delta^0$.
<!-- end proposition-40 -->
<!-- proof-63: body_md -->
For $t\dashv r$, the counit is the canonical equivalence $tr\simeq\mathrm{id}$. The unit $\mathrm{id}\to rt$ at an object $C\to B$ is represented by
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        C\ar[d,tail]&C\ar[l,equal]\ar[d,tail]\ar[r,tail]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center,pos=0.125,rotate=-90},draw=none,dl]&B\ar[d,equal]\\
        B&B\ar[r,equal]\ar[l,equal]&B.
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    This morphism is equivalent to the identity when $C\to B$ is an equivalence, and applying $t$ to it gives the identity. These are the two triangle identities.

    For $r\dashv s$, the unit is the canonical equivalence $\mathrm{id}\simeq sr$. The counit $rs\to\mathrm{id}$ at $C\to B$ is represented by
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        C\ar[d,equal]&C\ar[l,equal]\ar[d,equal]\ar[r,equal]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center,pos=0.125,rotate=-90},draw=none,dl]&C\ar[d,tail]\\
        C&C\ar[r,tail]\ar[l,equal]&B.
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    The triangle identities follow in the same way. Either adjunction shows that $r$ is fully faithful.
<!-- end proof-63 -->
<!-- definition-29: body_md -->
Let $\mathsf{O}^{\otimes}\to{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})$ be an $\mathsf{E}$-preoperad. Define $\mathsf{env}(\mathsf{O})^{\otimes}$ by the pullback
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        \mathsf{env}(\mathsf{O})^\otimes\ar[r]\ar[d]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        &\mathsf{O}^{\otimes}\ar[d]\\
        \mathsf{E}^{\otimes}\ar[r,"s"]\ar[d,"t"]
        &{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\\
        {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}).
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    We regard it as an object over ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})$ via the left vertical composite.
<!-- end definition-29 -->
<!-- proposition-41: body_md -->
The functor $\mathsf{env}(\mathsf{O})^{\otimes}\to{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})$ is a cocartesian fibration.
<!-- end proposition-41 -->
<!-- proof-64: body_md -->
We construct cocartesian lifts in every context and check that they are preserved by change of context. The construction is compatible with slicing, so we describe it in the global context.

    Let
    \[
    A\xleftarrow{x}F\xrightarrow{y}B
    \]
    be a morphism in ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})(*)$. An object of $\mathsf{env}(\mathsf{O})^{\otimes}(*)$ over $A$ consists of an object $O\in\mathsf{O}^{\otimes}(*)$ over $A'$ and an arrow $A'\to A$ in $\mathsf{E}(*)$. Its image in $\mathsf{E}^\otimes$ has the $t$-cocartesian lift
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        A'\ar[d]&F'\ar[l,"x'"']\ar[d]\ar[r,equal]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center,pos=0.125,rotate=-90},draw=none,dl]&F'\ar[d]\\
        A&F\ar[r,"y"]\ar[l,"x"]&B,
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    where $F'=A'\times_A F$. Applying $s$ gives a left-pointing arrow, which admits a cocartesian lift from $O$. Together these lifts give the required cocartesian lift in $\mathsf{env}(\mathsf{O})^{\otimes}$.

    Change of context preserves this construction, since it preserves the pullback defining $F'$ and the cocartesian lifts in the preoperad.
<!-- end proof-64 -->
<!-- definition-30: body_md -->
The \emph{envelope functor} is the composite
    \[
    \mathsf{env}:\mathsf{preOp}\to\mathsf{Cocart}_{{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})}
    \xrightarrow{\sim}\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}({\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}),\mathsf{Cat}),
    \]
    where the first functor sends $\mathsf{O}^{\otimes}$ to the cocartesian fibration $\mathsf{env}(\mathsf{O})^\otimes\to{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})$.
<!-- end definition-30 -->
<!-- proposition-42: body_md -->
There is a pullback square of $\mathcal{B}$-categories
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        \mathsf{env}(\mathsf{O})\ar[r]\ar[d]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]&\mathsf{O}^\otimes\ar[d]\\
        \mathsf{E}\ar[r]&{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}).
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
<!-- end proposition-42 -->
<!-- proof-65: body_md -->
In the diagram
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        \mathsf{env}(\mathsf{O})\ar[r]\ar[d]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        &\mathsf{env}(\mathsf{O})^\otimes\ar[r]\ar[d]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        &\mathsf{O}^\otimes\ar[d]\\
        \mathsf{E}\ar[r]\ar[d]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        &\mathsf{E}^\otimes\ar[r,"s"]\ar[d,"t"]
        &{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\\
        *\ar[r]&{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}),
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    all three squares are pullbacks. Pasting the two upper squares gives the claim.
<!-- end proof-65 -->
<!-- remark-13: body_md -->
Unless $\mathsf{E}=\left\{*\right\}$ is the context-free subuniverse of equivalences, $s$ is not a morphism of preoperads: it does not commute with the structure maps to ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})$. Indeed, ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})$ is the terminal preoperad, and the structure map of $\mathsf{E}^\otimes$ is $t$.

    In contrast, $r$ and $t$ are morphisms of preoperads. Once operads are defined below, they are also morphisms of $\mathsf{E}$-operads.
<!-- end remark-13 -->
<!-- proposition-43: body_md -->
\label{prop:eta_is_a_morphism_of_preoperads}
    Let $\mathsf{O}^\otimes\to{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})$ be an $\mathsf{E}$-preoperad. The identity $sr\simeq\mathrm{id}$ gives a pasting of pullbacks
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        \mathsf{O}^\otimes\ar[r,"\eta"]\ar[d]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        &\mathsf{env}(\mathsf{O})^\otimes\ar[r]\ar[d]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        &\mathsf{O}^\otimes\ar[d]\\
        {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\ar[r,"r"]
        &\mathsf{E}^\otimes\ar[r,"s"]
        &{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}).
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    The induced functor $\eta$ is a morphism of $\mathsf{E}$-preoperads.
<!-- end proposition-43 -->
<!-- proof-66: body_md -->
The functor $r$ preserves cocartesian lifts of left-pointing arrows. Its pullback $\eta$ therefore preserves these lifts as well.
<!-- end proof-66 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
\label{lem:right_adj_are_stable_under_BC}
    Let $p:\mathsf{X}\to\mathsf{D}$ be a cocartesian fibration of $\mathcal{B}$-categories, and let $R:\mathsf{C}\to\mathsf{D}$ admit a left adjoint $L\dashv R$. Then the pullback square
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        \mathsf{Y}\ar[r,"R'"]\ar[d,"q"']\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]&\mathsf{X}\ar[d,"p"]\\
        \mathsf{C}\ar[r,"R"]&\mathsf{D}
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    is horizontally left adjointable. Moreover, writing $L'\dashv R'$, the induced commutative square
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        \mathsf{Y}\ar[d,"q"']&\mathsf{X}\ar[d,"p"]\ar[l,"L'"]\\
        \mathsf{C}&\mathsf{D}\ar[l,"L"]
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    is a morphism of cocartesian fibrations.
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- proof-67: body_md -->
For $\infty$-categories, the statement is \cite[Lemma 2.13]{glossner2025modelindependentuniversalproperty}. Its proof constructs the adjunction using cocartesian lifts of the unit and counit and verifies the triangle identities. The construction applies in every context and is preserved by change of context, since change-of-context functors preserve cocartesian lifts. It therefore gives the internal adjunction and the asserted adjointability. Preservation of cocartesian lifts by $L'$ can likewise be checked in every context.
<!-- end proof-67 -->
<!-- proposition-44: body_md -->
\label{prop:preoperad_premonoidal_adjunction}
    The natural transformations $\eta$ and $\epsilon$ defined above are the unit and counit of an adjunction
    \[
    \mathsf{env}:\mathsf{preOp}
    \leftrightarrows\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}({\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}),\mathsf{Cat}):(-)^\otimes.
    \]
<!-- end proposition-44 -->
<!-- proof-68: body_md -->
Since $r$ is fully faithful, its pullback $\eta_{F^\otimes}$ is fully faithful. The counit of $\epsilon_F^\otimes\dashv\eta_{F^\otimes}$ is therefore an equivalence
    \[
    \epsilon_F^\otimes\eta_{F^\otimes}\simeq\mathrm{id}_{F^\otimes}.
    \]
    This proves the first triangle identity.

    For the second, let $\mathsf{O}^\otimes$ be an $\mathsf{E}$-preoperad. We must show that the composite
    \[
    \mathsf{env}(\mathsf{O})
    \xrightarrow{\mathsf{env}(\eta)}\mathsf{env}(\mathsf{env}(\mathsf{O})^\otimes)
    \xrightarrow{\epsilon_{\mathsf{env}(\mathsf{O})}}\mathsf{env}(\mathsf{O})
    \]
    is equivalent to the identity. It suffices to check this after unstraightening, for the composite
    \[
    \mathsf{env}(\mathsf{O})^\otimes
    \xrightarrow{\mathsf{env}(\eta)^\otimes}\mathsf{env}(\mathsf{env}(\mathsf{O})^\otimes)^\otimes
    \xrightarrow{\epsilon_{\mathsf{env}(\mathsf{O})}^\otimes}\mathsf{env}(\mathsf{O})^\otimes.
    \]

    Consider the pasting
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        \mathsf{env}(\mathsf{O})^\otimes\ar[r,"q"]\ar[d]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        &\mathsf{O}^\otimes\ar[r,"\eta_{\mathsf{O}}"]\ar[d]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        &\mathsf{env}(\mathsf{O})^\otimes\ar[d]\\
        \mathsf{E}^\otimes\ar[r,"s"]
        &{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\ar[r,"r"]
        &\mathsf{E}^\otimes.
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    Lifting the counit $rs\to\mathrm{id}$ gives a natural transformation
    \[
    \eta_{\mathsf{O}}q\to\mathrm{id}
    \]
    whose components are cocartesian. We will construct a second such transformation
    \[
    \eta_{\mathsf{O}}q
    \to\epsilon_{\mathsf{env}(\mathsf{O})}^\otimes\mathsf{env}(\eta)^\otimes
    \]
    over the same counit. Uniqueness of cocartesian lifts will then identify the composite with the identity.

    In the commutative diagram
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        \mathsf{env}(\mathsf{env}(\mathsf{O})^\otimes)^\otimes\ar[r,"\epsilon_{\mathsf{env}(\mathsf{O})}^\otimes"]\ar[d]
        &\mathsf{env}(\mathsf{O})^\otimes\ar[r,"\eta_{\mathsf{env}(\mathsf{O})^\otimes}"]\ar[d]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        &\mathsf{env}(\mathsf{env}(\mathsf{O})^\otimes)^\otimes\ar[r,"p"]\ar[d]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        &\mathsf{env}(\mathsf{O})^\otimes\ar[d]\\
        \mathsf{E}^\otimes\ar[r,"t"]
        &{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\ar[r,"r"]
        &\mathsf{E}^\otimes\ar[r,"s"]
        &{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}),
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    the middle and right squares are pullbacks; the left square need not be. The middle upper arrow is the unit at the preoperad $\mathsf{env}(\mathsf{O})^\otimes$, rather than $\mathsf{env}(\eta)^\otimes$.

    By construction, the unit
    \[
    \mathrm{id}\to
    \eta_{\mathsf{env}(\mathsf{O})^\otimes}\epsilon_{\mathsf{env}(\mathsf{O})}^\otimes
    \]
    is a cocartesian lift of $\mathrm{id}\to rt$. Postcomposing with $p$ gives a natural transformation
    \[
    p\to\epsilon_{\mathsf{env}(\mathsf{O})}^\otimes
    \]
    over $s\to t$. Precomposing with $\mathsf{env}(\eta)^\otimes$ then gives a transformation with cocartesian components
    \[
    p\mathsf{env}(\eta)^\otimes
    \to\epsilon_{\mathsf{env}(\mathsf{O})}^\otimes\mathsf{env}(\eta)^\otimes.
    \]
    Finally, the upper square in
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        \mathsf{env}(\mathsf{O})^\otimes\ar[r,"q"]\ar[d,"\mathsf{env}(\eta)^\otimes"']\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        &\mathsf{O}^\otimes\ar[d,"\eta_{\mathsf{O}}"]\\
        \mathsf{env}(\mathsf{env}(\mathsf{O})^\otimes)^\otimes\ar[d]\ar[r,"p"]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        &\mathsf{env}(\mathsf{O})^\otimes\ar[d]\\
        \mathsf{E}^\otimes\ar[r,"s"]
        &{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    identifies $p\mathsf{env}(\eta)^\otimes$ with $\eta_{\mathsf{O}}q$. Thus we have the required second cocartesian lift, proving the triangle identity.
<!-- end proof-68 -->
<!-- definition-31: body_md -->
\label{def:E_operads}
    An $\mathsf{E}$-preoperad is an \emph{$\mathsf{E}$-operad} if its envelope is an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal category. Thus the $\mathcal{B}$-category of $\mathsf{E}$-operads is defined by the pullback
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        \mathsf{Op}\ar[r]\ar[d]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        &\mathsf{preOp}\ar[d,"\mathsf{env}"]\\
        {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})\ar[r,hook]
        &\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}({\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}),\mathsf{Cat}).
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
<!-- end definition-31 -->
<!-- example-6: body_md -->
\label{ex:classical_E_operads}
    Let $\mathcal{B}=\mathrm{Ani}$, and let $\mathsf{E}$ be the context-free subuniverse corresponding to finite covering maps of anima. Then an $\mathsf{E}$-operad in the global context is the same as an $\infty$-operad in the sense of \cite[Definition 2.1.1.10]{HA}.
<!-- end example-6 -->
<!-- proof-69: body_md -->
By \cite[Corollary 5.1.15]{barkan2022envelopes}, $\infty$-operads in the sense of \cite[Definition 2.1.1.10]{HA} are equivalent to functors
    \[
    p:\mathcal{O}^\otimes\to\mathrm{Span}(\mathrm{Fin})
    \]
    satisfying the following conditions:
    \begin{mylist}
        \item The functor $p$ admits cocartesian lifts of inert, that is, left-pointing, morphisms.
        \item For every finite set $A$, the square
        \[
        \begin{tikzcd}
            \mathcal{O}^\otimes\times_{\mathrm{Span}(\mathrm{Fin})}\mathrm{Fin}_{/A}\ar[r]\ar[d]
            &(\mathcal{O}^\otimes\times_{\mathrm{Span}(\mathrm{Fin})}\mathrm{Fin})^A\ar[d]\\
            \mathrm{Fin}_{/A}\ar[r]&\mathrm{Fin}^A
        \end{tikzcd}
        \]
        is a pullback.
    \end{mylist}
    The lower arrow is an equivalence, so the second condition is equivalent to requiring the upper arrow to be an equivalence. This upper arrow is the comparison map for preservation of finite products by the functor classified by
    \[
    \operatorname{env}(\mathcal{O})^\otimes\to\mathrm{Span}(\mathrm{Fin}).
    \]
    Thus a preoperad is an $\infty$-operad precisely when its envelope preserves finite products, as required.
<!-- end proof-69 -->
<!-- warning-4: body_md -->
For a general topos $\mathcal{B}$, an object $[p:B\to A]\in\mathsf{E}(A)$ need not admit a section in context $A$. Sections after change of context play the role of the maps $l_b$ above.

    Nevertheless, a functor $F:{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\to\mathsf{Cat}$ has canonical comparison maps of $\mathcal{B}_{/A}$-categories
    \[
    F(B)\to F(A)^B,
    \]
    where $A$ denotes the terminal object in context $A$. By definition, $F$ is an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal category if and only if these comparison maps are equivalences in every context.
<!-- end warning-4 -->
<!-- notation-4: body_md -->
For $[B\to A]\in{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})(A)$, let $B^{A\triangleleft}$ be the $\mathcal{B}_{/A}$-category defined by the pushout
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        B\sqcup B\ar[r]\ar[d]&B\times\Delta^1\ar[d]\\
        A\sqcup B\ar[r]&B^{A\triangleleft}\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center,pos=0.125,rotate=180},draw=none,from=2-2,to=1-1].
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    Here the upper arrow includes the two endpoints, and the left arrow is the structure map on the first summand and the identity on the second. The projection $B\times\Delta^1\to\Delta^1$ induces a projection $B^{A\triangleleft}\to\Delta^1$, sending $A$ to the source and $B$ to the target.
<!-- end notation-4 -->
<!-- remark-14: body_md -->
This is the left cone $B^{\triangleleft}$ formed in $\mathcal{B}_{/A}$, as in \cite[Remark 4.1.4]{MWcocomplete}. We include $A$ in the notation to make the context explicit.
<!-- end remark-14 -->
<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
\label{lem:limit_cone_cocartesian_fib_critirion}
    Let
    \[
    \mathsf{Y}\xrightarrow{p}\mathsf{X}\xrightarrow{q}\mathsf{I}^{\triangleleft}
    \]
    be cocartesian fibrations of $\mathcal{B}$-categories, and write $\mathsf{sec}(q)$ for the $\mathcal{B}$-category of cocartesian sections of $q$.
    \begin{mylist}
        \item The functor $q$ classifies a limit cone if and only if the restriction functor
        \[
        \mathsf{sec}(q)\to\mathsf{sec}(q|_{\mathsf{I}})
        \]
        is an equivalence.
        \item Suppose that $q$ classifies a limit cone. Then $qp$ classifies a limit cone if and only if, for every object $\sigma:A\to\mathsf{sec}(q)$, the pullback $\sigma^*p$ in the diagram
        \[
        \begin{tikzcd}
            \sigma^*\mathsf{Y}\ar[r]\ar[d,"\sigma^*p"]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
            &\pi_A^*\mathsf{Y}\ar[d]\\
            \pi_A^*\mathsf{I}^{\triangleleft}\ar[dr,equal]\ar[r,"\sigma"]
            &\pi_A^*\mathsf{X}\ar[d]\\
            &\pi_A^*\mathsf{I}^{\triangleleft}
        \end{tikzcd}
        \]
        classifies a limit cone of $\mathcal{B}_{/A}$-categories.
    \end{mylist}
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- proof-70: body_md -->
For (a), \cite[Proposition 7.1.2]{MInternalStraightenning} identifies cocartesian sections with the limit of the classified functor. Since $\mathsf{I}^{\triangleleft}$ has an initial object, $\mathsf{sec}(q)$ identifies with the value at the cone point, while $\mathsf{sec}(q|_{\mathsf{I}})$ identifies with the limit over $\mathsf{I}$. The restriction functor is the comparison map between them, proving (a).

    For (b), consider the commutative square
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        \mathsf{sec}(qp)\ar[r]\ar[d]
        &\mathsf{sec}((qp)|_{\mathsf{I}})\ar[d]\\
        \mathsf{sec}(q)\ar[r]
        &\mathsf{sec}(q|_{\mathsf{I}}).
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    By (a), the lower arrow is an equivalence, and the upper arrow is an equivalence precisely when $qp$ classifies a limit cone. The vertical functors are cocartesian fibrations. It therefore suffices to check that the upper arrow induces an equivalence on the fibres over every object $\sigma:A\to\mathsf{sec}(q)$. The induced functor on these fibres is
    \[
    \mathsf{sec}(\sigma^*p)
    \to\mathsf{sec}((\sigma^*p)|_{\pi_A^*\mathsf{I}}),
    \]
    which is an equivalence precisely when $\sigma^*p$ classifies a limit cone, again by (a).
<!-- end proof-70 -->
<!-- definition-32: body_md -->
Let $[B\to A]\in{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})(A)$. Define a functor of $\mathcal{B}_{/A}$-categories
    \[
    T:B\to\bigl(\pi_A^*(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}})^{\mathrm{op}}\bigr)^{\Delta^1}
    \hookrightarrow(\pi_A^*{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}))^{\Delta^1}
    \]
    as follows. In context $[C\to A]$, a map $C\to B$ over $A$ determines a section $C\to C\times_A B$. We send it to the left-pointing span
    \[
    C\times_A B\leftarrow C=C.
    \]
    The source and target of $T$ are the constant diagrams on $[B\to A]$ and $[A=A]$, respectively. Since the corresponding functor $B\times\Delta^1\to\pi_A^*{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})$ is constant on the source, it factors through a cone
    \[
    B\times\Delta^1\to B^{A\triangleleft}
    \xrightarrow{c_B}\pi_A^*{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}).
    \]
<!-- end definition-32 -->
<!-- proposition-45: body_md -->
\label{prop:canonical_span_limit_cones}
    The cones $c_B:B^{A\triangleleft}\to\pi_A^*{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})$ are limit cones.
<!-- end proposition-45 -->
<!-- proof-71: body_md -->
By \crtCref{prop:limits_in_span_E_are_computed_in_E_op}, $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-limits in ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})$ are computed in $(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}})^{\mathrm{op}}$. It therefore suffices to check the dual statement in $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$.

    The constant diagram $B\to\pi_A^*\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$ on the terminal object $A$ has colimit $B$. In context $C$, its cocone sends a map $C\to B$ over $A$ to the corresponding section $C\to C\times_A B$. These are precisely the arrows defining $c_B$.
<!-- end proof-71 -->
<!-- proposition-46: body_md -->
\label{prop:otimes_sends_monoidal_to_operads}
    The functor
    \[
    (-)^\otimes:\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}({\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}),\mathsf{Cat})\to\mathsf{preOp}
    \]
    sends $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal categories to $\mathsf{E}$-operads.
<!-- end proposition-46 -->
<!-- proof-72: body_md -->
Let $F:{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\to\mathsf{Cat}$ define an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal category. We must show that $\mathsf{env}(F^\otimes)$ is $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-continuous. Consider the defining diagram
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        \mathsf{env}(F^\otimes)^\otimes\ar[r]\ar[d,"p"]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        &F^\otimes\ar[d,"q"]\\
        \mathsf{E}^\otimes\ar[r,"s"]\ar[d,"t"]
        &{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\\
        {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}).
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    It suffices to show that, for every context $A$ and every $[B\to A]\in\mathsf{E}(A)$, the pullback $c_B^*(tp)$ classifies a limit cone.

    The functor $t$ classifies an $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-continuous functor, so $c_B^*t$ already classifies a limit cone. By \crtCref{lem:limit_cone_cocartesian_fib_critirion}(b), it remains to show that $\sigma^*p$ classifies a limit cone for every $\pi:A'\to A$ and every $t$-cocartesian section
    \[
    \sigma:\pi^*B^{A\triangleleft}\to\pi_{A'}^*\mathsf{E}^\otimes
    \]
    over $\pi^*c_B$. Since
    \[
    \sigma^*p\simeq(s\sigma)^*q
    \]
    and $q$ classifies the $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-continuous functor $F$, it is enough to show that $s\sigma$ is an indexed limit cone in ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})$.

    After changing context from $A$ to $A'$, we may assume $A'=A$. By \crtCref{lem:limit_cone_cocartesian_fib_critirion}(a), the section $\sigma$ is determined by its value at the cone point. This value is an arrow $B'\to B$ in $\mathsf{E}(A)$. For a map $C\to B$ over $A$, cocartesianness determines the corresponding arrow of $\sigma$ as
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        C\times_A B'\ar[d]
        &P\ar[d]\ar[r,equal]\ar[l]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center,pos=0.125,rotate=-90},draw=none,from=1-2,to=2-1]
        &P\ar[d]\\
        C\times_A B
        &C\ar[l]\ar[r,equal]
        &C,
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    where $P=C\times_B B'$. Applying $s$ gives the cone whose dual cocone in $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$ exhibits $B'$ as the colimit of its fibres over $B$. Thus $s\sigma$ is a limit cone by the same argument as in \crtCref{prop:canonical_span_limit_cones}. This proves the required continuity.
<!-- end proof-72 -->
<!-- theorem-13: body_md -->
\label{thm:env_associated_operad_adjunction}
    The natural transformations $\eta$ and $\epsilon$ defined above are the unit and counit of an adjunction
    \[
    \mathsf{env}:\mathsf{Op}
    \leftrightarrows{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat}):(-)^\otimes.
    \]
<!-- end theorem-13 -->
<!-- proof-73: body_md -->
Both $\mathsf{Op}\subset\mathsf{preOp}$ and
    \[
    {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})\subset\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}({\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}),\mathsf{Cat})
    \]
    are full $\mathcal{B}$-subcategories. By definition, $\mathsf{env}$ sends operads to $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal categories. Conversely, \crtCref{prop:otimes_sends_monoidal_to_operads} shows that $(-)^\otimes$ sends $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal categories to operads. The adjunction of \crtCref{prop:preoperad_premonoidal_adjunction} therefore restricts as claimed.
<!-- end proof-73 -->
<!-- definition-33: body_md -->
\label{def:lax_E_monoidal_functors}
    Let $\mathsf{C}$ and $\mathsf{D}$ be $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-categories. A \emph{lax $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functor} $\mathsf{C}\to\mathsf{D}$ is a morphism of $\mathsf{E}$-operads
    \[
    \mathsf{C}^\otimes\to\mathsf{D}^\otimes.
    \]
<!-- end definition-33 -->
<!-- proposition-47: body_md -->
\label{prop:forgetting_E_to_I_monoidal_in_prr}
    The forgetful $\mathcal{B}$-functor
    \[
    {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})\to{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{Q}}(\mathsf{Cat})
    \]
    is accessible, conservative, and continuous. It admits a left adjoint.
<!-- end proposition-47 -->
<!-- proof-74: body_md -->
Restriction commutes with the forgetful functors to $\mathsf{Cat}$. These functors are accessible, conservative, and continuous, so the same properties hold for restriction. For accessibility, choose a $\mathcal{B}$-regular cardinal $\kappa$ such that both forgetful functors preserve $\kappa$-filtered colimits; conservativity then detects preservation of these colimits by restriction. The same argument applies to limits.

    Both categories are $\mathcal{B}$-presentable by \crtCref{prop:cmon_is_cat_module_in_prl}. The internal adjoint functor theorem \cite[Proposition 2.4.3.3]{MWPresentabilityAndTopoi} therefore gives the left adjoint.
<!-- end proof-74 -->
<!-- definition-34: body_md -->
Let $\mathsf{I}\subset\mathsf{E}$ be context-free subuniverses, with $\mathsf{I}$ inductible. An $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category $\mathsf{C}$ is \emph{$\mathsf{I}$-cartesian}, respectively \emph{$\mathsf{I}$-cocartesian}, if its image under
    \[
    {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})\to{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{Cat})
    \]
    is cartesian, respectively cocartesian. We write
    \[
    {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E},\mathsf{I}\text{-}\sqcap}(\mathsf{Cat})
    \quad\text{and}\quad
    {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E},\mathsf{I}\text{-}\sqcup}(\mathsf{Cat})
    \]
    for the corresponding full $\mathcal{B}$-subcategories of ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})$.
<!-- end definition-34 -->
<!-- proposition-48: body_md -->
\label{prop:pushout_in_prl_defining_E_mon_I_cocart}
    There is a pushout square in ${\mathsf{Pr^L}}$
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{Cat})\ar[r]\ar[d]
        &\mathsf{Cat}^{\mathsf{I}\text{-}\sqcup}\ar[d]\\
        {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})\ar[r]
        &{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E},\mathsf{I}\text{-}\sqcup}(\mathsf{Cat})
        \arrow[ul,"\lrcorner"{anchor=center,pos=0.125,rotate=180},draw=none].
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    The horizontal functors are Bousfield localizations. The left vertical functor is the left adjoint to restriction.
<!-- end proposition-48 -->
<!-- proof-75: body_md -->
By definition, the full $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory of $\mathsf{I}$-cocartesian $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal categories is the pullback of
    \[
    \operatorname{Equip}^{\operatorname{cc}}:\mathsf{Cat}^{\mathsf{I}\text{-}\sqcup}
    \hookrightarrow{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{Cat})
    \]
    along restriction. By \crtCref{prop:forgetting_E_to_I_monoidal_in_prr,thm:cocart_cats_are_localization_of_monoidal}, these are accessible right adjoints. Passing to left adjoints gives the displayed pushout. The horizontal right adjoints are fully faithful, so the horizontal left adjoints are Bousfield localizations.
<!-- end proof-75 -->
<!-- definition-35: body_md -->
\label{def:P_I_ambi_E_monoidal_cats}
    Let $\mathsf{I},\mathsf{P}\subset\mathsf{E}$ be inductible context-free subuniverses of a context-free subuniverse $\mathsf{E}$. An $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category is \emph{$(\mathsf{P,I})$-ambidextrous} if it is $\mathsf{P}$-cartesian and $\mathsf{I}$-cocartesian. We write
    \[
    {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E},(\mathsf{P,I})\text{-}\oplus}(\mathsf{Cat})
    \]
    for the full $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory of ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})$ spanned by these categories.
<!-- end definition-35 -->
<!-- proposition-49: body_md -->
\label{prop:localization_to_partial_ambidexterity}
    There is a Bousfield localization
    \[
    L_{\oplus}:{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})
    \twoheadrightarrow{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E},(\mathsf{P,I})\text{-}\oplus}(\mathsf{Cat}).
    \]
<!-- end proposition-49 -->
<!-- proof-76: body_md -->
By \crtCref{prop:pushout_in_prl_defining_E_mon_I_cocart} and its cartesian analogue obtained by taking opposites, there are Bousfield localizations onto
    \[
    {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E},\mathsf{I}\text{-}\sqcup}(\mathsf{Cat})
    \quad\text{and}\quad
    {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E},\mathsf{P}\text{-}\sqcap}(\mathsf{Cat}).
    \]
    The pullback of their fully faithful right adjoints is the full $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory of $(\mathsf{P,I})$-ambidextrous categories. Passing to left adjoints identifies this category with the pushout of the two localizations in ${\mathsf{Pr^L}}$ and gives $L_{\oplus}$.
<!-- end proof-76 -->
<!-- example-7: body_md -->
\label{cor:existance_of_free_ambi_monoidal_category}
    For $A\in\mathcal{B}$, the $(\mathsf{P,I})$-ambidextrous category $L_{\oplus}\mathsf{E}^{\simeq}[A]$ internally represents the composite
    \[
    \begin{aligned}
    \Phi:{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E},(\mathsf{P,I})\text{-}\oplus}(\mathsf{Cat})
    &\hookrightarrow{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})\\
    &\to\mathsf{Cat}\xrightarrow{{\mathsf{map}}(A,-)}\mathsf{\Omega}.
    \end{aligned}
    \]
    This follows from the adjunction defining $L_{\oplus}$ and the universal property in \crtCref{example:free_E_monoidal_cat}.
<!-- end example-7 -->
<!-- remark-15: body_md -->
The following are special cases of the preceding construction. In the last two cases, assume that $\mathsf{E}$ is inductible.
    \begin{mylist}
        \item If $\mathsf{I}=\mathsf{P}=\left\{*\right\}$ is the context-free subuniverse of equivalences, then
