        \[
        L_{\oplus}\mathsf{E}^{\simeq}\simeq\mathsf{E}^{\simeq}.
        \]
        \item If $\mathsf{I}=\mathsf{E}$ and $\mathsf{P}=\left\{*\right\}$, then
        \[
        L_{\oplus}\mathsf{E}^{\simeq}\simeq\mathsf{E}.
        \]
        This follows from the free cocompletion property in \crtCref{prop:S_is_free_with_S_colmitis} and the full faithfulness of the cocartesian construction in \crtCref{thm:uniqueness_of_cartesian_structures}.
        \item If $\mathsf{I}=\mathsf{P}=\mathsf{E}$, then
        \[
        L_{\oplus}\mathsf{E}^{\simeq}\simeq{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}).
        \]
        Its universal property among $\mathsf{E}$-ambidextrous $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal categories is established in \cite{CLLambi}.
    \end{mylist}
<!-- end remark-15 -->
<!-- definition-36: body_md -->
An $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category $\mathsf{C}$ is \emph{inductively $(\mathsf{P,I})$-ambidextrous} if the inductive norm constructions of \crtCref{def:cartesian_S_monoidal_category} and its dual are defined and give natural equivalences
    \[
    s_\sharp\xrightarrow{\sim}s_\otimes
    \quad\text{for }s\in\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}},
    \qquad
    s_\otimes\xrightarrow{\sim}s_*
    \quad\text{for }s\in\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},
    \]
    in every context.
<!-- end definition-36 -->
<!-- proposition-50: body_md -->
\label{prop:inductive_amby_iff_ambi}
    An $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category is inductively $(\mathsf{P,I})$-ambidextrous if and only if it is $(\mathsf{P,I})$-ambidextrous.
<!-- end proposition-50 -->
<!-- proof-77: body_md -->
If the category is inductively $(\mathsf{P,I})$-ambidextrous, restricting the norm conditions to $\mathsf{I}$ and $\mathsf{P}$ shows that the induced structures are cocartesian and cartesian, respectively.

    Conversely, the norm constructions and the condition that they be equivalences are independent of context. A morphism in $\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}}$, respectively $\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}}$, can be regarded in the context of its target as an object of $\mathsf{I}$, respectively $\mathsf{P}$. The required norm equivalences therefore follow from the cocartesian and cartesian structures on the restrictions.
<!-- end proof-77 -->
<!-- corollary-11: body_md -->
\label{cor:critiria_for_amby}
    An $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category $\mathsf{C}$ is $(\mathsf{P,I})$-ambidextrous if and only if the following conditions hold in every context $A$:
    \begin{mylist}
        \item For every $p:C\to B$ in $\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}}(A)$, the functor
        \[
        p_\otimes:\mathsf{C}^{C}\to\mathsf{C}^{B}
        \]
        is $\mathsf{I}$-cocontinuous.
        \item For every $p:C\to B$ in $\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}}(A)$, the functor
        \[
        p_\otimes:\mathsf{C}^{C}\to\mathsf{C}^{B}
        \]
        is $\mathsf{P}$-continuous.
    \end{mylist}
<!-- end corollary-11 -->
<!-- proof-78: body_md -->
This follows from \crtCref{prop:inductive_amby_iff_ambi,prop:C_is_cartesian_iff_tensor_preserves_limits}.
<!-- end proof-78 -->
<!-- proposition-51: body_md -->
The $\mathcal{B}$-category ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})$ carries a canonical symmetric monoidal structure induced by products in $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$.
<!-- end proposition-51 -->
<!-- proof-79: body_md -->
Observe that in every context $A\in\mathcal{B}$, the $\infty$-category $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}(A)$ admits finite products since morphisms in $\mathsf{E}$ are stable under base change in $\mathcal{B}$. Moreover, for $p:B\to A$, the functor $p^*:\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}(A)\to\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}(B)$ preserves finite products.

    Thus, by \cite[Theorem 1.2(iv)]{Haugseng_2017}, the functor ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}):\mathcal{B}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Cat}$ lifts canonically to a limit-preserving functor ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}):\mathcal{B}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{CMon}(\mathrm{Cat})$. In every context $A\in\mathcal{B}$, the symmetric monoidal structure can be described on objects in ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})(A)$ by binary products in $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}(A)$.
<!-- end proof-79 -->
<!-- corollary-12: body_md -->
The $\mathcal{B}$-category $\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}({\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}),\mathsf{\Omega})$ carries a symmetric monoidal structure such that the Yoneda embedding
    \[
    {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})^{\mathrm{op}}\hookrightarrow\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}({\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}),\mathsf{\Omega})
    \]
    is symmetric monoidal.
<!-- end corollary-12 -->
<!-- proof-80: body_md -->
As explained above, this follows from \cite[Remark 2.6.2.6]{MWPresentabilityAndTopoi}.
<!-- end proof-80 -->
<!-- corollary-13: body_md -->
\label{cor:E_cmon_is_symmetric_monoidal}
    The $\mathcal{B}$-category ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}$ carries a symmetric monoidal structure such that the localization
    \[
    \underline{\mathsf{Fun}}({\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}),\mathsf{\Omega})\twoheadrightarrow{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}
    \]
    is symmetric monoidal.
<!-- end corollary-13 -->
<!-- proof-81: body_md -->
The proof of \cite[Lemma 4.23]{Ben_Moshe_ambi_K} carries over unchanged to the internal setting and can be checked in every context.
<!-- end proof-81 -->
<!-- corollary-14: body_md -->
\label{cor:E_monoidal_cats_are_symmetric_monoidal}
    The $\mathcal{B}$-category ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})$ carries a symmetric monoidal structure such that the inclusion
    \[
    {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}\hookrightarrow{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})
    \]
    is a morphism of commutative algebras in ${\mathsf{Pr^L}}$.
<!-- end corollary-14 -->
<!-- proof-82: body_md -->
Recall that we showed in the proof of \crtCref{prop:cmon_is_cat_module_in_prl} that
    \[
    {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})\simeq{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}\otimes\mathsf{Cat},
    \]
    with respect to the multilinear tensor product. The inclusion is identified with the tensor product of the unit $\mathsf{\Omega}\hookrightarrow\mathsf{Cat}$ with ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}$.
<!-- end proof-82 -->
<!-- notation-5: body_md -->
Diverging from Ben-Moshe's notation, we will denote the tensor product in ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})$ by $\otimes$. If we have several context-free subuniverses, then we might denote the different tensor products by $\otimes^{\mathsf{E}}$.

    We also have an internal Hom functor, which we denote by $\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\otimes}$ or $\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{E}-\otimes}$.
<!-- end notation-5 -->
<!-- remark-16: body_md -->
Note that if $\mathsf{E}$ is inductible, then $\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{E}-\otimes}$ agrees with the self-enrichment described in \crtCref{cor:cmon_is_self_enriched_if_inductible}, as both of them lift the $\mathsf{Cat}$-enrichment coming from the $\mathsf{Cat}$-module structure.
<!-- end remark-16 -->
<!-- proposition-52: body_md -->
\label{prop:I_cocart_loc_is_sym_monoidal}
    The $\mathcal{B}$-category ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E},\mathsf{I}-\sqcup}(\mathsf{Cat})$ carries a symmetric monoidal structure such that the localization
    \[
    L_{\mathsf{I}-\sqcup}:{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})\twoheadrightarrow{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E},\mathsf{I}-\sqcup}(\mathsf{Cat})
    \]
    is a morphism of commutative algebras in ${\mathsf{Pr^L}}$.
<!-- end proposition-52 -->
<!-- proof-83: body_md -->
By the same argument as in \cite[Lemma 4.20]{Ben_Moshe_ambi_K}, it is enough to show that a morphism $F:\mathsf{C}\to\mathsf{D}$ is an $L_{\mathsf{I}-\sqcup}$-equivalence if and only if, for any $\mathsf{I}$-cocartesian $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category $\mathsf{T}$, the morphism
    \[
    \underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{E}-\otimes}(\mathsf{D},\mathsf{T})\to\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{E}-\otimes}(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{T})
    \]
    is an equivalence.

    Note that since the forgetful functor ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})\to\mathsf{Cat}\hookrightarrow\mathsf{\Omega}_{\Delta}$ is conservative, a $\mathcal{B}$-category $\mathsf{T}$ is internally local with respect to $F:\mathsf{C}\to\mathsf{D}$ if and only if, for every $n$, $\mathsf{T}^{\Delta^n}$ is local with respect to $F:\mathsf{C}\to\mathsf{D}$.

    Thus, the result follows by observing that an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category $\mathsf{T}$ is $\mathsf{I}$-cocartesian if and only if $\mathsf{T}^{\Delta^n}$ is $\mathsf{I}$-cocartesian for every $n$.
<!-- end proof-83 -->
<!-- proposition-53: body_md -->
\label{prop:rel_free_is_sym_mon}
    Let $\mathsf{I}\subset\mathsf{E}$ be an inductible context-free subuniverse. Then the functor
    \[
    F_{\mathsf{I}}^{\mathsf{E}}:{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{Cat})\to{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat}),
    \]
    which is left adjoint to the forgetful functor $U^{\mathsf{E}}_{\mathsf{I}}:{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})\to{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{Cat})$, can be promoted to a morphism of commutative algebras in ${\mathsf{Pr^L}}$.
<!-- end proposition-53 -->
<!-- proof-84: body_md -->
The functor ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{I}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{I})\hookrightarrow{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})$ is symmetric monoidal since the inclusion $\mathsf{I}\hookrightarrow\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$ preserves products. Thus, we get that ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}\to{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}$ is a morphism of commutative algebras in ${\mathsf{Pr^L}}$.

    The morphism $F_{\mathsf{I}}^{\mathsf{E}}:{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{Cat})\to{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})$ is obtained by tensoring ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}\to{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}$ with $\mathsf{Cat}$.
<!-- end proof-84 -->
<!-- proposition-54: body_md -->
\label{prop:pushout_in_prl_I_cocart}
    The following is a pushout in ${\mathsf{CAlg}}({\mathsf{Pr^L}})$:
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{Cat})\ar[d]\ar[r]
        &\mathsf{Cat}^{\mathsf{I}-\sqcup}\ar[d]\\
        {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})\ar[r]
        &{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E},\mathsf{I}-\sqcup}(\mathsf{Cat}).
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
<!-- end proposition-54 -->
<!-- proof-85: body_md -->
Note that the horizontal morphisms are monoidal Bousfield localizations. Hence, to show that the square is a pushout in ${\mathsf{CAlg}}({\mathsf{Pr^L}})$, it suffices to show that it is a pushout in ${\mathsf{Pr^L}}$. This was shown in \crtCref{prop:pushout_in_prl_defining_E_mon_I_cocart}.
<!-- end proof-85 -->
<!-- corollary-15: body_md -->
Let $\mathsf{C}$ be an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category. Then ${\mathsf{CAlg}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{C})$ carries a canonical $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal structure extending the $\mathsf{I}$-monoidal structure that was discussed before. Moreover, we have a canonical isomorphism of $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-categories:
    \[
    {\mathsf{CAlg}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{C})\simeq\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{E}-\otimes}(F_{\mathsf{I}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{I}),\mathsf{C}).
    \]
<!-- end corollary-15 -->
<!-- proof-86: body_md -->
This follows since
    \begin{align*}
        U^{\mathsf{E}}_{\mathsf{I}}(\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{E}-\otimes}(F_{\mathsf{I}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{I}),\mathsf{C}))
        &\simeq\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{I}-\otimes}(\mathsf{I},U^{\mathsf{E}}_{\mathsf{I}}\mathsf{C})\\
        &\simeq{\mathsf{CAlg}}^{\mathsf{I}}(U^{\mathsf{E}}_{\mathsf{I}}\mathsf{C}).
    \end{align*}
<!-- end proof-86 -->
<!-- corollary-16: body_md -->
The fully faithful right adjoint
    \[
    {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E},\mathsf{I}-\sqcup}(\mathsf{Cat})\hookrightarrow{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})
    \]
    has a further right adjoint, which is given by ${\mathsf{CAlg}}^{\mathsf{I}}$.
<!-- end corollary-16 -->
<!-- proof-87: body_md -->
Note that $U^{\mathsf{E}}_{\mathsf{I}}:{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})\to{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{Cat})$ is conservative. Thus, the $\mathcal{B}$-category ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E},\mathsf{I}-\sqcup}(\mathsf{Cat})$ is exactly the full $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory of objects for which the natural morphism of endofunctors
    \[
    {\mathsf{CAlg}}^{\mathsf{I}}\to\mathrm{id}
    \]
    is an isomorphism. Hence this is the counit of the adjunction.
<!-- end proof-87 -->
<!-- corollary-17: body_md -->
The unit of ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E},\mathsf{I}-\sqcup}(\mathsf{Cat})$ is $F_{\mathsf{I}}^{\mathsf{E}}\mathsf{I}$.
<!-- end corollary-17 -->
<!-- proof-88: body_md -->
The Beck--Chevalley transformation of \crtCref{prop:pushout_in_prl_I_cocart} gives an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functor $F_{\mathsf{I}}^{\mathsf{E}}\mathsf{I}\to L_{\mathsf{I}-\sqcup}F_{\mathsf{I}}^{\mathsf{E}}\mathsf{I}^{\simeq}$. The target is the unit of ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E},\mathsf{I}-\sqcup}(\mathsf{Cat})$.

    This functor identifies the target with the $L_{\mathsf{I}-\sqcup}$-localization of the source. Thus, we must show that the source is $L_{\mathsf{I}-\sqcup}$-local.

    The composition
    \[
    {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})\xrightarrow{{\mathsf{CAlg}}^{\mathsf{I}}}{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E},\mathsf{I}-\sqcup}(\mathsf{Cat})\hookrightarrow{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})
    \]
    is given by $\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{E}-\otimes}(F_{\mathsf{I}}^{\mathsf{E}}\mathsf{I},-)$. Thus, its left adjoint is given by $F_{\mathsf{I}}^{\mathsf{E}}\mathsf{I}\otimes-$. Applying this to the unit gives that $F_{\mathsf{I}}^{\mathsf{E}}\mathsf{I}$ is $\mathsf{I}$-cocartesian.
<!-- end proof-88 -->
<!-- theorem-14: body_md -->
\label{thm:cocart_is_a_mode}
    The $\mathcal{B}$-category $L_{\mathsf{I}-\sqcup}(\mathsf{E}^{\simeq})$ is an idempotent algebra in ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})$.

    Let $\mathsf{C}$ be an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category. Then there is a canonical isomorphism
    \[
    L_{\mathsf{I}-\sqcup}\mathsf{C}\simeq\mathsf{C}\otimes L_{\mathsf{I}-\sqcup}(\mathsf{E}^{\simeq}).
    \]
<!-- end theorem-14 -->
<!-- proof-89: body_md -->
We show the first statement. Observe that the arrow ${\mathsf{CAlg}}^{\mathsf{I}}\circ{\mathsf{CAlg}}^{\mathsf{I}}\to{\mathsf{CAlg}}^{\mathsf{I}}$ is an equivalence of endofunctors of ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})$. Passing to left adjoints, we get an isomorphism of endofunctors of ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})$
    \[
    L_{\mathsf{I}-\sqcup}(\mathsf{E}^{\simeq})\otimes L_{\mathsf{I}-\sqcup}(\mathsf{E}^{\simeq})\otimes-\simeq L_{\mathsf{I}-\sqcup}(\mathsf{E}^{\simeq})\otimes-,
    \]
    establishing the result.

    We show the second statement. By \crtCref{prop:I_cocart_loc_is_sym_monoidal}, the morphism of endofunctors of ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})$, $\mathrm{id}\to-\otimes L_{\mathsf{I}-\sqcup}(\mathsf{E}^{\simeq})$, is an $L_{\mathsf{I}-\sqcup}$-equivalence. We want to show that the target is always $L_{\mathsf{I}-\sqcup}$-local. By the same argument as in \crtCref{cor:Icocart_iff_forgetful_colocal}, it is enough to show that for any $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-categories $\mathsf{C,T}$, the morphism
    \[
    \begin{aligned}
        &\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{E}-\otimes}(\mathsf{C}\otimes L_{\mathsf{I}-\sqcup}(\mathsf{E}^{\simeq}),{\mathsf{CAlg}}^{\mathsf{I}}(\mathsf{T}))\\
        &\qquad\to\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{E}-\otimes}(\mathsf{C}\otimes L_{\mathsf{I}-\sqcup}(\mathsf{E}^{\simeq}),\mathsf{T})
    \end{aligned}
    \]
    is an isomorphism. This follows from the first statement.
<!-- end proof-89 -->
<!-- corollary-18: body_md -->
\label{cor:P_I_ambi_is_a_smashing_localization}
    We have an equivalence
    \[
    L_{(\mathsf{P},\mathsf{I})-\oplus}(\mathsf{E}^{\simeq})\simeq L_{\mathsf{P}-\sqcap}(\mathsf{E}^{\simeq})\otimes L_{\mathsf{I}-\sqcup}(\mathsf{E}^{\simeq})
    \]
    in ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})$. Therefore, $L_{(\mathsf{P},\mathsf{I})-\oplus}(\mathsf{E}^{\simeq})$ is an idempotent algebra in ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})$.

    Let $\mathsf{C}$ be an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category. Then there is a canonical isomorphism
    \[
    L_{(\mathsf{P,I})-\oplus}\mathsf{C}\simeq\mathsf{C}\otimes L_{(\mathsf{P},\mathsf{I})-\oplus}(\mathsf{E}^{\simeq}).
    \]
<!-- end corollary-18 -->
<!-- proof-90: body_md -->
The equivalence $L_{(\mathsf{P},\mathsf{I})-\oplus}(\mathsf{E}^{\simeq})\simeq L_{\mathsf{P}-\sqcap}(\mathsf{E}^{\simeq})\otimes L_{\mathsf{I}-\sqcup}(\mathsf{E}^{\simeq})$ follows since both objects have the same universal property in ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E},(\mathsf{P,I})-\oplus}(\mathsf{Cat})$. Idempotent algebras are closed under tensor products, and thus $L_{(\mathsf{P},\mathsf{I})-\oplus}(\mathsf{E}^{\simeq})$ is an idempotent algebra.

    We now show the equivalence $L_{(\mathsf{P,I})-\oplus}\mathsf{C}\simeq\mathsf{C}\otimes L_{(\mathsf{P},\mathsf{I})-\oplus}(\mathsf{E}^{\simeq})$. Indeed, we have equivalences:
    \begin{align*}
        L_{(\mathsf{P,I})-\oplus}\mathsf{C}
        &\simeq L_{\mathsf{P}-\sqcap}L_{\mathsf{I}-\sqcup}\mathsf{C}\\
        &\simeq L_{\mathsf{P}-\sqcap}(\mathsf{E}^{\simeq})\otimes L_{\mathsf{I}-\sqcup}(\mathsf{E}^{\simeq})\otimes\mathsf{C}\\
        &\simeq L_{(\mathsf{P},\mathsf{I})-\oplus}(\mathsf{E}^{\simeq})\otimes\mathsf{C}.
    \end{align*}
<!-- end proof-90 -->
<!-- definition-37: body_md -->
\label{def:internal_two_categories}
    We define a $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-category $\bm{\mathsf{C}}$ as a sheaf 
    \[
    \bm{\mathsf{C}}:\mathcal{B}^{\mathrm{op}}\to \operatorname{2Cat}
    \]
    on $\mathcal{B}$ taking values in the $(\infty,1)$-category of $(\infty,2)$-categories.

    We define the $\infty$-category of $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-categories as the Lurie tensor product \[\operatorname{2Cat}(\mathcal{B}):=\mathcal{B}\otimes \operatorname{2Cat} \simeq \mathrm{Fun}^R(\mathcal{B}^{\mathrm{op}}, \operatorname{2Cat}). \]

    Using the construction $\mathsf{\Omega}\otimes \operatorname{2Cat}$ from \cite[Construction A.1]{MWcocomplete}, we define the large $\mathcal{B}$-category of $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-categories ${\mathsf{2Cat}}\simeq \operatorname{2Cat}\otimes \mathsf{\Omega}$, or more explicitly \[{\mathsf{2Cat}}: \mathcal{B}^{\mathrm{op}}\to \widehat{\mathrm{Cat}}: A\mapsto \operatorname{2Cat}(\mathcal{B}_{/A}).\]

    Of course, we also have large versions of these objects, denoted by $\widehat{\operatorname{2Cat}}(\mathcal{B})$ and $\widehat{{\mathsf{2Cat}}}$, respectively.
<!-- end definition-37 -->
<!-- example-8: body_md -->
Note that the $\infty$-category of $\mathcal{B}$-categories $\mathrm{Cat}(\mathcal{B})$ is also defined as the Lurie tensor product $\mathcal{B}\otimes \mathrm{Cat}$ and thus it is a $\mathrm{Cat}$-module in $\mathrm{Pr}^{\mathrm{L}}$. In particular, it is the underlying $\infty$-category of a $(\infty,2)$-category ${\mathbf{Cat}}(\mathcal{B})$. We define the large $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-category of $\mathcal{B}$-categories 
    \[\bm{\mathsf{Cat}}:\mathcal{B}^{\mathrm{op}}\to \widehat{\operatorname{2Cat}}:A\mapsto {\mathbf{Cat}}(\mathcal{B}_{/A}).\]
<!-- end example-8 -->
<!-- example-9: body_md -->
Since the $\infty$-category of $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-categories $\operatorname{2Cat}(\mathcal{B})$ is defined as the Lurie tensor product $\mathcal{B}\otimes \operatorname{2Cat}$, and since $\operatorname{2Cat}$ is a $\mathrm{Cat}$-module in $\mathrm{Pr}^{\mathrm{L}}$, $\operatorname{2Cat}(\mathcal{B})$ is a $\mathrm{Cat}$-module in $\mathrm{Pr}^{\mathrm{L}}$. In particular, it is the underlying $\infty$-category of a $(\infty,2)$-category $\mathbf{2Cat}(\mathcal{B})$. We define the large $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-category of $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-categories 
    \[\bm{\mathsf{2Cat}}:\mathcal{B}^{\mathrm{op}}\to \widehat{\operatorname{2Cat}}:A\mapsto \mathbf{2Cat}(\mathcal{B}_{/A}).\]
<!-- end example-9 -->
<!-- definition-38: body_md -->
Let $\bm{\mathsf{C}}$ be a $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-category. We define a \emph{$\mathcal{B}$-$2$-subcategory} to be a morphism $\bm{\mathsf{C}}_0\to \bm{\mathsf{C}}$  such that in every context $A\in \mathcal{B}$, the $2$-functor $\bm{\mathsf{C}}_0(A)\to \bm{\mathsf{C}}(A)$ is an inclusion of a $(\infty,2)$-subcategory.

    We say that a $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-subcategory is full if in every context $A\in \mathcal{B}$ the $(\infty,2)$-subcategory $\bm{\mathsf{C}}_0(A)\to \bm{\mathsf{C}}(A)$ is full in the sense that it is an equivalence on mapping $\infty$-categories.

    We say that a $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-subcategory is locally full if in every context $A\in \mathcal{B}$ the $(\infty,2)$-subcategory $\bm{\mathsf{C}}_0(A)\to \bm{\mathsf{C}}(A)$ is locally full in the sense that it is fully faithful on mapping $\infty$-categories.
<!-- end definition-38 -->
<!-- example-10: body_md -->
We have natural inclusions of full $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-subcategories \[\bm{\mathsf{Cat}}\subset \bm{\mathsf{2Cat}}, \quad \widehat{\bm{\mathsf{Cat}}}\subset \widehat{\bm{\mathsf{2Cat}}}.\]
    We also have natural inclusions of $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-subcategories
    \[\mathsf{Cat}\subset \bm{\mathsf{Cat}},\quad {\mathsf{2Cat}}\subset \bm{\mathsf{2Cat}}.\]

    We will not denote any of these inclusions in the text, as we view them as natural inclusions.
<!-- end example-10 -->
<!-- proposition-55: body_md -->
The natural inclusion 
    \[\mathsf{Cat}\subset {\mathsf{2Cat}}\]
    admits a right adjoint $(-)^{\simeq2}:{\mathsf{2Cat}}\to \mathsf{Cat}$. The counit $\bm{\mathsf{C}}^{\simeq2}\hookrightarrow \bm{\mathsf{C}}$ is the embedding of the $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-subcategory spanned by invertible $2$-morphisms.
<!-- end proposition-55 -->
<!-- proof-91: body_md -->
This follows since the inclusion $\mathrm{Cat}\hookrightarrow \operatorname{2Cat}$ is a morphism in $\mathrm{Pr}^{\mathrm{L}}$ and so it induces an adjunction after applying $-\otimes \mathsf{\Omega}$.
<!-- end proof-91 -->
<!-- proposition-56: body_md -->
\label{prop:gray_module_structures}
    The $\infty$-category $\operatorname{2Cat}(\mathcal{B})$ carries a left and a right module structure over $\operatorname{2Cat}$, equipped with the monoidal structure given by the Gray tensor product $\mathbin{\vec{\times}}$. Thus $\operatorname{2Cat}(\mathcal{B})$ is tensored and cotensored under $\operatorname{2Cat}$ in two different ways.
<!-- end proposition-56 -->
<!-- proof-92: body_md -->
This follows immediately from the isomorphism $\operatorname{2Cat}(\mathcal{B})\simeq \operatorname{2Cat}\otimes \mathcal{B}$ in $\mathrm{Pr}^{\mathrm{L}}$.
<!-- end proof-92 -->
<!-- proposition-57: body_md -->
\label{prop:internal_gray_tensor_product}
    $\operatorname{2Cat}(\mathcal{B})$ carries a further structure of an associative algebra in $\mathrm{Pr}^{\mathrm{L}}$.
<!-- end proposition-57 -->
<!-- proof-93: body_md -->
This follows since the functor \[-\otimes \mathcal{B}: \mathrm{Pr}^{\mathrm{L}}\to \operatorname{Mod}_{\mathcal{B}}(\mathrm{Pr}^{\mathrm{L}})\]
    is symmetric monoidal, and its right adjoint, which is the forgetful functor $\operatorname{Mod}_{\mathcal{B}}(\mathrm{Pr}^{\mathrm{L}})\to \mathrm{Pr}^{\mathrm{L}}$, is lax symmetric monoidal.
<!-- end proof-93 -->
<!-- remark-17: body_md -->
Let $\mathbb{I}$ be some $(\infty,2)$-category. Then we can view $\mathbb{I}$ as the constant sheaf on $\mathcal{B}$ with value $\mathbb{I}$. In this case we have that the two meanings of \[\bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}^{\operatorname{lax}}(\mathbb{I},-),\] as the internal hom in $\operatorname{2Cat}(\mathcal{B})$ and the one given by the structure of $\operatorname{2Cat}(\mathcal{B})$ as cotensored over $\operatorname{2Cat}$ coincide.
<!-- end remark-17 -->
<!-- definition-39: body_md -->
Let $p:\mathbb{C}\to \mathbb{D}$ be a functor of $(\infty,2)$-categories. Let $f:x\to y$ be a $1$-morphism in $\mathbb{C}$. We say that $f$ is $p$-cocartesian if the following square is a pullback of $\infty$-categories.
    \[
        \begin{tikzcd}
        \mathrm{Fun}_{\mathbb{C}}(y,z)
          \arrow[r, "{\circ f}"]
          \arrow[d, "p"']
        &
        \mathrm{Fun}_{\mathbb{C}}(x,z)
          \arrow[d, "p"]
        \\
        \mathrm{Fun}_{\mathbb{D}}(p(y),p(z))
          \arrow[r, "{\circ p(f)}"']
        &
        \mathrm{Fun}_{\mathbb{D}}(p(x),p(z)).
        \end{tikzcd}
    \]

    In this case we say that $f$ is a cocartesian lift of $p(f):p(x)\to p(y)$ at $x$.
<!-- end definition-39 -->
<!-- definition-40: body_md -->
\label{def:one_cocartesian_fibration}
    Let $p:\mathbb{C}\to \mathbb{D}$ be a functor of $(\infty,2)$-categories. We will say that $p$ is a $1$-cocartesian fibration if the following conditions hold:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $p$ admits cocartesian lifts.
        \item For any $x,y\in \mathbb{C}$, the functor \[\mathrm{Fun}_{\mathbb{C}}(x,y)\to \mathrm{Fun}_{\mathbb{D}}(p(x),p(y))\] is a right fibration.
    \end{enumerate}


    A morphism of $1$-cocartesian fibrations from $p:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{D}$ to $q:\mathbb{X}\to\mathbb{Y}$ is a commutative square in $\operatorname{2Cat}$:
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
        \mathbb{C}\ar[r]\ar[d, "p"]& \mathbb{X}\ar[d, "q"]\\
        \mathbb{D}\ar[r] & \mathbb{Y}
    \end{tikzcd}\]
    such that the upper horizontal functor sends $p$-cocartesian edges to $q$-cocartesian edges.
<!-- end definition-40 -->
<!-- theorem-15: body_md -->
(\cite[Theorem 3.2]{CLRUniversalityOfUnferling})
    Let $\mathbb{C}\in \operatorname{2Cat}$. Then there is an equivalence of $(\infty,2)$-categories 
    \[\mathbf{Cocart}_{\mathbb{C}}\simeq \mathbf{Fun}(\mathbb{C},{\mathbf{Cat}}).\]
<!-- end theorem-15 -->
<!-- example-11: body_md -->
\label{example:oplax_slice}
    Let $\mathbb{C}$ be an $(\infty,2)$-category. Let $x\in \mathbb{C}$ be an object. Let $\mathbb{C}_{x//}$ denote the following pullback:
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
        \mathbb{C}_{x//}\ar[d]\ar[r]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        &\mathbf{Fun}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\Delta^1,\mathbb{C})\ar[d,"s"]\\
        * \ar[r] & \mathbb{C}.
    \end{tikzcd}\]
    Then the composition 
    \[\mathbb{C}_{x//}\to \mathbf{Fun}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\Delta^1,\mathbb{C})\xrightarrow{t} \mathbb{C}\]
    is the cocartesian fibration classifying the $2$-functor 
    \[\mathrm{Fun}_{\mathbb{C}}(x,-):\mathbb{C}\to {\mathbf{Cat}}.\]
<!-- end example-11 -->
<!-- definition-41: body_md -->
\label{def:internal_one_cocartesian_fibration}
    We say that a functor of $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-categories $p:\bm{\mathsf{C}}\to \bm{\mathsf{D}}$ is a $1$-cocartesian fibration if in every context $A\in \mathcal{B}$, the $2$-functor 
    \[p(A):\bm{\mathsf{C}}(A)\to \bm{\mathsf{D}}(A)\]
    is a $1$-cocartesian fibration and for every change of context $s:B\to A$ the square 
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
        \bm{\mathsf{C}}(A)\ar[r,"s^*"]\ar[d,"p"] & \bm{\mathsf{C}}(B)\ar[d,"p"]\\
        \bm{\mathsf{D}}(A)\ar[r,"s^*"] &\bm{\mathsf{D}}(B).
    \end{tikzcd}\]
    is a morphism of $1$-cocartesian fibrations of $(\infty,2)$-categories.
<!-- end definition-41 -->
<!-- example-12: body_md -->
Since \[\bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\Delta^1,\bm{\mathsf{C}})(A)\simeq \mathbf{Fun}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\Delta^1,\bm{\mathsf{C}}(A))\] is computed contextwise, and pullbacks of sheaves agree with pullbacks of presheaves, we get that if $\bm{\mathsf{C}}$ is a $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-category and $x:A\to \bm{\mathsf{C}}$ is an object defined in the context $A$, we may define a $\mathcal{B}_{/A}$-$2$-category $\bm{\mathsf{C}}_{x//}$ by the pullback in $\operatorname{2Cat}(\mathcal{B})$:
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        \bm{\mathsf{C}}_{x//}\ar[d]\ar[r]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        &\bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\Delta^1,\bm{\mathsf{C}})\ar[d,"s"]\\
        *\ar[r,"x"] & \bm{\mathsf{C}}.
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    Then the composition $\bm{\mathsf{C}}_{x//}\to \bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\Delta^1,\bm{\mathsf{C}}) \xrightarrow{t} \bm{\mathsf{C}}$ is a $1$-cocartesian fibration of $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-categories.
<!-- end example-12 -->
<!-- proposition-58: body_md -->
Let the following be a pullback in $\operatorname{2Cat}(\mathcal{B})$. If $p$ is a $1$-cocartesian fibration of $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-categories, then so is $p'$.
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
        \bm{\mathsf{X}}\ar[r]\ar[d,"p'"']\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        &\bm{\mathsf{Y}}\ar[d,"p"]\\
        \bm{\mathsf{Z}}\ar[r] &\bm{\mathsf{W}}.
    \end{tikzcd}\]
<!-- end proposition-58 -->
<!-- proof-94: body_md -->
This follows since pullbacks of sheaves are computed as pullbacks of presheaves.
<!-- end proof-94 -->
<!-- lemma-12: body_md -->
Let $p:\bm{\mathsf{Y}}\to \bm{\mathsf{W}}$ be a $1$-cocartesian fibration of $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-categories. If $\bm{\mathsf{W}}$ is a $\mathcal{B}$-category, i.e. all its $2$-arrows are isomorphisms, then so is $\bm{\mathsf{Y}}$. Moreover, $p$ is then a cocartesian fibration of $\mathcal{B}$-categories.
<!-- end lemma-12 -->
<!-- proof-95: body_md -->
$\bm{\mathsf{Y}}$ is a $\mathcal{B}$-category since a right fibration over a groupoid is a groupoid. 

    $p$ is a cocartesian fibration by the first condition in the definition of $1$-cocartesian fibrations of $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-categories.
<!-- end proof-95 -->
<!-- lemma-13: body_md -->
Let $p:\bm{\mathsf{Y}}\to \bm{\mathsf{W}}$ be a $1$-cocartesian fibration of $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-categories. Then the following square is a pullback square:
        \[\begin{tikzcd}
        \bm{\mathsf{Y}}^{\simeq2}\ar[r]\ar[d,"p'"']\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        &\bm{\mathsf{Y}}\ar[d,"p"]\\
        \bm{\mathsf{W}}^{\simeq2}\ar[r] &\bm{\mathsf{W}}.
    \end{tikzcd}\]
    In particular, $p'$ is a cocartesian fibration of $\mathcal{B}$-categories.
<!-- end lemma-13 -->
<!-- proof-96: body_md -->
We must show that a $2$-morphism $\alpha:f\to g:X\to Y$ in the context $A$ in $\bm{\mathsf{Y}}$ is an isomorphism if and only if $p(\alpha)$ is an isomorphism. This follows from $p$ being a homwise right fibration.
<!-- end proof-96 -->
<!-- theorem-16: body_md -->
\label{prop:univ_internal_2_cocart_fib}
    Let $\bm{\mathsf{Cat}}_{*//}$ be the oplax slice for the terminal $\mathcal{B}$-category $*\in \bm{\mathsf{Cat}}(*)$. Then \[(\bm{\mathsf{Cat}}_{*//})^{\simeq_2}\to \bm{\mathsf{Cat}}^{\simeq_2}\simeq \mathsf{Cat}\] is the cocartesian fibration of $\mathcal{B}$-categories classifying the identity functor $\mathrm{id}:\mathsf{Cat}\to \mathsf{Cat}$.
<!-- end theorem-16 -->
<!-- proof-97: body_md -->
Let $\mathsf{Un}(\mathrm{id})\to \mathsf{Cat}$ be the unstraightening of the identity.  \cite[Proposition 6.4.9]{MInternalStraightenning} states that in each context $A$ the cocartesian fibration of $\infty$-categories $\mathsf{Un}(\mathrm{id})(A)\to \mathsf{Cat}(A)$ classifies the functor \[\Gamma:\mathsf{Cat}(A)\simeq \mathrm{Cat}(\mathcal{B}_{/A})\to \mathrm{Cat}.\]

    In every context $A$, the $2$-functor 
    \[\Gamma:{\mathbf{Cat}}(\mathcal{B}_{/A})\to {\mathbf{Cat}}\] is $2$-representable by the terminal $\mathcal{B}_{/A}$-category $*\in {\mathbf{Cat}}(\mathcal{B}_{/A})$ in the sense that there is a canonical equivalence of functors $\mathrm{Fun}_{{\mathbf{Cat}}(\mathcal{B}_{/A})}(*,-)\simeq\Gamma:{\mathbf{Cat}}(\mathcal{B}_{/A})\to {\mathbf{Cat}}$. Thus, in every context $A$ the functor \[(\bm{\mathsf{Cat}}_{*//})(A)\to \bm{\mathsf{Cat}}(A)\]
    classifies the functor $\Gamma$. 
    
    Therefore, in every context $A$, $\mathsf{Un}(\mathrm{id})(A)\to \mathsf{Cat}(A)$ agrees with $(\bm{\mathsf{Cat}}_{*//})^{\simeq_2}(A)\to \bm{\mathsf{Cat}}^{\simeq_2}(A)$. This identification can be  made functorial in $A$ by functoriality of the $2$-Yoneda embedding \cite{BenMosheEnrichedYoneda}, thus proving the claim.
<!-- end proof-97 -->
<!-- definition-42: body_md -->
\label{def:internal_two_unstraightening}
    Let 
    \[F:\bm{\mathsf{X}}\to \bm{\mathsf{Cat}}\]
    be a functor of $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-categories. Then we define the $1$-cocartesian unstraightening of $F$ as the left vertical morphism in the following pullback.
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
    \bm{\mathsf{Un}}(F)\ar[r]\ar[d]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr] & \bm{\mathsf{Cat}}_{*//}\ar[d]\\
    \bm{\mathsf{X}}\ar[r] & \bm{\mathsf{Cat}}.
\end{tikzcd}\]
<!-- end definition-42 -->
<!-- theorem-17: body_md -->
\label{thm:lax_unstraightening_external}
    Let $\mathbb{C}$ be an $(\infty,2)$-category. Then there is an equivalence of $(\infty,2)$-categories 
    \[\mathbf{Fun}^{\operatorname{lax}}(\mathbb{C}, {\mathbf{Cat}}) \simeq \mathbf{2Cat}^{\operatorname{cocart}}_{/\mathbb{C}}\]
    where the right-hand side is the full $(\infty,2)$-subcategory of $\mathbf{2Cat}_{/\mathbb{C}}$ spanned by $1$-cocartesian fibrations.
<!-- end theorem-17 -->
<!-- proof-98: body_md -->
This is a restriction of \cite[Theorem A]{AbellanGagnaHaugseng2025} to functors landing in ${\mathbf{Cat}}\subset \mathbf{2Cat}$ and to $1$-cocartesian fibrations of $(\infty,2)$-categories.
<!-- end proof-98 -->
<!-- theorem-18: body_md -->
\label{thm:desc_of_the_unst_of_universal_lax_natural_transformation}
    We have a commutative square in $\widehat{\mathbf{2Cat}}_{/ \mathbf{Fun}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\Delta^1, {\mathbf{Cat}})}$:
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
        \mathbf{Un}(s)\ar[r,"\sim"]\ar[d,"\mathbf{Un}(\alpha_{\operatorname{univ}})"'] & \mathbf{Fun}^{\operatorname{oplax},0-*}(\Delta^2, {\mathbf{Cat}})\ar[d,"\Lambda^2_2\hookrightarrow\Delta^2"]\\
        \mathbf{Un}(t)\ar[r,"\sim"] & \mathbf{Fun}^{\operatorname{oplax},0-*}(\Lambda^2_2, {\mathbf{Cat}}),
    \end{tikzcd}\]
    where the horizontal functors are equivalences.
<!-- end theorem-18 -->
<!-- proof-99: body_md -->
We prove the upper horizontal equivalence.
    
    Observe the following pasting of squares in $\widehat{\operatorname{2Cat}}$, which we claim are cartesian.
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
        \mathbf{Fun}^{\operatorname{oplax},0-*}(\Delta^2, {\mathbf{Cat}})\ar[r]\ar[d]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        &\mathbf{Fun}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\Delta^2, {\mathbf{Cat}})\ar[r,"\left\{1,2\right\}"]\ar[d,"\left\{0,1\right\}"]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        & \mathbf{Fun}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\Delta^1, {\mathbf{Cat}})\ar[d,"s"]\\
        {\mathbf{Cat}}_{*//}\ar[r]\ar[d]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        &\mathbf{Fun}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\Delta^1, {\mathbf{Cat}})\ar[r,"t"]\ar[d,"s"]
        &{\mathbf{Cat}}\\
        \left\{*\right\}\ar[r]
        &{\mathbf{Cat}}.
    \end{tikzcd}\]
    The upper right square follows from the pushout in $\mathrm{Cat}\subset \operatorname{2Cat}$: 
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
        \Delta^0\ar[r,"1"]\ar[d,"0"'] & \Delta^1\ar[d]\\
        \Delta^1 \ar[r] & \Delta^2.	\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125, rotate=180}, draw=none, from=2-2, to=1-1]
    \end{tikzcd}\]
    The lower square is a pullback by the definition of ${\mathbf{Cat}}_{*//}$, and the upper left square is a pullback by the pasting lemma applied to the vertical pasting of squares on the left.

    Recall that the middle horizontal composition is the universal unstraightening. Thus the upper horizontal composition is the unstraightening of $s$ as we claimed before.

    The proof of the lower horizontal equivalence is similar and is left as an exercise to the reader. 

    We are left to show that the square in the theorem commutes.  
    The functoriality of $\mathbf{Un}(\alpha_{\operatorname{univ}})$ is given by mapping an object to the target of the cocartesian lift of the arrow it sits over in $\mathbf{Fun}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\Delta^1,{\mathbf{Cat}})$.
    This sends $x\in C$ to the image of $x$ in $D$.
<!-- end proof-99 -->
<!-- definition-43: body_md -->
Let \[\bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}^{\operatorname{oplax},0-*}(\Delta^2, \bm{\mathsf{Cat}})\subset \bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\Delta^2, \bm{\mathsf{Cat}})\]
    and let 
    \[\bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}^{\operatorname{oplax},0-*}(\Lambda^2_2, \bm{\mathsf{Cat}})\subset \bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\Lambda^2_2, \bm{\mathsf{Cat}})\]
    denote the full $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-subcategories spanned by functors that in every context $A$ send $0\in \Delta^2$ (respectively $0\in \Lambda^2_2$) to the terminal object in $\bm{\mathsf{Cat}}(A)$.
<!-- end definition-43 -->
<!-- proposition-59: body_md -->
\label{prop:extra_functoriality_of_unst_univ_case}
    $\bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}^{\operatorname{oplax},0-*}(\Delta^2, \bm{\mathsf{Cat}})$ and $\bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}^{\operatorname{oplax},0-*}(\Lambda^2_2, \bm{\mathsf{Cat}})$ are the unstraightenings of the functors $s$ and $t$, respectively.
<!-- end proposition-59 -->
<!-- proof-100: body_md -->
The proof of \crtCref{thm:desc_of_the_unst_of_universal_lax_natural_transformation} applies here in every context and is functorial under change of context since $\bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}^{\operatorname{oplax}}$ is applied contextwise.
<!-- end proof-100 -->
<!-- corollary-19: body_md -->
\label{cor:extra_functoriality_of_unst}
    Let \[\alpha:F\to G:\bm{\mathsf{X}}\to \bm{\mathsf{Cat}}\] be a lax natural transformation. Then there exists a commutative triangle 
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
        \bm{\mathsf{Un}}(F)\ar[rr,"\bm{\mathsf{Un}}(\alpha)"]\ar[dr] && \bm{\mathsf{Un}}(G)\ar[dl] \\
        &\bm{\mathsf{X}}
    \end{tikzcd}\]
    such that for any object $x:A\to \bm{\mathsf{X}}$ in the context $A$, the restriction of $\bm{\mathsf{Un}}(\alpha)$ to the fiber over $x$ agrees with the component $F(x)\to G(x)$  of $\alpha$ at $x$ in $ \bm{\mathsf{Cat}}(A)$.
<!-- end corollary-19 -->
<!-- proof-101: body_md -->
\crtCref{prop:extra_functoriality_of_unst_univ_case} proves this for the universal case and gives a functor $\bm{\mathsf{Un}}(s)\to \bm{\mathsf{Un}}(t)$. Let us prove this for the general case. 
    
    The data of $\alpha:F\to G$ are equivalent to the data of a functor
    \[\bm{\mathsf{X}}\to \bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\Delta^1,\bm{\mathsf{Cat}}).\]
    
    We have that \[\bm{\mathsf{Un}}(F)\simeq \bm{\mathsf{X}}\times_{\bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\Delta^1,\bm{\mathsf{2Cat}})}\bm{\mathsf{Un}}(s)\] and that
    \[\bm{\mathsf{Un}}(G)\simeq \bm{\mathsf{X}}\times_{\bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\Delta^1,\bm{\mathsf{2Cat}})}\bm{\mathsf{Un}}(t).\] Thus the result follows from the universal case.
<!-- end proof-101 -->
<!-- definition-44: body_md -->
\label{def:internal_span_two_category}
    Let $(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C'})\in \operatorname{SpanPairs}(\mathcal{B})$. Then the following composition \[\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{1.5}}(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C'}): \mathcal{B}^{\mathrm{op}}\xrightarrow{(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C'})}\operatorname{SpanPairs}\xrightarrow{{\mathbf{Span}^{1.5}}}\operatorname{2Cat}\]
    is a $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-category which we call the internal span $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-category attached to $(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C'})$.

    This construction defines a functor 
    \[\operatorname{SpanPairs}(\mathcal{B})\to \operatorname{2Cat}(\mathcal{B}).\]
<!-- end definition-44 -->
<!-- proposition-60: body_md -->
\label{prop:univ_prop_of_span_half}
    We have an equivalence of $\infty$-categories
    \[\mathrm{Fun}_{\mathbf{2Cat}(\mathcal{B})}^{\mathsf{C}'\operatorname{-radj}}(\mathsf{C}^{\mathrm{op}},\bm{\mathsf{D}})\simeq \mathrm{Fun}_{\mathbf{2Cat}(\mathcal{B})}(\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{1.5}}(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}'),\bm{\mathsf{D}}).\]
<!-- end proposition-60 -->
<!-- proof-102: body_md -->
This follows from applying the universal property pointwise.
<!-- end proof-102 -->
<!-- example-13: body_md -->
A $\mathcal{B}$-category $\mathsf{D}$ is $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-complete iff $\mathsf{D}$ admits a structure of a cartesian $\mathsf{E}$-monoid in $\bm{\mathsf{Cat}}$.
<!-- end example-13 -->
<!-- definition-45: body_md -->
\label{def:E_two_complete}
    We say that a $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-category $\bm{\mathsf{D}}$ is $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-$2$-complete if $\bm{\mathsf{D}}$ admits a structure of a cartesian $\mathsf{E}$-monoid in $\bm{\mathsf{2Cat}}$.
<!-- end definition-45 -->
<!-- proposition-61: body_md -->
\label{prop:E_two_complete_criterion}
    Let $\bm{\mathsf{D}}$ be a $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-category. Then the following conditions are equivalent:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $\bm{\mathsf{D}}$ is $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-$2$-complete.
        \item The functor \[\bm{\mathsf{D}}:\mathcal{B}^{\mathrm{op}}\to \mathbf{2Cat}\] is $\mathcal{E}$-right adjointable, where $\mathcal{E}$ is the local class corresponding to the context-free subuniverse $\mathsf{E}$.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end proposition-61 -->
<!-- proof-103: body_md -->
Suppose $\bm{\mathsf{D}}$ is $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-$2$-complete. 

    That is, we assume that the functor $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}(A)^{\mathrm{op}}\to \mathbf{2Cat}(\mathcal{B}_{/A})$ sending $[s:B\to A]\mapsto s_*s^*\pi_A^*(\bm{\mathsf{D}})$ is $\mathsf{E}(A)$-right adjointable. 
    
    We first prove that $\bm{\mathsf{D}}:\mathcal{B}^{\mathrm{op}}\to \mathbf{2Cat}$ sends morphisms in $\mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{op}}$ to left adjoints. Let $s:B\to A \in \mathcal{E}$. We must show that $s^*:\bm{\mathsf{D}}(A)\to \bm{\mathsf{D}}(B)$ is a left adjoint.
    
    Then the morphism $\pi_A^*(\bm{\mathsf{D}})\to s_*s^*\pi_A^*(\bm{\mathsf{D}})$ is a left adjoint in $\mathbf{2Cat}(\mathcal{B}_{/A})$. 
    
    Recall that $\Gamma:\mathbf{2Cat}(\mathcal{B}_{/A})\to \mathbf{2Cat}$ is a $2$-functor. It sends $\pi_A^*(\bm{\mathsf{D}})$ to $\bm{\mathsf{D}}(A)$ and it sends $ s_*s^*\pi_A^*(\bm{\mathsf{D}})$ to $\bm{\mathsf{D}}(B)$.
    
    The resulting morphism $s^*:\bm{\mathsf{D}}(A)\to \bm{\mathsf{D}}(B)$ is a left adjoint as we stated. We next must show the adjointability for pullback squares, but this follows from the fact that adjunctions in $\mathbf{2Cat}(\mathcal{B}_{/A})$ require adjointability of squares.
    
    The proof of the other implication is analogous.
<!-- end proof-103 -->
<!-- example-14: body_md -->
The $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-category $\bm{\mathsf{Cat}}\in\widehat{\bm{\mathsf{2Cat}}}$ is $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-$2$-complete.
<!-- end example-14 -->
<!-- proof-104: body_md -->
The functor $\bm{\mathsf{Cat}}:\mathcal{B}^{\mathrm{op}}\to \widehat{\mathbf{2Cat}}$ is given on underlying $\infty$-categories as the composition
    \[
    \bm{\mathsf{Cat}}:\mathcal{B}^{\mathrm{op}}\xrightarrow{A\mapsto \mathcal{B}_{/A}}\mathrm{Pr}^{\mathrm{L}} \xrightarrow{-\otimes \mathrm{Cat}}\operatorname{Mod}_{\mathrm{Cat}}(\mathrm{Pr}^{\mathrm{L}})\to \widehat{\mathbf{2Cat}}.
    \]
    It sends all morphisms in $\mathcal{B}^{\mathrm{op}}$ to left adjoints by definition. The Beck-Chevalley conditions can also be verified directly.
<!-- end proof-104 -->
<!-- example-15: body_md -->
Let $\bm{\mathsf{D}}$ be $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-$2$-complete, and let $\mathbb{I}\in \operatorname{2Cat}$. Then $\bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\mathbb{I},\bm{\mathsf{D}})$ is $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-$2$-complete.
<!-- end example-15 -->
<!-- proof-105: body_md -->
The functor $\bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\mathbb{I},\bm{\mathsf{D}})$ is given as the composition
    \[\mathcal{B}^{\mathrm{op}}\xrightarrow{\bm{\mathsf{D}}}\mathbf{2Cat}\xrightarrow{\mathbf{Fun}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\mathbb{I},-)}\mathbf{2Cat}.\]
    The result follows since $\mathbf{Fun}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\mathbb{I},-)$ is a $2$-functor.
<!-- end proof-105 -->
<!-- definition-46: body_md -->
\label{def:E_two_continuous}
    Let $F:\bm{\mathsf{C}}\to \bm{\mathsf{D}}$ be a $2$-functor between $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-$2$-complete $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-categories. 
    Recall that \[\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{E}-\sqcap}((\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}})^{\mathrm{op}}, \bm{\mathsf{2Cat}}^{\simeq_2})\simeq \bm{\mathsf{2Cat}}^{\simeq_2}.\]
    
    We say that $F$ is $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-$2$-continuous if the corresponding natural transformation  
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
    	(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}})^{\mathrm{op}} && \bm{\mathsf{2Cat}}
    	\arrow[""{name=0, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, shift right=2, curve={height=18pt}, from=1-1, to=1-3]
    	\arrow[""{name=1, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, shift left=2, curve={height=-12pt}, from=1-1, to=1-3]
    	\arrow[between={0.2}{0.8}, Rightarrow, nfold, from=1, to=0]
    \end{tikzcd}\]
    corresponding to $F$ is $\mathsf{E}$-right adjointable.
<!-- end definition-46 -->
<!-- proposition-62: body_md -->
\label{prop:E_two_continuous_criterion}
    Let $F:\bm{\mathsf{C}}\to \bm{\mathsf{D}}$ be a $2$-functor between $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-$2$-complete $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-categories. Then the following are equivalent:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $F$ is  $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-$2$-continuous.
        \item The natural transformation $F$ of the type
        \[\begin{tikzcd}
        	\mathcal{B}^{\mathrm{op}} && \mathbf{2Cat}
        	\arrow[""{name=0, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, shift right=2, curve={height=18pt}, from=1-1, to=1-3]
        	\arrow[""{name=1, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, shift left=2, curve={height=-12pt}, from=1-1, to=1-3]
        	\arrow[between={0.2}{0.8}, Rightarrow, nfold, from=1, to=0]
        \end{tikzcd}\]
        is $\mathcal{E}$-right adjointable.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end proposition-62 -->
<!-- proof-106: body_md -->
The same proof as before works.
<!-- end proof-106 -->
<!-- proposition-63: body_md -->
The inclusion $(\mathbf{2Cat}(\mathcal{B})^{\mathsf{E}-2\sqcap})^{\simeq2}\subset \mathbf{2Cat}(\mathcal{B})^{\simeq2}$ preserves all limits.
<!-- end proposition-63 -->
<!-- proof-107: body_md -->
The $\infty$-category $(\mathbf{2Cat}(\mathcal{B})^{\mathsf{E}-2\sqcap})^{\simeq2}$ is the full $\infty$-subcategory of \[\mathrm{Fun}({\mathbf{Span}^{1.5}}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{E}), \mathbf{2Cat})\] spanned by those functors that restrict to sheaves on $\mathcal{B}^{\mathrm{op}}$. The inclusion in the proposition above agrees with restriction along $\mathcal{B}^{\mathrm{op}}\hookrightarrow {\mathbf{Span}^{1.5}}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{E})$ and thus preserves all limits.
<!-- end proof-107 -->
<!-- proposition-64: body_md -->
Let $\mathbb{I}\to \mathbb{J}$ be a $2$-functor. Let $\bm{\mathsf{D}}$ be an $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-$2$-complete $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-category. Then the functor \[\bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\mathbb{J},\bm{\mathsf{D}})\to \bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\mathbb{I},\bm{\mathsf{D}}) \]
    is $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-$2$-continuous.
<!-- end proposition-64 -->
<!-- proof-108: body_md -->
This arrow agrees with the whiskering 
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
        \mathcal{B}^{\mathrm{op}}\ar[r]&\mathbf{2Cat} && \mathbf{2Cat}
        \arrow[""{name=0, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, "{\mathbf{Fun}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\mathbb{I},-)}"', shift right=2, curve={height=18pt}, from=1-2, to=1-4]
        \arrow[""{name=1, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, "{\mathbf{Fun}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\mathbb{J},-)}", shift left=2, curve={height=-12pt}, from=1-2, to=1-4]
        \arrow[between={0.2}{0.8}, Rightarrow, nfold, from=1, to=0]
    \end{tikzcd}\]
    which is right adjointable since whiskering with a natural transformation of $2$-functors preserves adjointability.
<!-- end proof-108 -->
<!-- example-16: body_md -->
Let $\bm{\mathsf{D}}$ be $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-$2$-complete. Assume $\bm{\mathsf{D}}$ has a terminal object $*$. Then $\bm{\mathsf{D}}_{*//}$ is $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-$2$-complete.
<!-- end example-16 -->
<!-- proof-109: body_md -->
The following is a pullback in $\mathbf{2Cat}(\mathcal{B})^{\mathsf{E}-2\sqcap}$.
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        \bm{\mathsf{D}}_{*//}\ar[d]\ar[r]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        &\bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\Delta^1,\bm{\mathsf{D}})\ar[d,"s"]\\
        *\ar[r,"*"] & \bm{\mathsf{D}}.
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
<!-- end proof-109 -->
<!-- theorem-19: body_md -->
\label{thm:univ_unst_is_monoidal}
    The three $\mathcal{B}$-categories $\mathsf{Cat}_{*/},\mathsf{Cat}_{*//},\mathsf{Cat}$ are $
    \mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-complete and both functors in the composition \[\mathsf{Cat}_{*/}\to \mathsf{Cat}_{*//} \to \mathsf{Cat} \] are $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-continuous.
<!-- end theorem-19 -->
<!-- proof-110: body_md -->
Consider the following diagram:
        \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        \mathsf{Cat}_{*/}\ar[d]\ar[r]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        &\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}(\Delta^1,\mathsf{Cat})\ar[d,hook]\ar[r]
        &\mathsf{Cat}\ar[d,equal]\\
        \mathsf{Cat}_{*//}\ar[d]\ar[r]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        &\bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\Delta^1,\bm{\mathsf{Cat}})^{\simeq2}\ar[d,"s"]\ar[r]
        &\mathsf{Cat}\\
        *\ar[r,"*"] & \mathsf{Cat}.
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    It is enough to show that all of it is in $\mathsf{Cat}^{\mathsf{E}-\sqcap}$.

    The lower left square is in $\mathsf{Cat}^{\mathsf{E}-\sqcap}$ by the example above. 
    
    Therefore, to show that the upper left square is in $\mathsf{Cat}^{\mathsf{E}-\sqcap}$ it suffices to show that the middle upper vertical morphism is in  $\mathsf{Cat}^{\mathsf{E}-\sqcap}$. This follows since $\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}(\Delta^1,\mathsf{Cat}) \simeq \bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\Delta^1,\bm{\mathsf{Cat}}^{\simeq2})^{\simeq2}$ and the inclusion $\bm{\mathsf{Cat}}^{\simeq2}\hookrightarrow \bm{\mathsf{Cat}}$ is $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-continuous. A similar argument explains why the upper right square is in $\mathsf{Cat}^{\mathsf{E}-\sqcap}$.
<!-- end proof-110 -->
<!-- theorem-20: body_md -->
\label{thm:univ_unst_of_lax_natural_transformation_is_E_monoidal}
    The universal unstraightening of the universal lax natural transformation  \[\bm{\mathsf{Un}}(\alpha_{\operatorname{univ}}):\bm{\mathsf{Un}}(s)\to \bm{\mathsf{Un}}(t)\]
    described in \crtCref{prop:extra_functoriality_of_unst_univ_case} is an $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-$2$-continuous functor between $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-$2$-complete $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-categories.
<!-- end theorem-20 -->
<!-- proof-111: body_md -->
The pullbacks defining both $\bm{\mathsf{Un}}(s), \bm{\mathsf{Un}}(t)$ are in $\mathbf{2Cat}(\mathcal{B})^{\mathsf{E}-2\sqcap}$ and the morphism between them as described in \crtCref{thm:desc_of_the_unst_of_universal_lax_natural_transformation} is a base change of a morphism in $\mathbf{2Cat}(\mathcal{B})^{\mathsf{E}-2\sqcap}$.
<!-- end proof-111 -->
<!-- proposition-65: body_md -->
\label{prop:E_cart_S_is_equivalent_to_span}
    The composition
    \[\mathsf{S}\subset\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{1.5}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})_{//*} \to \bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\Delta^1, \bm{\mathsf{Span}^{1.5}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}))\xrightarrow{s}\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{1.5}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\]
    is an equivalence between $\mathsf{S}$ and ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\simeq \bm{\mathsf{Span}^{1.5}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})^{\simeq_2}$.
<!-- end proposition-65 -->
<!-- proof-112: body_md -->
We will show that the composition in the proposition defines an equivalence on the $\mathcal{B}$ anima of objects and on the $\mathcal{B}$ anima of morphisms, which is enough. 

    The fact that this is an equivalence on objects is obvious. The fact that it is an equivalence on morphisms comes from the fact that morphisms in $\mathsf{S}$ are of the form
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
    {B} && {F} && C \\
    &&& {F} \\
    {B} &&&& C \\
    & {B} \\
    {A} && {A} && {A}.
    \arrow[from=1-3, to=1-1]
    \arrow[tail,from=1-3, to=1-5]
    \arrow[equal,from=2-4, to=1-3]
    \arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125, rotate=90}, draw=none, from=2-4, to=1-5]
    \arrow[tail, from=2-4, to=3-5]
    \arrow[equal,from=3-1, to=1-1]
    \arrow[from=3-1, to=5-1]
                              
                              
    \arrow[equal,from=3-5, to=1-5]
    \arrow[tail,from=3-5, to=5-5]
    \arrow[from=2-4, to=4-2]
    \arrow[equal,from=4-2, to=3-1]
    \arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125, rotate=-90}, draw=none, from=4-2, to=5-1]
    \arrow[tail,from=4-2, to=5-3]
    \arrow[equal,from=5-3, to=5-1]
    \arrow[equal,from=5-3, to=5-5]
    \end{tikzcd}\]
    and are visibly determined uniquely by the first row.
<!-- end proof-112 -->
<!-- proposition-66: body_md -->
\label{prop:construction_of_iterated_spans}
    There exists a pullback-preserving fully faithful inclusion  $C\subset C'$, where $C'$ has all pullbacks.

    Furthermore, restricting $\mathbf{Span}^2(C')$ to objects in $C$, $1$-morphisms in $\mathrm{Span}(C,C_R)$ and $2$-morphisms as described above defines a  $(\infty,2)$-subcategory \[\mathbf{Span}^2(C,C_R)^{C}_{C_R}\subset \mathbf{Span}^2(C').\]
<!-- end proposition-66 -->
<!-- proof-113: body_md -->
For the existence of $C'$, take, for example, the Yoneda embedding.

    For the second part, the construction of $\mathbf{Span}^2(C,E)_{P,I}$ described in \cite[Construction 4.12]{CLLuniv} works in this situation as well.
<!-- end proof-113 -->
<!-- proposition-67: body_md -->
\label{construction_of_span_2_as_a_functor_on_span_pairs}
    The construction 
    \[(C,C_R)\mapsto \mathbf{Span}^2(C,C_R)^{C}_{C_R}\]
    assembles into a limit-preserving functor
    \[\operatorname{SpanPairs}\to \operatorname{2Cat}.\]
<!-- end proposition-67 -->
<!-- proof-114: body_md -->
We first explain the functoriality. Take $C'=\operatorname{PSh}(C)$. A morphism of span pairs $F:(C,C_R)\to(D,D_R)$ induces by left Kan extension a functor
    \[
    F_!:\operatorname{PSh}(C)\to\operatorname{PSh}(D)
    \]
    satisfying $F_!\circ \text{\usefont{U}{dmjhira}{m}{n}\symbol{"48}}_C\simeq \text{\usefont{U}{dmjhira}{m}{n}\symbol{"48}}_D\circ F$, where $\text{\usefont{U}{dmjhira}{m}{n}\symbol{"48}}_C$ and $\text{\usefont{U}{dmjhira}{m}{n}\symbol{"48}}_D$ are the Yoneda embeddings. Although $F_!$ need not preserve all pullbacks, it preserves the pullback squares among representables arising from pullbacks along morphisms in $C_R$, since $F$ preserves these pullbacks and the Yoneda embeddings preserve existing limits. Thus, applying $F_!$ to the diagrams defining the restricted iterated span $(\infty,2)$-categories preserves the prescribed markings and all pullbacks used in composition, giving a $2$-functor
    \[
    \mathbf{Span}^2(C,C_R)^C_{C_R}\to\mathbf{Span}^2(D,D_R)^D_{D_R}.
    \]
    The functoriality of left Kan extension makes this construction functorial in span pairs.

    To check that the functor preserves limits, it is enough to check that it preserves limits on spaces of objects, $1$-morphisms and $2$-morphisms. 


                                                                                                                               
    Recall that limits in $\operatorname{SpanPairs}$ are computed in the $\infty$-category $\operatorname{Pairs}$ of pairs of an $\infty$-category and a wide $\infty$-subcategory. 
    The functor sending a span pair $(C,C_R)$ to the space of $2$-morphisms of $\mathbf{Span}^2(C,C_R)^{C}_{C_R}$ can be described as the composition 
    \[\operatorname{SpanPairs}\hookrightarrow \operatorname{Pairs}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{map}((X,X'),-)}\mathrm{Ani}\]
    where $(X,X')$ is the pair of $(1,1)$-categories in which $X$ is the following diagram and $X'$ is the wide $\infty$-subcategory of tailed arrows: 
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
    	& \bullet & \\
    	\bullet & \bullet & \bullet \\
    	& \bullet.
    	\arrow[from=1-2, to=2-1]
    	\arrow[tail, from=1-2, to=2-3]
    	\arrow[from=2-2, to=1-2]
    	\arrow[tail, from=2-2, to=3-2]
    	\arrow[from=3-2, to=2-1]
    	\arrow[tail, from=3-2, to=2-3]
    \end{tikzcd}\]
    Thus it preserves limits.

    The proofs that the functors of $1$-morphisms and of objects are limit-preserving are similar.
<!-- end proof-114 -->
<!-- proposition-68: body_md -->
\label{prop:pullback_describing_span_EfE_times_using_span_2}
    We have a pullback of $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-categories:
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})^\times\ar[r]\ar[d]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        & (\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{2}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})^{\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}}_{\mathsf{E}})_{*//}\ar[d]\\
        {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\ar[r]
        &\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{2}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})^{\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}}_{\mathsf{E}}.
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
<!-- end proposition-68 -->
<!-- proof-115: body_md -->
Consider the composition of pullbacks:
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})^\times\ar[r]\ar[d]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        & \bm{\mathsf{P}}\ar[r]\ar[d]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        &(\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{2}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})^{\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}}_{\mathsf{E}})_{*//}\ar[d]\\
        {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\ar[r]
        &\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{1.5}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})^{\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}}\ar[r]&\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{2}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})^{\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}}_{\mathsf{E}}.
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    The middle vertical map classifies, in the context $A$, the $2$-functor
    \[
    \bm{\mathsf{Span}^{1.5}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})^{\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}}(A) = {\mathbf{Span}^{1.5}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}(A),\mathsf{E}(A))\to {\mathbf{Cat}},
    \]
    sending $B\to A$ to \[\mathrm{Fun}_{\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{2}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})^{\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}}_{\mathsf{E}}(A)}(*,B)\simeq{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})^B(A)\simeq {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})(B).\]
    
    This functor is the unique $2$-functor on ${\mathbf{Span}^{1.5}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}(A),\mathsf{E}(A))$ which arises from the unfurling construction and thus its restriction to ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})$ agrees with the cocartesian fibration classifying the unfurling construction. 
    
    Finally, by definition, the unfurling construction is classified by the cocartesian fibration ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})^\times\to {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})$, proving the claim.
<!-- end proof-115 -->
<!-- proposition-69: body_md -->
The functor 
    \[\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{2}}(\mathsf{D})_{*//} \to \bm{\mathsf{Span}^{2}}(\mathsf{D})\]
    is a $1$-cocartesian fibration of $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-categories.
<!-- end proposition-69 -->
<!-- proof-116: body_md -->
This follows contextwise from \crtCref{example:oplax_slice}.
<!-- end proof-116 -->
<!-- proposition-70: body_md -->
We have a pullback
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
        (\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{2}}(\mathsf{D})_{*//})^{\simeq2}\ar[r]\ar[d]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        &\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{2}}(\mathsf{D})_{*//}\ar[d]\\
        {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{D})\ar[r]
        &\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{2}}(\mathsf{D}).
    \end{tikzcd}\]
    Thus the left-hand arrow is the cocartesian fibration classifying the functor 
    \[{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{D})\to \mathsf{Cat}\]
    sending $X\in {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{D})(A)$ to \[\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}_{\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{2}}(\mathsf{D})}(*,X).\]
<!-- end proposition-70 -->
<!-- proof-117: body_md -->
This follows by the same argument appearing in the proof of \crtCref{prop:univ_internal_2_cocart_fib}.
<!-- end proof-117 -->
<!-- definition-47: body_md -->
Let $\mathsf{Y},\mathsf{X}\subset \mathsf{D}^{\Delta^1}$ denote the following wide $\mathcal{B}$-subcategories. Let $A\in \mathcal{B}$. Then an arrow of $\mathsf{D}^{\Delta^1}(A)$ is a commutative square 
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
        X'\ar[r]\ar[d,"x"] &Y'\ar[d,"y"]\\X\ar[r] & Y
    \end{tikzcd}\]
    viewed as a morphism from the left arrow $x$ to the right arrow $y$.
    
    We let morphisms in $\mathsf{Y}$ be those morphisms which are pullback squares. We let morphisms in $\mathsf{X}$ be those morphisms in which the source component $X'\to Y'$ is an isomorphism.
<!-- end definition-47 -->
<!-- proposition-71: body_md -->
\label{prop:arrow_markings_stable_under_base_change}
    The wide $\mathcal{B}$-subcategories $\mathsf{Y},\mathsf{X}\subset \mathsf{D}^{\Delta^1}$ are stable under base change in $\mathsf{D}^{\Delta^1}$.
<!-- end proposition-71 -->
<!-- proof-118: body_md -->
For $\mathsf{X}$, this follows since isomorphisms are stable under base change in $\mathsf{D}$ and for $\mathsf{Y}$, this follows by the pasting lemma.
<!-- end proof-118 -->
<!-- proposition-72: body_md -->
The functor 
    \[t: \bm{\mathsf{Span}^{2}}(\mathsf{D}^{\Delta^1})^{\mathsf{X}}_{\mathsf{Y}}\to \bm{\mathsf{Span}^{2}}(\mathsf{D})\]
    sending an arrow $x:X'\to X$ to its target $X$ is a $1$-cocartesian fibration of $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-categories.
<!-- end proposition-72 -->
<!-- proof-119: body_md -->
Let $A\in \mathcal{B}$. We first want to show that 
    \[t: \bm{\mathsf{Span}^{2}}(\mathsf{D}^{\Delta^1})^{\mathsf{X}}_{\mathsf{Y}}(A)\to \bm{\mathsf{Span}^{2}}(\mathsf{D})(A)\]
    is a $1$-cocartesian fibration.

    Indeed, for an object $f:X'\to X$ and an arrow in $\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{2}}(\mathsf{D})(A)$ 
    \[X\leftarrow F\to Y,\]
    the cocartesian lifts on underlying $\infty$-categories are of the form
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
    	X' & F' & F' \\
    	X & F & Y.
    	\arrow[from=1-1, to=2-1]
    	\arrow[from=1-2, to=1-1]
    	\arrow[from=1-2, to=1-3,equal]
    	\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125, rotate=-90}, draw=none, from=1-2, to=2-1]
    	\arrow[from=1-2, to=2-2]
    	\arrow[from=1-3, to=2-3]
    	\arrow[from=2-2, to=2-1]
    	\arrow[from=2-2, to=2-3]
    \end{tikzcd}\]

    By \cite[Lemma 3.3]{CLRUniversalityOfUnferling}, if we show that $t$ above is a homwise right fibration, then we get that $t$ is a $1$-cocartesian fibration. This follows since cartesian $2$-morphisms (which are given by opposites of the span of arrows directly above) are the only allowed $2$-morphisms in $\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{2}}(\mathsf{D}^{\Delta^1})^{\mathsf{X}}_{\mathsf{Y}}(A)$.

    We are left to show that change of context preserves cocartesian lifts. This follows since it preserves pullbacks and isomorphisms.
<!-- end proof-119 -->
<!-- proposition-73: body_md -->
\label{prop:description_of_oplax_slice}
    We have an equivalence of cocartesian fibrations of $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-categories 
    \[\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{2}}(\mathsf{D})_{*//} \simeq \bm{\mathsf{Span}^{2}}(\mathsf{D}^{\Delta^1})^{\mathsf{X}}_{\mathsf{Y}}.\]
<!-- end proposition-73 -->
<!-- proof-120: body_md -->
We first show this equivalence in a context $A$.

    Let 
    \[T:\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{2}}(\mathsf{D})(A)\to{\mathbf{Cat}}\] be the $2$-functor classified by $\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{2}}(\mathsf{D}^{\Delta^1})^{\mathsf{X}}_{\mathsf{Y}}$. The $2$-functor classified by $\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{2}}(\mathsf{D})_{*//}$ is $\text{\usefont{U}{dmjhira}{m}{n}\symbol{"48}}(*)$, the $2$-Yoneda embedding of $*$. Then, by the $2$-Yoneda lemma, we have a natural transformation $\text{\usefont{U}{dmjhira}{m}{n}\symbol{"48}}(*) \to T$  determined by the object $*=*$ in $T(*)$.

    In the context $A$, we have that 
    \[T(B) = \mathrm{Span}(\mathsf{D}(A)_{/B}).\]
    The component at $B$ of this natural transformation is the usual equivalence: 
    \[\mathrm{Fun}_{\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{2}}(\mathsf{D})(A)}(*,B)\simeq \mathrm{Span}(\mathsf{D}(A)_{/B}). \]

    By the $2$-categorical unstraightening theorem, we get an equivalence $\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{2}}(\mathsf{D}^{\Delta^1})^{\mathsf{X}}_{\mathsf{Y}}(A)\simeq \bm{\mathsf{Span}^{2}}(\mathsf{D})_{*//}(A)$.

    By naturality of Yoneda, this equivalence is natural as well.
<!-- end proof-120 -->
<!-- corollary-20: body_md -->
\label{cor:square_with_span_of_arrows_and_span_2_exists_for_presh}
    We have a commutative square 
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:diag_of_BC_comp}\begin{tikzcd}
        {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{D}^{\Delta^1})\ar[r]\ar[d]
        & \bm{\mathsf{Span}^{2}}(\mathsf{D})_{*//}\ar[d]\\
        {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{D})\ar[r]
        &\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{2}}(\mathsf{D}).
    \end{tikzcd}\end{equation}
<!-- end corollary-20 -->
<!-- proof-121: body_md -->
By \crtCref{prop:description_of_oplax_slice}, the left-hand functor is the core of the right-hand functor.
<!-- end proof-121 -->
<!-- definition-48: body_md -->
\label{def:span_of_arrows_E}
    Let $\mathsf{Sp}_{\mathsf{E}}^{(1)}\subset {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{D}^{\Delta^1})$ denote the following $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory. In the context $A$, the allowed objects are morphisms \[Y'\rightarrowtail Y\]
    where both $Y$ and $Y'$ are in $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$ and the morphism is in $\mathsf{E}$. The allowed morphisms are spans
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
        Y'\ar[tail,d]
        &X'\ar[d]\ar[tail,r]\ar[l]
        &Z'\ar[tail,d]\\
        Y
        &X\ar[l]\ar[tail,r]
        &Z
    \end{tikzcd}\]
    where $X,X'$ are in $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$ and the tailed morphisms are required to be in $\mathsf{E}$. This defines a $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory since  $(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})$ is a span pair, so the required pullbacks exist in $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$ and are preserved by the Yoneda embedding.
<!-- end definition-48 -->
<!-- remark-18: body_md -->
The $\mathcal{B}$-category $\mathsf{Sp}_{\mathsf{E}}^{(1)}$ need not be a span $\mathcal{B}$-category of any sub-adequate triplet of $(\mathsf{D}^{\Delta^1},\mathsf{D}^{\Delta^1},\mathsf{D}^{\Delta^1})$. Indeed, the arrows in the roof of the spans are more general objects of ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{D}^{\Delta^1})$ than the objects of  $\mathsf{Sp}_{\mathsf{E}}^{(1)}$ so that there is no appropriate factorization system of left-pointing and right-pointing maps.
<!-- end remark-18 -->
<!-- corollary-21: body_md -->
\label{cor:square_with_span_of_arrows_and_span_2_exists}
    The commutative diagram of \crtCref{cor:square_with_span_of_arrows_and_span_2_exists_for_presh} restricts to a pullback square: 
    \begin{equation} \label{eq:diag_of_BC_comp_restricted}\begin{tikzcd}
        \mathsf{Sp}_{\mathsf{E}}^{(1)}\ar[r]\ar[d]
        & (\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{2}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})^{\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}}_{\mathsf{E}})_{*//}\ar[d]\\
        {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\ar[r]
        &\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{2}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})^{\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}}_{\mathsf{E}}.
    \end{tikzcd}\end{equation}
<!-- end corollary-21 -->
<!-- proof-122: body_md -->
To check that the square exists, we need to check that each object, each morphism and each $2$-morphism in each of the $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-categories is sent by each arrow to the $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-subcategory in the target. We will only show that the upper morphism is well-defined\footnote{In fact, all other checks are subsumed in this one.}.

    Let
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:diag_of_morph_in_sp_1}\begin{tikzcd}
        Y'\ar[tail,d]
        &X'\ar[d]\ar[tail,r]\ar[l]
        &Z'\ar[tail,d]\\
        Y
        &X\ar[l]\ar[tail,r]
        &Z
    \end{tikzcd}\end{equation}
    be a morphism in $\mathsf{Sp}_{\mathsf{E}}^{(1)}$. The upper arrow in \crtCref{eq:diag_of_BC_comp} sends this morphism to the arrow
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:diag_of_morph_inlax_slice_of_sp_2}\begin{tikzcd}
    	{*} && {Y'} && Y \\
    	&&& {Y'\times_YX} \\
    	{*} && X' && X \\
    	& {Z'} \\
    	{*} && {Z'} && Z.
    	\arrow[from=1-3, to=1-1]
    	\arrow[tail, from=1-3, to=1-5]
    	\arrow[from=2-4, to=1-3]
    	\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125, rotate=90}, draw=none, from=2-4, to=1-5]
    	\arrow[from=2-4, to=3-5]
    	\arrow[equal, from=3-1, to=1-1]
    	\arrow[equal, from=3-1, to=5-1]
    	\arrow[from=3-3, to=2-4]
    	\arrow[tail, from=3-3, to=4-2]
    	\arrow[from=3-5, to=1-5]
    	\arrow[tail, from=3-5, to=5-5]
    	\arrow[from=4-2, to=3-1]
    	\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125, rotate=-90}, draw=none, from=4-2, to=5-1]
    	\arrow[equal, from=4-2, to=5-3]
    	\arrow[from=5-3, to=5-1]
    	\arrow[tail, from=5-3, to=5-5]
    \end{tikzcd}\end{equation}
    
    
    We now check  that the  square \crtCref{eq:diag_of_BC_comp_restricted} is a pullback square. Since $\mathsf{Sp}_{\mathsf{E}}^{(1)}$ is a sheaf of $\infty$-categories, it is enough to check this contextwise on the anima of objects and morphisms. The statement about objects is trivial. 

    Note that in \crtCref{eq:diag_of_BC_comp_restricted} the lower horizontal functor is the inclusion of the maximal $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory. Thus we only need to show in every context $A$ that the upper morphism gives an equivalence on the anima of $1$-morphisms.

    The anima of $1$-morphisms in $\mathsf{Sp}_{\mathsf{E}}^{(1)}(A)$ is equivalent to the anima of diagrams as in \crtCref{eq:diag_of_morph_in_sp_1}. The anima of $1$-morphisms in $(\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{2}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})^{\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}}_{\mathsf{E}})_{*//}(A)$ is equivalent to the anima of diagrams as in \crtCref{eq:diag_of_morph_inlax_slice_of_sp_2}, that is, the anima of diagrams of the shape in \crtCref{eq:diag_of_morph_inlax_slice_of_sp_2} in $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}(A)$ such that the morphisms denoted by $=$ are isomorphisms, the objects denoted by $*$ are terminal and the marked squares in the corners are pullbacks.
    The morphism between these animae described above is clearly an equivalence.
<!-- end proof-122 -->
<!-- proposition-74: body_md -->
\label{prop:span_operad_as_spans_of_arrows}
    There is an equivalence of cocartesian fibrations
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
        \mathsf{Sp}_{\mathsf{E}}^{(1)}\ar[r,"\sim"]\ar[d]
        &{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})^{\times}\ar[d]\\
        {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\ar[r, equal] & {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}).
    \end{tikzcd}\]
<!-- end proposition-74 -->
<!-- proof-123: body_md -->
By \crtCref{eq:diag_of_BC_comp_restricted}, it is enough to show that ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})^\times$ sits in the following pullback:
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
        {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})^\times \ar[r]\ar[d]
        & (\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{2}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})^{\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}}_{\mathsf{E}})_{*//}\ar[d]\\
        {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\ar[r]
        &\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{2}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})^{\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}}_{\mathsf{E}}.
    \end{tikzcd}\]

    This was shown in \crtCref{prop:pullback_describing_span_EfE_times_using_span_2}.
<!-- end proof-123 -->
<!-- proposition-75: body_md -->
\label{prop:description_of_mu_for_span}
    The composition 
    \[\mathsf{Sp}_{\mathsf{E}}^{(1)}\simeq {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})^\times\xrightarrow{\mu} {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\]
    is equivalent to the source functor 
    \[s: \mathsf{Sp}_{\mathsf{E}}^{(1)}\to{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\]
    sending $(X'\rightarrowtail X)\mapsto X'$.
<!-- end proposition-75 -->
<!-- proof-124: body_md -->
Both $s$ and $\mu$ were constructed by sending an arrow to its source. The equivalence above is immediate from those constructions.
<!-- end proof-124 -->
<!-- corollary-22: body_md -->
\label{cor:s_and_mu_compatibility_diagram}
    There is a commutative diagram 
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
        &\mathsf{E}^\otimes\ar[dd,hook]\ar[dr,"s"]\\
        {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\ar[ru,"r"]\ar[dr,"\tau"']
        &&{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\\
        &{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})^\times\ar[ru,"\mu"']
    \end{tikzcd}\]
<!-- end corollary-22 -->
<!-- proof-125: body_md -->
Since $\mathsf{E}\subset {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})$ is an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory, we have a functor $\mathsf{E}^\otimes \hookrightarrow {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})^\times$ which is an inclusion of a $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory.

    In \crtCref{cor:description_of_the_env_of_triv} we showed that morphisms in $\mathsf{E}^\otimes$ are given by diagrams of the form
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
        Y'\ar[tail,d]
        &X'\ar[tail,d]\ar[tail,r]\ar[l]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125, rotate=-90}, draw=none, dl]
        &Z'\ar[tail,d]\\
        Y
        &X\ar[l]\ar[tail, r]
        &Z.
    \end{tikzcd}\]
    Morphisms in ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})^\times$ are given by diagrams as in \crtCref{eq:diag_of_morph_in_sp_1}, and the inclusion sends a diagram above to itself. Thus we get the commutativity of the right triangle from \crtCref{prop:description_of_mu_for_span}.
    
     The commutativity of the left triangle was the definition of $\tau$.
<!-- end proof-125 -->
<!-- corollary-23: body_md -->
\label{cor:associated_operad_total_category_complete}
    Let $F:{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}) \to \mathsf{Cat}$ be an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category with $\mathsf{C}= F(*)$. Then $\mathsf{C}^\otimes := \mathsf{Un}(F)$ is $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-complete and the classifying cocartesian fibration $\mathsf{C}^\otimes\to {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})$ is $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-continuous. Moreover, the $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory of $\mathsf{C}^\otimes$ spanned by cocartesian edges is closed under $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-limits.
<!-- end corollary-23 -->
<!-- proof-126: body_md -->
The pullback
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
        \mathsf{C}^\otimes\ar[r]\ar[d]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr] & \mathsf{Cat}_{*//}\ar[d]\\
        {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\ar[r] & \mathsf{Cat}
    \end{tikzcd}\]
    is a pullback of $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-complete $\mathcal{B}$-categories along $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-continuous functors. Thus it can be computed in $\mathsf{Cat}$ since the functor $\mathsf{Cat}^{\mathsf{E}-\sqcap}\to \mathsf{Cat}$ is continuous.
<!-- end proof-126 -->
<!-- corollary-24: body_md -->
\label{cor:unst_of_monoidal_functor_is_monoidal}
    Let $\mathsf{J}$ be an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category and let $F:\mathsf{J}\to \mathsf{Cat}$ be an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functor where the target is equipped with the cartesian $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal structure. Then $\mathsf{Un}(F)$ carries a natural $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal structure such that the unstraightening functor $\mathsf{Un}(F)\to \mathsf{J}$ is $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal. Moreover, the $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory of $\mathsf{Un}(F)$ spanned by cocartesian edges is an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory.
<!-- end corollary-24 -->
<!-- proof-127: body_md -->
The forgetful functor ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})\to \mathsf{Cat}$ preserves pullbacks, and since $\mathsf{Cat}_{*//}\to \mathsf{Cat}$ preserves $\mathsf{E}$-limits, its base change to $\mathsf{J}$ along $F$ is $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal.
<!-- end proof-127 -->
<!-- lemma-14: body_md -->
\label{lem:mu_is_equifibed_for_univ_unst}
    Let $\mathsf{Cat}_{*//}\to \mathsf{Cat}$ be the universal cocartesian fibration. Then the commutative naturality square
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        (\mathsf{Cat}_{*//})^\times\ar[r,"\mu"]\ar[d]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        &\mathsf{Cat}_{*//}\ar[d]\\
        \mathsf{Cat}^\times\ar[r,"\mu"']
        &\mathsf{Cat}
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    is cartesian.
<!-- end lemma-14 -->
<!-- proof-128: body_md -->
To show that a square of $\mathcal{B}$-categories is cartesian, it is enough to check that for each $A\in \mathcal{B}$, the functors ${\mathsf{map}}(A, -)$ and ${\mathsf{map}}(A\times \Delta^1, - )$ send it to cartesian squares in $\mathcal{B}$. 

    Let $A\in \mathcal{B}$. A functor $A\to \mathsf{Cat}_{*//}$ classifies a $\mathcal{B}_{/A}$-category $\mathsf{D}$ and an object $x:A\to \mathsf{D}$. A functor $A\to \mathsf{Cat}^\times$ classifies an object $[\pi_B:B\to A]\in {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})(A)$ and a $\mathcal{B}_{/B}$-category $\mathsf{C}$. Thus, an object in the pullback classifies a $\mathcal{B}_{/A}$-category $\mathsf{D}$, a $\mathcal{B}_{/B}$-category $\mathsf{C}$, an isomorphism $(\pi_B)_*\mathsf{C}\simeq \mathsf{D}$ and an object $x:A\to \mathsf{D}$. The data of an object $x$ correspond uniquely to the data of an object $y:B\to \mathsf{C}$. Thus we get that mapping from $A$ to the pullback amounts to giving $[\pi_B:B\to A]$, $\mathsf{C}$, and $y:B\to \mathsf{C}$. This is exactly the data of an object in $\mathsf{Cat}_{*//}^\times(A)$.

    Next, we must show that ${\mathsf{map}}(A\times \Delta^1, - )$ sends our square to a cartesian square in $\mathcal{B}$. This is achieved by a similar argument.
<!-- end proof-128 -->
<!-- proposition-76: body_md -->
The inclusion
    \[\left\{*\right\}\to {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\]
    can be given the structure of a lax $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functor
    \[\tau:{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\to {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})^\times.\]
<!-- end proposition-76 -->
<!-- proof-129: body_md -->
We have a natural inclusion of an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory
    \[\mathsf{E}\hookrightarrow {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}).\]
    Thus, it is enough to give $*\hookrightarrow \mathsf{E}$ the structure of a lax $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functor. Recall the morphism of $\mathsf{E}$-operads
    \[
    r:{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\hookrightarrow \mathsf{E}^\otimes.
    \]
    This morphism classifies a lax monoidal structure for the functor $\left\{*\right\}\hookrightarrow \mathsf{E}$.

    Hence we get that the composition of morphisms of $\mathsf{E}$-operads
    \[
    {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\xrightarrow{r} \mathsf{E}^\otimes\to {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})^\times
    \]
    gives the desired result.
<!-- end proof-129 -->
<!-- proposition-77: body_md -->
\label{prop:s_and_mu_compatibility_diagram}
    There is a commutative diagram 
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
        &\mathsf{E}^\otimes\ar[dd,hook, "i"]\ar[dr,"s"]\\
        {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\ar[ru,"r"]\ar[dr,"\tau"']
        &&{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\\
