        &{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})^\times\ar[ru,"\mu"']
    \end{tikzcd}\]
<!-- end proposition-77 -->
<!-- corollary-25: body_md -->
The composition 
    \[{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\xrightarrow{\tau} {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})^\times\xrightarrow{\mu}{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}) \]
    is homotopic to the identity.
<!-- end corollary-25 -->
<!-- proof-130: body_md -->
Consider the following isomorphism:
    \[\mathrm{id} \simeq s\circ r \simeq \mu\circ i \circ r \simeq \mu\circ \tau.\]
<!-- end proof-130 -->
<!-- proposition-78: body_md -->
There exists a canonical pullback diagram 
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
        \mathsf{C}^\otimes \ar[r,"\tau_{\mathsf{C}}"]\ar[d]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        &(\mathsf{C}^\otimes)^\times\ar[d]\\
        {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\ar[r,"\tau"]
        &{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})^\times,
    \end{tikzcd}\]
    natural in $\mathsf{C}$, and the upper functor $\tau_{\mathsf{C}}$ is a morphism of $\mathsf{E}$-operads.
<!-- end proposition-78 -->
<!-- proof-131: body_md -->
Let \[F:{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\to\mathsf{Cat}\] denote the functor defining the $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal structure of $\mathsf{C}$.

    Consider the following pasting of pullbacks of $\mathcal{B}$-categories:
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
        \mathsf{P}\ar[r]\ar[d]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        &(\mathsf{C}^\otimes)^\times \ar[r]\ar[d]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        &\mathsf{Cat}_{*//}^\times \ar[r,"\mu"]\ar[d]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        &\mathsf{Cat}_{*//}\ar[d]\\
        {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\ar[r,"\tau"]
        &{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})^\times\ar[r,"F^\times"]
        &\mathsf{Cat}^\times\ar[r,"\mu"]
        &\mathsf{Cat}.
    \end{tikzcd}\]
    The right square is the pullback square described in \crtCref{lem:mu_is_equifibed_for_univ_unst}.
    The middle square is obtained by applying $(-)^\times$ to the pullback square defining $\mathsf{C}^\otimes$. The left square is defined as the pullback as written. 
    
    We claim that $\mathsf{P}\simeq \mathsf{C}^\otimes$ and so the promised pullback is the left square. 
    
    To check this, it is enough to verify that the lower composition is homotopic to $F$. Indeed, this follows since 
    \[\mu\circ F^\times \circ \tau \simeq F\circ \mu \circ \tau \simeq F\circ \mathrm{id} \simeq F.\]

    The morphism $\tau_{\mathsf{C}}$ is a morphism of operads since $\tau$ is.

    Lastly, we need to check that $\tau_{\mathsf{C}}$ is natural, but this follows since all the ingredients in its construction are functorial.
<!-- end proof-131 -->
<!-- theorem-21: body_md -->
\label{thm:C_otimes_res_to_E_is_envelope}
    The functor $\iota_{\mathsf{C}}$ is an inclusion of an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory, participating in a pullback of $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-categories:
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
        \mathsf{env}(\mathsf{C}^\otimes)\ar[r,"\iota_{\mathsf{C}}"]\ar[d]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        &\mathsf{C}^\otimes\ar[d]\\
        \mathsf{E}\ar[r]
        &{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}).
    \end{tikzcd}\]
<!-- end theorem-21 -->
<!-- proof-132: body_md -->
Any $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functor which is an inclusion of a $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory is canonically an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal equivalence with the $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory spanned by its image. Thus the existence of a pullback square as in the statement of the theorem will imply the first statement.

    The square in the statement of the theorem is the naturality square of $\iota$ applied to the canonical $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functor $\mathsf{C}\to *$. Since the functor 
    \[(-)^\otimes:{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})\to \mathsf{Op}\] is a conservative right adjoint, it suffices to show that the square is cartesian after applying $(-)^\otimes$.
    
    Consider the following diagram:
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
        \mathsf{env}(\mathsf{C}^\otimes)^\otimes && (\mathsf{C}^\otimes)^\times && \mathsf{C}^\otimes & \\
        &&& \mathsf{Cat}_{*//}^\times && \mathsf{Cat}_{*//} \\
        \mathsf{E}^\otimes && {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})^\times && {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}) \\
        &&& \mathsf{Cat}^\times && \mathsf{Cat}.
        \arrow[from=1-1, to=1-3]
        \arrow[from=1-1, to=3-1]
        \arrow[from=1-3, to=1-5]
        \arrow[from=1-3, to=2-4]
        \arrow[from=1-3, to=3-3]
        \arrow[from=1-5, to=2-6]
        \arrow[from=1-5, to=3-5]
        \arrow[from=3-3, to=3-5]
        \arrow[from=2-4, to=2-6, crossing over]
        \arrow[from=2-4, to=4-4, crossing over]
        \arrow[from=2-6, to=4-6]
        \arrow[from=3-1, to=3-3]
        \arrow[from=3-3, to=4-4]
        \arrow[from=3-5, to=4-6]
        \arrow[from=4-4, to=4-6]
    \end{tikzcd}\]
    We wish to show first that the back square of the cube is cartesian. This follows since, as we showed before, the front face is cartesian as well as the right and left faces.

    The outer rectangle at the back is the cartesian square defining $\mathsf{env}(\mathsf{C}^\otimes)^\otimes$. Thus, by the pasting lemma, the left square is cartesian, and so is the square in the statement of the theorem.
<!-- end proof-132 -->
<!-- proposition-79: body_md -->
\label{prop:lax_E_monoidal_unst}
    Let 
    \[F:\mathsf{C}\to \mathsf{Cat}\]
    be a lax $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functor. Then the unstraightening $\mathsf{Un}(F)\to \mathsf{C}$ is canonically an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functor of $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-categories.
<!-- end proposition-79 -->
<!-- proof-133: body_md -->
Let us consider the following pullback of $\mathsf{E}$-operads
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
    \mathsf{P}\ar[r]\ar[d]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
    &(\mathsf{Cat}_{*//})^\times\ar[d]\\
    \mathsf{C}^{\otimes}\ar[r]&\mathsf{Cat}^\times.    
    \end{tikzcd}\]
    
    The right-hand functor is a cocartesian fibration, and so is the left-hand functor. Thus, the composition  $\mathsf{P}\to \mathsf{C}^{\otimes}\to {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})$ is a composition of cocartesian fibrations and the arrow  $\mathsf{P}\to \mathsf{C}^{\otimes}$ preserves cocartesian lifts.

    Thus $\mathsf{P}$ classifies an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal structure on $\mathsf{Un}(F)$ and the functor $\mathsf{P}\to \mathsf{C}^{\otimes}$ classifies an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functor.
<!-- end proof-133 -->
<!-- example-17: body_md -->
\label{ex:lax_unstraightening_recovers_monoidal_structure}
    Let $\mathsf{C}$ be an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category. Then consider the following composition
    \[*\hookrightarrow \mathsf{E}\hookrightarrow {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}) \to \mathsf{Cat}.\]
    This composition chooses the $\mathcal{B}$-category $\mathsf{C}$. The composition above has a canonical structure of a lax $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functor. We get that the unstraightening is $\mathsf{C}$ with its original $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal structure.
<!-- end example-17 -->
<!-- proof-134: body_md -->
Let us consider the following pasting of pullbacks of operads:
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
        \mathsf{P}\ar[r]\ar[d]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        &\mathsf{env}(\mathsf{C}^{\otimes})^{\otimes}\ar[r]\ar[d]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        &(\mathsf{Cat}_{*//})^{\times}\ar[d]\\
        {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}) \ar[r,"r"] 
        &\mathsf{E}^\otimes \ar[r]
        &\mathsf{Cat}^\times.
    \end{tikzcd}\]
    The bottom composition is the composition of morphisms of operads classifying the lax $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functor described as the composition in the example above.

    The right square is a pullback by \crtCref{thm:C_otimes_res_to_E_is_envelope}. The left square computes the same pullback as the left square appearing in \crtCref{prop:eta_is_a_morphism_of_preoperads}.

    Thus, $\mathsf{P}$ is canonically isomorphic to $\mathsf{C}^\otimes$, proving the claim.
<!-- end proof-134 -->
<!-- definition-49: body_md -->
\label{def:E_monoidal_two_categories}
    We define $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-categories as $\mathsf{E}$-monoids in ${\mathsf{2Cat}}$.
    We define the $\mathcal{B}$-category of $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-categories as  ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}({\mathsf{2Cat}})$.

    The $\mathcal{B}$-category ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}({\mathsf{2Cat}})$ has a canonical structure of a $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-category $\bm{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\bm{\mathsf{2Cat}})$ since \[\bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}({\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}),\bm{\mathsf{2Cat}})\]
    is a $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-category and ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}({\mathsf{2Cat}})$ is a full $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory of its core.  

    We denote by $\mathbf{2Cat}^{\mathsf{E}-\otimes}(\mathcal{B})$ the $(\infty,2)$-category of global sections of this $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-categorical refinement of ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}({\mathsf{2Cat}})$.
<!-- end definition-49 -->
<!-- example-18: body_md -->
\label{ex:cartesian_monoidal_two_category}
    Let $\bm{\mathsf{X}}$ be an $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-$2$-complete $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-category. Then $\bm{\mathsf{X}}$ has a canonical structure of an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-category $\mathsf{Cart}_{\otimes}(\bm{\mathsf{X}})$, which we call the cartesian structure. 
    
    The construction is as follows. $\bm{\mathsf{X}}$ determines a unique $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-continuous functor
    \[ (\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}})^{\mathrm{op}}\to \bm{\mathsf{2Cat}} \]
    which is $\mathsf{E}$-right adjointable.
    Thus we get a canonical functor of $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-categories
    \[\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{1.5}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\to \bm{\mathsf{2Cat}}.\]
    We restrict this functor to a functor 
    \[{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\to {\mathsf{2Cat}}.\]
    Since this functor extends an $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-continuous functor from $(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}})^{\mathrm{op}}$, it determines an $\mathsf{E}$-monoid in ${\mathsf{2Cat}}$ by \crtCref{prop:limits_in_span_E_are_computed_in_E_op}.

    This construction gives rise to a functor of $\infty$-categories 
    \[\mathsf{Cart}_{\otimes}:\operatorname{2Cat}(\mathcal{B})^{\mathsf{E}-2\sqcap}\to \mathrm{CMon}^{\mathsf{E}}({\mathsf{2Cat}}).\]
<!-- end example-18 -->
<!-- proposition-80: body_md -->
The functor $\mathsf{Cart}_{\otimes}$ preserves all limits and is conservative.
<!-- end proposition-80 -->
<!-- proof-135: body_md -->
We have a commutative triangle:
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
        \operatorname{2Cat}(\mathcal{B})^{\mathsf{E}-2\sqcap} \ar[dr]\ar[rr]
        && \mathrm{CMon}^{\mathsf{E}}({\mathsf{2Cat}})\ar[dl]\\
        &\operatorname{2Cat}(\mathcal{B}).
    \end{tikzcd}\]
    The downward-pointing morphisms are both conservative and preserve limits. Thus the horizontal morphism is also conservative and preserves limits.
<!-- end proof-135 -->
<!-- proposition-81: body_md -->
\label{prop:monoidal_two_unstraightening}
    Let $F:\bm{\mathsf{C}}\to \mathsf{Cart}_\otimes(\bm{\mathsf{Cat}})$ be an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functor. Then $\bm{\mathsf{Un}}(F)$ carries a natural $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal structure.

    Moreover, if $F$ is given by applying $\mathsf{Cart}_\otimes$ to a $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-$2$-continuous functor, then $\bm{\mathsf{Un}}(F)$ is $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-$2$-complete and the $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal structure agrees with the cartesian one.
<!-- end proposition-81 -->
<!-- proof-136: body_md -->
Recall that the following pullback defines $\bm{\mathsf{Un}}(F)$ as a $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-category:
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
    \bm{\mathsf{Un}}(F)\ar[r]\ar[d]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr] & \bm{\mathsf{Cat}}_{*//}\ar[d]\\
    \bm{\mathsf{C}}\ar[r] & \bm{\mathsf{Cat}}.
    \end{tikzcd}\]
    If $F$ is $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal, then this pullback can be taken in $\mathrm{CMon}^{\mathsf{E}}({\mathsf{2Cat}})$. If $F$ is $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-$2$-continuous, then the pullback can be taken in $\operatorname{2Cat}(\mathcal{B})^{\mathsf{E}-2\sqcap}$.
<!-- end proof-136 -->
<!-- proposition-82: body_md -->
Let $\bm{\mathsf{C}}$ be an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-category. Then $\bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\Delta^1, \bm{\mathsf{C}})$ carries a canonical $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal structure such that both \[s,t:\bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\Delta^1, \bm{\mathsf{C}})\to \bm{\mathsf{C}}\]
    are $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functors.
<!-- end proposition-82 -->
<!-- proof-137: body_md -->
This follows since 
    \[{\mathsf{2Cat}}\xrightarrow{\bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\Delta^1, -)}{\mathsf{2Cat}}\] is $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-continuous and thus induces a functor  
    \[{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}({\mathsf{2Cat}})\xrightarrow{\bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\Delta^1, -)}{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}({\mathsf{2Cat}}).\]
<!-- end proof-137 -->
<!-- definition-50: body_md -->
Let $F,G:\bm{\mathsf{C}}\to \bm{\mathsf{D}}$ be two $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functors of $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-categories. We define an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal lax natural transformation $\alpha:F\to G$ as an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functor  \[T:\bm{\mathsf{C}}\to \bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\Delta^1,\bm{\mathsf{D}})\] together with identifications of $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functors $s\circ T \simeq F,  t\circ T\simeq G$.
<!-- end definition-50 -->
<!-- proposition-83: body_md -->
\label{prop:monoidal_unstraightening_of_lax_transformation}
    Let $F,G:\bm{\mathsf{C}}\to \bm{\mathsf{Cat}}$ be two $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functors, and let $\alpha:F\to G$ be an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal lax natural transformation. Then the functor $\bm{\mathsf{Un}}(\alpha):\bm{\mathsf{Un}}(F)\to \bm{\mathsf{Un}}(G)$ coming from \crtCref{cor:extra_functoriality_of_unst} is canonically an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functor.
<!-- end proposition-83 -->
<!-- proof-138: body_md -->
It is enough to show this for the universal case, where it was proven in \crtCref{thm:univ_unst_of_lax_natural_transformation_is_E_monoidal}.
<!-- end proof-138 -->
<!-- definition-51: body_md -->
\label{def:lax_monoidal_lax_natural_transformation}
    Let $\mathsf{C}$ be an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category and let $\bm{\mathsf{D}}$ be an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-category.
    Let $F,G:\mathsf{C}\to \bm{\mathsf{D}}^{\simeq2}$ be two lax $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functors of $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-categories. We define a lax $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal lax natural transformation $\alpha:F\to G$ as a morphism of $\mathsf{E}$-operads  \[T:\mathsf{C}^{\otimes}\to (\bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\Delta^1,\bm{\mathsf{D}})^{\simeq2})^{\otimes}\] together with identifications of lax $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functors $s\circ T \simeq F,  t\circ T\simeq G$.
<!-- end definition-51 -->
<!-- proposition-84: body_md -->
\label{prop:unst_of_lax_E_monoidal_lax_natural_transformation}
    Let $F,G:\mathsf{C}\to \bm{\mathsf{Cat}}$ be two lax $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functors, and let $\alpha:F\to G$ be a lax $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal lax natural transformation. Then the functor $\mathsf{Un}(\alpha):\mathsf{Un}(F)\to \mathsf{Un}(G)$ coming from \crtCref{cor:extra_functoriality_of_unst} is a lax $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functor.
<!-- end proposition-84 -->
<!-- proof-139: body_md -->
Consider the following pasting in $\mathsf{Op}^{\mathsf{E}}$:
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        \mathsf{Un}(F)^{\otimes}\ar[r]\ar[d]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        &(\bm{\mathsf{Un}}(s)^{\simeq2})^{\otimes}\ar[d]\\
        \mathsf{Un}(G)^{\otimes}\ar[r]\ar[d]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        &(\bm{\mathsf{Un}}(t)^{\simeq2})^{\otimes}\ar[d]\\
        \mathsf{C}^{\otimes} \ar[r]
        &(\bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\Delta^1,\bm{\mathsf{Cat}})^{\simeq2})^{\otimes}.
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    The upper left vertical functor encodes a lax $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functor $\mathsf{Un}(\alpha):\mathsf{Un}(F)\to \mathsf{Un}(G)$.
<!-- end proof-139 -->
<!-- definition-52: body_md -->
Let $\mathsf{E}\subset \mathsf{\Omega}$ be a context-free subuniverse and let $\mathsf{I}\subset\mathsf{E}$ be another context-free subuniverse. 
    Let $A\in \mathcal{B}$. Recall from \crtCref{def:free_on_A_with_E_colimits} that $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}[A]\subset\mathsf{PSh}(A)$ is the free $\mathsf{E}$-cocomplete $\mathcal{B}$-category on $A$. We endow it, using \crtCref{prop:categories_with_E_colimits_have_E_monoidal_structure}, with an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal structure. Recall that in the context $B$, a morphism in $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}[A](B)^{\Delta^1}$ consists of the following data: a morphism $D\to C$  with commuting arbitrary morphisms to $A$ and commuting morphisms in $\mathsf{E}$ to $B$ (see \crtCref{fig:morphism_in_E_A}).
    
    Let $\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}}[A]\subset \mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}[A]$ denote the wide $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory with morphisms in $\mathsf{I}$. That is, $D\to C \in \mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}[A](B)^{\Delta^1}$ over $A$ is in $\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}}[A](B)$ if and only if $(D\to C)\in \mathsf{I}(C)$.
<!-- end definition-52 -->
<!-- proposition-85: body_md -->
$\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}}[A]\subset \mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}[A]$ is an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory.
<!-- end proposition-85 -->
<!-- proof-140: body_md -->
The $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal structure of $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}[A]$ is given by change of context. The question of whether $D\to C$ is in $\mathsf{I}$ is independent of the context.
<!-- end proof-140 -->
<!-- proposition-86: body_md -->
\label{prop:E_I_is_cocart}
    Assume $\mathsf{I}$ is inductible. Then
    $\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}}[A]$ is an $\mathsf{I}$-cocartesian $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category.
<!-- end proposition-86 -->
<!-- proof-141: body_md -->
It is straightforward to verify that $\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}}[A]\subset \mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}[A]$ preserves $\mathsf{I}$-colimits, and thus the criterion of \crtCref{cor:critiria_for_amby} is automatic.
<!-- end proof-141 -->
<!-- definition-53: body_md -->
Let $\mathsf{C}$ be an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category. Let $(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_L,\mathsf{C}_R)$ be an adequate triplet of $\mathcal{B}$-categories. We say that $(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_L,\mathsf{C}_R)$ is an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal adequate triplet if $\mathsf{C}_L,\mathsf{C}_R\subset \mathsf{C}$ are $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-subcategories, and if for each $p:C\to B\in \mathsf{E}(A)$, the functor of $\mathcal{B}_{/A}$-categories $p_\otimes:\mathsf{C}^C\to \mathsf{C}^B$ induces a morphism of adequate triplets
    \[(\mathsf{C}^C,\mathsf{C}_L^C,\mathsf{C}_R^C)\to (\mathsf{C}^B,\mathsf{C}_L^B,\mathsf{C}_R^B).\]
<!-- end definition-53 -->
<!-- proposition-87: body_md -->
\label{prop:E_monoidal_span_cats}
    Let $(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_L,\mathsf{C}_R)$ be an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal adequate triplet. Then ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_L,\mathsf{C}_R)$ carries a natural $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal structure.
<!-- end proposition-87 -->
<!-- proof-142: body_md -->
By the proof of \crtCref{prop:monoidal_subcategories_are_monoidal}, we get that $(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_L,\mathsf{C}_R)$ determines an $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-continuous functor \[{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\to \mathsf{AdTrip}\] which we can post-compose with ${\mathsf{Span}}$.
<!-- end proof-142 -->
<!-- proposition-88: body_md -->
\label{prop:E_monoidal_span_subcats}
    In the situation of \crtCref{prop:E_monoidal_span_cats}, if $\mathsf{C}_L'\subset \mathsf{C}_L,\mathsf{C}_R'\subset\mathsf{C}_R$ are wide $\mathcal{B}$-subcategories such that $(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_L',\mathsf{C}_R')$ is another $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal adequate triplet, then ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_L',\mathsf{C}_R')\subset {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}_L,\mathsf{C}_R)$ is an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory in the sense that it satisfies the universal property of \crtCref{prop:monoidal_subcategories_are_monoidal}.
<!-- end proposition-88 -->
<!-- proof-143: body_md -->
This is immediate from the construction.
<!-- end proof-143 -->
<!-- definition-54: body_md -->
\label{def:span_EPI_A}
    We denote \[{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})[A]:={\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}[A],\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}}[A],\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}}[A]).\]
<!-- end definition-54 -->
<!-- proposition-89: body_md -->
\label{prop:span_EPI_A_is_monoidal}
    Let $\mathsf{I},\mathsf{P}\subset \mathsf{E}$ be two inductible context-free subuniverses. Then ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})[A]$
    is an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category.
<!-- end proposition-89 -->
<!-- proof-144: body_md -->
This is a direct application of \crtCref{prop:E_monoidal_span_subcats}.
<!-- end proof-144 -->
<!-- proposition-90: body_md -->
\label{prop:span_EPI_A_is_ambidextrous}
    ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})[A]$ is $(\mathsf{P,I})$-ambidextrous.
<!-- end proposition-90 -->
<!-- proof-145: body_md -->
${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})[A]$ is $\mathsf{I}$-cocomplete and $\mathsf{P}$-complete by the same argument as in \crtCref{prop:limits_in_span_E}. Moreover, the inclusion $\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}}[A]^{\mathrm{op}}\hookrightarrow {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})[A]$ is $\mathsf{P}^{\operatorname{full}}$-continuous and the inclusion $\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}}[A]\hookrightarrow {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})[A]$ is $\mathsf{I}^{\operatorname{full}}$-cocontinuous.
    
    Thus the criterion of \crtCref{cor:critiria_for_amby} applies, since it can be checked in $\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}}[A]^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}}[A]$.
<!-- end proof-145 -->
<!-- proposition-91: body_md -->
\label{prop:E_monoidal_span_two_cats}
    Let $(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}')$ be an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal span pair. Then $\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{1.5}}(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}')$ carries a natural $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal structure.
<!-- end proposition-91 -->
<!-- proof-146: body_md -->
The proof of \crtCref{prop:E_monoidal_span_cats} works in this case as well.
<!-- end proof-146 -->
<!-- proposition-92: body_md -->
\label{prop:univ_prop_of_E_monoidal_span_half}
    We have an equivalence of $\infty$-categories
    \[\mathrm{Fun}_{\mathbf{2Cat}^{\mathsf{E}-\otimes}(\mathcal{B})}^{\otimes,\mathsf{C}'\operatorname{-radj}}(\mathsf{C}^{\mathrm{op}},\bm{\mathsf{D}})\simeq \mathrm{Fun}_{\mathbf{2Cat}^{\mathsf{E}-\otimes}(\mathcal{B})}^{\otimes}(\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{1.5}}(\mathsf{C},\mathsf{C}'),\bm{\mathsf{D}}).\]
<!-- end proposition-92 -->
<!-- proof-147: body_md -->
This follows from applying the universal property of \crtCref{prop:univ_prop_of_span_half} pointwise.
<!-- end proof-147 -->
<!-- assumption-1: body_md -->
\label{assumption:global_trunc_bound}
    There exists an integer $n \geq -2$ such that every morphism in $\mathsf{I},\mathsf{P}$ in any context is $n$-truncated.\footnote{See \crtCref{remark:colimit_of_n_truncated} for a discussion of whether this assumption is necessary for \crtCref{main_theorem:free_E_monoidal_semiadditive}.}
<!-- end assumption-1 -->
<!-- proposition-93: body_md -->
The functor $F$ is an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functor.
<!-- end proposition-93 -->
<!-- proof-148: body_md -->
The functor $F_0$ is $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-continuous by assumption. Thus it is $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal for the cartesian structure. By \crtCref{prop:univ_prop_of_E_monoidal_span_half}, the functor $F$ is $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal as well.
<!-- end proof-148 -->
<!-- proposition-94: body_md -->
\label{prop:core_of_unst_F_is_associated_operad}
    We have an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal equivalence \[\bm{\mathsf{Un}}(F)^{\simeq2}\simeq \mathsf{C}^{\otimes}|_{{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})}.\]
<!-- end proposition-94 -->
<!-- proof-149: body_md -->
The inclusion of 
    \[{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})\hookrightarrow \bm{\mathsf{Span}^{1.5}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}, \mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})^{\mathrm{co}}\]
    agrees with the inclusion of the underlying $\mathcal{B}$-category and is $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal itself.

    Thus, the result follows from a general statement: the underlying $\infty$-category of a $1$-cocartesian fibration $p:\mathbb{P}\to \mathbb{X}$ between $(\infty,2)$-categories is the cocartesian fibration classifying the restriction of the functor $\mathbb{X}\to {\mathbf{Cat}}$ to $\mathbb{X}^{\simeq2}$.

    We now need to compare the two monoidal functors
    \[{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})\to \mathsf{Cat}:\]
    the one coming from $F$ and the one coming from the restriction of the $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal structure of $\mathsf{C}$.
    
    The restrictions to $(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}})^{\mathrm{op}}$ agree since they agree on the image $\mathsf{C}$ of $*$ and they both classify $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-continuous functors 
    \[(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}})^{\mathrm{op}}\to \mathsf{Cat}.\]

    By \crtCref{assumption:global_trunc_bound}, every morphism in $\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}}$ is truncated.\footnote{This is the only place in the construction where we use \crtCref{assumption:global_trunc_bound} about $\mathsf{I}$.}
    
    Then the two monoidal functors agree by \crtCref{thm:internal_uniqueness_of_unfurling}.
<!-- end proof-149 -->
<!-- lemma-15: body_md -->
\label{lem:lifting_of_adjunction_by_cocart_fibrations}
    Let 
    \[p:\mathbb{P}\to \mathbb{X}\]
    be a $1$-cocartesian fibration between $(\infty,2)$-categories. Then a cocartesian $1$-morphism $f:x\to y\in \mathbb{P}$ admits a left adjoint if and only if $p(f)$ admits a left adjoint.

    Moreover, a commutative square 
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
        x\ar[r,"f"]\ar[d] &y\ar[d]\\
        x'\ar[r,"f'"] & y'
    \end{tikzcd}\]
    of cocartesian edges is horizontally left adjointable if and only if the square 
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
        p(x)\ar[r,"p(f)"]\ar[d] &p(y)\ar[d]\\
        p(x')\ar[r,"p(f')"] & p(y')
    \end{tikzcd}\]
    is horizontally left adjointable.
<!-- end lemma-15 -->
<!-- proof-150: body_md -->
Let $r':x'\to y' \in \mathbb{P}$. If $r'$ has a left adjoint, then so does $r:=p(r')$ since $p$ is a $2$-functor and thus preserves adjunctions.

    Let $r':x'\to y'\in \mathbb{P}$ be a cocartesian edge. Suppose that $[r:x\to y ]= [p(r'):p(x')\to p(y')]$ has a left adjoint $l$. Then we want to show that $r'$ has a left adjoint.

    Let $\epsilon':e\to \mathrm{id}_{x'}$ be the $2$-cartesian lift of the counit $\epsilon:lr\to \mathrm{id}_x$. Then $p(e) = lr$ factors through $r$ and thus, since $r'$ is cocartesian, $e$ factors as a composition 
    \[x'\xrightarrow{r'} y' \xrightarrow{l'} x'.\]
    
    Let $\eta':f'\to r'l'$ be likewise a $2$-cartesian lift of the unit $\eta:\mathrm{id}_{y}\to rl$. By the zig-zag identity for $l\dashv r$, both $(r'*\epsilon')\circ(\eta'*r'):f'\circ r'\to r'$ and the identity $2$-morphism $r' \to r'$ are cartesian lifts of the identity $2$-morphism of $r$. Thus $f'\circ r' = r'$. By the universal property of the cocartesian edge $r'$, we get that $f' = \mathrm{id}_{y'}$ as both are sources of a $2$-cartesian lift of the same morphism. 

    We claim that $\eta',\epsilon'$ are unit and counit of an adjunction $l'\dashv r'$.
    The zig-zag identities follow from functoriality of cartesian lifts.

    The statement about the adjointability of squares is similar. The Beck-Chevalley property is preserved by any functor. The Beck-Chevalley property is reflected since $p$ induces right fibrations on mapping categories and right fibrations are conservative.
<!-- end proof-150 -->
<!-- proposition-95: body_md -->
The composition
    \[
    \mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}[A]^{\mathrm{op}}\xrightarrow{x'} \mathsf{C}^{\otimes}|_{{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})} \hookrightarrow \bm{\mathsf{Un}}(F)
    \]
    is an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}}[A]$-left adjointable functor.
<!-- end proposition-95 -->
<!-- proof-151: body_md -->
The composition above is $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal by \crtCref{prop:core_of_unst_F_is_associated_operad}.

    By \crtCref{lem:lifting_of_adjunction_by_cocart_fibrations}, to check that the composition is $\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}}[A]$-left adjointable, it is enough to check that the composition
    \[
    \mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}[A]^{\mathrm{op}}\xrightarrow{x'} \mathsf{C}^{\otimes}|_{{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})} \hookrightarrow \bm{\mathsf{Un}}(F) \to \bm{\mathsf{Span}^{1.5}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}, \mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})^{\mathrm{co}}
    \]
    is $\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}}[A]$-left adjointable.

    Note that the projection $\mathsf{C}^{\otimes}|_{{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})}\to {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}, \mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})$ is $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-continuous. Thus, by construction of $x'$, this composition is the $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}$-continuous functor $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}[A]^{\mathrm{op}}\to {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}, \mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})$ corresponding to the constant functor $A\to {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}, \mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})$  on $*$.

    Thus the functor $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}[A]^{\mathrm{op}}\to \bm{\mathsf{Span}^{1.5}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}, \mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})^{\mathrm{co}}$ factors as 
    \[\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}[A]^{\mathrm{op}}\to (\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}})^\mathrm{op} \hookrightarrow \bm{\mathsf{Span}^{1.5}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}, \mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})^{\mathrm{co}}.\]

    Note that the functor \[\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}[A]\to \mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}\] preserves pullbacks and sends $\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}}[A]$ to $\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}}$. Thus we get that the composition $\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}[A]^{\mathrm{op}}\to (\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}})^\mathrm{op} \hookrightarrow \bm{\mathsf{Span}^{1.5}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}}, \mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})^{\mathrm{co}}$ is $\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}}[A]$-left adjointable.
<!-- end proof-151 -->
<!-- proposition-96: body_md -->
Suppose $\mathsf{C}$ is a $\mathsf{P}$-cartesian $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category. Then the composition of $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functors
    \[\mathsf{E}\hookrightarrow {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}) \to \bm{\mathsf{Cat}}\] is $\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}}$-left adjointable.
<!-- end proposition-96 -->
<!-- proof-152: body_md -->
Let $[p:B\to A]\in \mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}}(A)$.
    The existence of the left adjoints $p^*$ to \[p_*\simeq p_\otimes: \mathsf{C}^{B}\to \mathsf{C}^A\] is immediate from the definition. The adjointability follows from the fact that the $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal structure of $\mathsf{C}$ is indexed by ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})$ and the declared base-change maps in that functoriality agree with the Beck-Chevalley transformations.
<!-- end proof-152 -->
<!-- corollary-26: body_md -->
\label{cor:extending_the_alg_structure_of_C_to_backwards_facing_morphisms}
    The $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal composition 
                                                                                           
    \[\mathsf{E}\hookrightarrow {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E}) \to \bm{\mathsf{Cat}}\]
    extends to an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functor of $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-categories:
    \[\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{1.5}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E})\to \bm{\mathsf{Cat}}.\]
<!-- end corollary-26 -->
<!-- proof-153: body_md -->
This is a direct application of \crtCref{prop:univ_prop_of_E_monoidal_span_half}.
<!-- end proof-153 -->
<!-- proposition-97: body_md -->
The upper morphism in the pullback above is lax $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal.
<!-- end proposition-97 -->
<!-- proof-154: body_md -->
Consider the following pullback in $\mathsf{Op}^{\mathsf{E}}$:
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
        \mathsf{P}\ar[d]\ar[r]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        &(\bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\Delta^1, \bm{\mathsf{Span}^{1.5}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}))^{\simeq2})^{\otimes}\ar[d,"t^{\otimes}"]\\
        {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\ar[r]
        & {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E})^{\otimes},
    \end{tikzcd}\]
    where the right and bottom arrows classify the lax $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functors on the right and bottom of the previous square.

    The functor $t$ in the previous square is a cocartesian fibration. Therefore, the right functor $t^\otimes$ of the diagram directly above is a cocartesian fibration. Therefore, the left functor in the diagram above is a cocartesian fibration. Thus, the operad $\mathsf{P}$ is associated to an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal structure on $(\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{1.5}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E})_{//*})^{\simeq 2}$ and the upper morphism is a morphism of operads encoding the promised lax $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal structure.
<!-- end proof-154 -->
<!-- proposition-98: body_md -->
\label{prop:oplax_slice_source_is_monoidal}
    The functor 
    \[(\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{1.5}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E})_{//*})^{\simeq 2}\xrightarrow{s} {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E})\]
    is $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal.
<!-- end proposition-98 -->
<!-- proof-155: body_md -->
We first show that the functor $s$ above is lax $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal.
    This functor is the composition of a lax $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functor with an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functor:
    \[(\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{1.5}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E})_{//*})^{\simeq 2}\xrightarrow{a} \bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\Delta^1, \bm{\mathsf{Span}^{1.5}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}))^{\simeq2}\xrightarrow{s} {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}).\]

    Next, we need to check that the composition is actually $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal. Let 
    \[x = (B\leftarrow B' \to A')\]
    be an object in $(\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{1.5}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E})_{//*})^{\simeq 2}(A')$. Let $p:A'\to A\in \mathsf{E}(A)$. We must check that $p_\otimes(s(x)) \to  s(p_\otimes (x))$ is an equivalence. 
    
    We first write the comparison map for $p_\otimes(a(x)) \to  a(p_\otimes (x))$ in 
    $\bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\Delta^1, \bm{\mathsf{Span}^{1.5}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}))^{\simeq2}(A)$:
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
    	{B} && {B} && B \\
    	&&& {B'} \\
    	{B'} &&&& B' \\
    	& {B'} \\
    	{A'} && {A'} && {A}.
    	\arrow[equal,from=1-3, to=1-1]
    	\arrow[equal,from=1-3, to=1-5]
    	\arrow[from=2-4, to=1-3]
    	\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125, rotate=90}, draw=none, from=2-4, to=1-5]
    	\arrow[equal,from=2-4, to=3-5]
    	\arrow[from=3-1, to=1-1]
    	\arrow[from=3-1, to=5-1]
    	                          
    	                          
    	\arrow[from=3-5, to=1-5]
    	\arrow[from=3-5, to=5-5]
        \arrow[equal,from=2-4, to=4-2]
    	\arrow[equal,from=4-2, to=3-1]
    	\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125, rotate=-90}, draw=none, from=4-2, to=5-1]
    	\arrow[from=4-2, to=5-3]
    	\arrow[equal,from=5-3, to=5-1]
    	\arrow[from=5-3, to=5-5]
    \end{tikzcd}\]
    This is sent by $s$ to the span in the upper edge, which is clearly an isomorphism.
<!-- end proof-155 -->
<!-- proposition-99: body_md -->
\label{prop:oplax_slice_S_is_monoidal}
    $\mathsf{S}$ is an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-subcategory.
<!-- end proposition-99 -->
<!-- proof-156: body_md -->
We must show that for any $s:B\to A\in \mathsf{E}(A)$, the functor \[s_\otimes: (\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{1.5}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E})_{//*})^{\simeq 2}(B)\to (\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{1.5}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E})_{//*})^{\simeq 2}(A)\] sends objects in $\mathsf{S}(B)$ to objects in $\mathsf{S}(A)$.
    
    This is clear by the description of objects and of the $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal structure above.
<!-- end proof-156 -->
<!-- proposition-100: body_md -->
The composition 
    \[\mathsf{S}\subset (\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{1.5}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E})_{//*})^{\simeq 2}
    \xrightarrow{s} {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E})\]
    is an equivalence of $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-categories.
<!-- end proposition-100 -->
<!-- proof-157: body_md -->
The composition is $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal by \crtCref{prop:oplax_slice_source_is_monoidal,prop:oplax_slice_S_is_monoidal}. Thus it is enough to check that it is an equivalence of $\mathcal{B}$-categories.
    
    To do that, the same proof as in \crtCref{prop:E_cart_S_is_equivalent_to_span} works in this case.
<!-- end proof-157 -->
<!-- proposition-101: body_md -->
The lax $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functor 
    \[s\circ T:{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E})\to \mathsf{Cat}\]
    is equivalent to the $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functor
    \[\widetilde{F}:{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E})\hookrightarrow {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\xrightarrow{F}\mathsf{Cat}.\]
<!-- end proposition-101 -->
<!-- proof-158: body_md -->
Consider the following diagram:
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
        \bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\Delta^1, \bm{\mathsf{Span}^{1.5}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}))^{\simeq2}& \bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\Delta^1, \bm{\mathsf{Cat}})^{\simeq2}\\
        {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}) & \mathsf{Cat}
        \arrow[from=1-1, to=1-2]
        \arrow["s", from=1-1, to=2-1]
        \arrow["s", from=1-2, to=2-2]
        \arrow[shift left=3, dashed, from=2-1, to=1-1]
        \arrow[from=2-1, to=2-2]
    \end{tikzcd}\]
    The solid arrows form a canonical commutative square of $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-categories. The left dashed arrow is the lax $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal section to $s$ factoring through $(\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{1.5}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E})_{//*})^{\simeq 2}$ constructed above. Its composite with $s$ is $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal and is equivalent to the identity as an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functor. 
    
    The functor $T$ is by definition the composition of the upper morphism with the section.

    Thus $s\circ T$ is equivalent to the bottom arrow in this diagram.

    The bottom arrow in this diagram is by definition the underlying $\mathcal{B}$-functor of the $\mathcal{B}$-$2$-functor defined in \crtCref{cor:extending_the_alg_structure_of_C_to_backwards_facing_morphisms}.

    By \crtCref{thm:internal_uniqueness_of_unfurling}, this functor agrees with the restriction of $F:{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\to \mathsf{Cat}$ because their restrictions to $\mathsf{E}$ agree by definition. Indeed, $\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}}$ is left cancellable because $\mathsf{P}$ is inductible (\crtCref{prop:from_local_class_to_subuniverse}), and every morphism in $\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}}$ is truncated by \crtCref{assumption:global_trunc_bound}.
    \footnote{This is the only place in the construction where we use that $\mathsf{P}$ satisfies \crtCref{assumption:global_trunc_bound}.}
<!-- end proof-158 -->
<!-- proposition-102: body_md -->
The lax $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functor 
    \[t\circ T:{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E})\to \mathsf{Cat}\]
    is equivalent to the lax $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functor
    \[\widetilde{G}:{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E})\to \left\{*\right\}\hookrightarrow {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E}^{\operatorname{full}},\mathsf{E})\xrightarrow{F}\mathsf{Cat}.\]
<!-- end proposition-102 -->
<!-- proof-159: body_md -->
Consider the following diagram of $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-categories and lax $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functors:
    \[\scalebox{0.75}{
    \begin{tikzcd}[ampersand replacement=\&]
        {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E})\ar[d,equal]\ar[r]
        \&(\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{1.5}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E})_{//*})^{\simeq 2}\ar[r]\ar[d,"t"]\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, dr]
        \&\bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\Delta^1, \bm{\mathsf{Span}^{1.5}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}))^{\simeq2}\ar[r]\ar[d,"t"]
        \& \bm{\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}}^{\operatorname{oplax}}(\Delta^1, \bm{\mathsf{Cat}})^{\simeq2}\ar[d,"t"]\\
        {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E})\ar[r]
        \&*\ar[r]
        \&{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E})\ar[r]
        \&\mathsf{Cat}.
    \end{tikzcd}
    }\]
    The left square is commutative since $*$ is the terminal $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category. The middle square is commutative since it is the pullback defining the $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-category $(\bm{\mathsf{Span}^{1.5}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E})_{//*})^{\simeq 2}$. The right square is a naturality square for $t$.
    
    The lower composition is $\widetilde{G}$ by definition. The upper composition followed by the rightmost arrow $t$ is $t\circ T$ by definition.
<!-- end proof-159 -->
<!-- proposition-103: body_md -->
$\psi$ is an equivalence for every $p:B\to A$.
<!-- end proposition-103 -->
<!-- proof-160: body_md -->
An object of $\mathsf{C}^{\otimes}|_{{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})}(B)$ is an object $q:C\to B\in {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})(B)$, that is, an object $q:C\to B\in \mathsf{E}(B)$, and an object $x\in \mathsf{C}(C)$.

    The functor $\Psi:\mathsf{C}^{\otimes}|_{{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})}(B)\to \mathsf{C}(B)$ by definition applies the component of $\alpha$ at $C$ in the context $B$. Thus, it sends $x$ to $q_\otimes(x)$.

    Thus, the composition of the upper morphism and the right morphism takes $x$ to $p_\otimes q_\otimes x$.

    The left morphism takes $(x,q:C\to B)\in \mathsf{C}^{\otimes}|_{{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})}(B)$ to $(x,p\circ q:C\to A)\in \mathsf{C}^{\otimes}|_{{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})}(A)$. Then $\Psi$ takes $(x,p\circ q:C\to A)$ to $(p\circ q)_\otimes x$.

    The natural transformation $\psi$ can be seen to be the natural isomorphism $(p\circ q)_\otimes x\simeq p_\otimes q_\otimes x$.
<!-- end proof-160 -->
<!-- corollary-27: body_md -->
\label{cor:xi_x_univ_is_id}
    The functor $x_{\operatorname{univ}}^A:A\to {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})[A]$ gives rise to an endofunctor \[\Xi_{x_{\operatorname{univ}}^A}:{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})[A]\to {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})[A].\]
    This functor is an equivalence.
<!-- end corollary-27 -->
<!-- proof-161: body_md -->
$\Xi_{x_{\operatorname{univ}}^A}$ is an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functor under the canonical $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functor from $\mathsf{E}[A]^{\simeq}$, that is, we have a commutative diagram:
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        &\mathsf{E}[A]^{\simeq}\ar[dl]\ar[dr]\\
        {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})[A]\ar[rr, "\Xi_{x_{\operatorname{univ}}^A}"'] && {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})[A].
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    Thus $\Xi_{x_{\operatorname{univ}}^A}$ is homotopic to the identity on groupoid cores.

    The anima of morphisms $C\to D$ in ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})[A](B)$ is the anima of iterated spans
    \[\begin{tikzcd}
         & C\ar[dl, "\pi_C"']\ar[dr, "p_C"]\\
        A & F\ar[u,"p"']\ar[d,"i"] & B\\
         & D\ar[ul, "\pi_D"]\ar[ur, "p_D"']\\
    \end{tikzcd}\]
    with $p\in \mathsf{P}(C)$ and $i\in \mathsf{I}(D)$.

    The morphisms associated with $p$ and $i$ come from the unit and counit, respectively, of the corresponding adjunctions determined by the $(\mathsf{P,I})$-ambidextrous $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal structure on ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})[A]$. Thus, $\Xi_{x_{\operatorname{univ}}^A}$ acts as the identity on this anima.

    We have shown that $\Xi_{x_{\operatorname{univ}}^A}$ restricts to the identity on groupoid cores and that it is homotopic to the identity on mapping spaces. Thus $\Xi_{x_{\operatorname{univ}}^A}$ is an equivalence.
<!-- end proof-161 -->
<!-- remark-19: body_md -->
It will follow later from \crtCref{thm:generalized_main_C} that this endofunctor is homotopic to the identity, as suggested by the proof.
<!-- end remark-19 -->
<!-- remark-20: body_md -->
The construction \[[x:A\to \mathsf{C}]\mapsto[\Xi_x:{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})[A]\to \mathsf{C}]\] is functorial in the sense that it lifts to a functor \[\Xi:{\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E},(\mathsf{P,I})-\oplus}(\mathsf{Cat})\times_{\mathsf{Cat}}\mathsf{Cat}_{A/} \to {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E},(\mathsf{P,I})-\oplus}(\mathsf{Cat})_{{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})[A]/}.\] Moreover, this functor fits into a commutative triangle:
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E},(\mathsf{P,I})-\oplus}(\mathsf{Cat})\times_{\mathsf{Cat}}\mathsf{Cat}_{A/}\ar[rr]\ar[rd]
        && {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E},(\mathsf{P,I})-\oplus}(\mathsf{Cat})_{{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})[A]/}\ar[dl]\\
        &\mathsf{Cat}.
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]

    Indeed, it is enough to verify that \[\Phi_x:{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})[A]\to \mathsf{C}^{\otimes}|_{{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})}\] is functorial, which is evident from the construction of $\Phi_x$.
<!-- end remark-20 -->
<!-- theorem-22: body_md -->
\label{thm:generalized_main_C}
    Let $\mathsf{E},\mathsf{P},\mathsf{I}$ satisfy the standing hypotheses of \crtCref{sec:proof_of_C}, including \crtCref{assumption:global_trunc_bound}.
    For every $A\in\mathcal{B}$, we have an equivalence of $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal $\mathcal{B}$-categories \[L_{\oplus}\mathsf{E}^{\simeq}[A]\simeq {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})[A].\]
<!-- end theorem-22 -->
<!-- proof-162: body_md -->
Applying the construction of $\Xi_x$ to the tautological object $A\to L_{\oplus}\mathsf{E}^{\simeq}[A]$ gives an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functor ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})[A]\to L_{\oplus}\mathsf{E}^{\simeq}[A]$. 
    
    
    We have a canonical $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functor $\mathsf{E}^{\simeq}[A]\to {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})[A]$ from the universal property described in \crtCref{prop:free_E_monoid_on_A} applied to $x_{\operatorname{univ}}^A$. By adjunction, we get an $\mathsf{E}$-monoidal functor $L_{\oplus}\mathsf{E}^{\simeq}[A]\to {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})[A]$.

    The composition 
        \[
        L_{\oplus}\mathsf{E}^{\simeq}[A]\to {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})[A]\to L_{\oplus}\mathsf{E}^{\simeq}[A]
        \]
    is canonically homotopic to the identity by the universal property of $L_{\oplus}\mathsf{E}^{\simeq}[A]$ (\crtCref{cor:existance_of_free_ambi_monoidal_category}), which combines the free-monoid universal property with the localization adjunction. 

    The composition \[{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})[A]\to L_{\oplus}\mathsf{E}^{\simeq}[A] \to {\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})[A]\] is canonically homotopic to $\Xi_{x_{\operatorname{univ}}^A}$ by the naturality of $\Xi$. Thus it is an equivalence by \crtCref{cor:xi_x_univ_is_id}.
<!-- end proof-162 -->
<!-- remark-21: body_md -->
\label{remark:colimit_of_n_truncated}
    It is natural to ask whether \crtCref{assumption:global_trunc_bound} is actually needed. Indeed, we used it to show that the $\mathcal{B}$-categories $\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}}$ and $\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}}$ are truncated. 
    
    Without the assumption, $\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}}$ and $\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}}$ are not necessarily truncated. Indeed, take $\mathcal{B} = \mathrm{Ani}$, take $\mathsf{I}$ to consist of morphisms with $\pi$-finite homotopy fibres, take $\mathsf{P}$ to consist of isomorphisms, and take $\mathsf{E}$ to consist of morphisms whose homotopy fibres admit countable CW structures. Then in $\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}}(*)$ we have the morphism
    \[\coprod_{n\in\mathbb{N}}B^nC_2 \to \mathbb{N}.\]
    This morphism is locally truncated on its target and is in $\mathsf{I}$ in the context of its target. However, this morphism is \emph{not} locally truncated in the context $*$.

    Nevertheless, we do not know if \crtCref{assumption:global_trunc_bound} is needed for the correctness of \crtCref{main_theorem:free_E_monoidal_semiadditive}.
<!-- end remark-21 -->
<!-- lemma-16: body_md -->
\label{lem:extension_of_formalisms_to_presheaves}
    The inclusion $\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})\subset \mathrm{Span}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{E})$ induces an equivalence of $\infty$-categories:
    \[
    \mathrm{Fun}^{\mathcal{B}-R}(\mathrm{Span}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{E}), \mathcal{D}) \simeq \mathrm{Fun}(\mathrm{Span}({C},{E}), \mathcal{D}).
    \]
<!-- end lemma-16 -->
<!-- proof-163: body_md -->
Note that $\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})\subset \mathrm{Span}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{E})$ is fully faithful. Thus, by \cite[Proposition 4.3.2.17]{HTT}, right Kan extension along it is fully faithful. It remains to show that its essential image consists precisely of those functors whose restriction to $\mathcal{B}^{\mathrm{op}}$ preserves limits. This follows from a very similar argument to \cite[Proposition A.5.16]{Mann6Functors}.
<!-- end proof-163 -->
<!-- proposition-104: body_md -->
\label{prop:2FF_are_E_mon}
    There is an equivalence of $\infty$-categories \[\mathrm{Fun}^{\mathcal{B}-R}(\mathrm{Span}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{E}), \mathrm{Cat})\simeq {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})(*).\]
<!-- end proposition-104 -->
<!-- proof-164: body_md -->
The equivalence of \crtCref{prop:extra_back_functoriality_for_E_monoidal_cats} induces an equivalence of $\infty$-categories on global sections
    \[
    {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})(*) \simeq \underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{\Omega}-\sqcap}({\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{\Omega},\mathsf{\Omega}_{\mathsf{E}}), \mathsf{Cat})(*).
    \]
    The right-hand side is a full sub-$\infty$-category of the $\infty$-category of $\mathcal{B}$-functors from ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{\Omega},\mathsf{\Omega}_{\mathsf{E}})$ to $\mathsf{Cat}$. 
    
    We get a functor 
    \[\theta:\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{\Omega}-\sqcap}({\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{\Omega},\mathsf{\Omega}_{\mathsf{E}}), \mathsf{Cat})(*)\to \mathrm{Fun}(\mathrm{Span}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{E}), \mathrm{Cat})\]
    as follows. We evaluate a $\mathcal{B}$-functor $F:{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{\Omega},\mathsf{\Omega}_{\mathsf{E}})\to \mathsf{Cat}$ at the terminal object $*$ to get a functor $\mathrm{Span}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{E})\to \mathrm{Cat}(\mathcal{B})$ and compose it with the global sections functor $\mathrm{Cat}(\mathcal{B})\to \mathrm{Cat}$.

    We show this functor lands in $\mathrm{Fun}^{\mathcal{B}-R}(\mathrm{Span}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{E}),\mathrm{Cat})$. Since $F$ preserves $\mathsf{\Omega}$-limits, the restriction of $\theta(F)$ to $\mathcal{B}^{\mathrm{op}}$ reconstructs the underlying $\mathcal{B}$-category of $F$. This functor is continuous by definition. 

    There is an inverse of $\theta$ which we will now explain how to construct. 
    
    Let $X\in \mathcal{B}$. Denote by $\mathrm{Span}(\mathcal{B}_{/X},\mathcal{E})$ the span $\infty$-category of $\mathcal{B}_{/X}$ with right-pointing maps that are in $\mathcal{E}$. There is a functor $(\mathcal{B}_{/X})^{\mathrm{op}}\times \mathrm{Span}(\mathcal{B}_{/X},\mathcal{E})\to \mathrm{Span}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{E})$ taking $A\to X \in (\mathcal{B}_{/X})^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $B\to X \in \mathrm{Span}(\mathcal{B}_{/X},\mathcal{E})$ to the pullback $A\times_X B$. It is not hard to see that this is functorial in $X\in \mathcal{B}^{\mathrm{op}}$ in the following sense:

    Given $G:\mathrm{Span}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{E})\to \mathrm{Cat}$ in $\mathrm{Fun}^{\mathcal{B}-R}(\mathrm{Span}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{E}),\mathrm{Cat})$, we get, functorially in $X\in \mathcal{B}^{\mathrm{op}}$, a functor \[{\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{\Omega},\mathsf{\Omega}_{\mathsf{E}})(X)\simeq  \mathrm{Span}(\mathcal{B}_{/X},\mathcal{E})\to \mathrm{Fun}^R((\mathcal{B}_{/X})^{\mathrm{op}}, \mathrm{Cat})\simeq \mathsf{Cat}(X).\]

    Checking that this constructs an inverse to $\theta$ is straightforward.
<!-- end proof-164 -->
<!-- theorem-23: body_md -->
\label{thm:equiv_between_2ff_and_E_monoidal}
    There is an equivalence of $\infty$-categories 
    \[\mathrm{Fun}(\mathrm{Span}({C},{E}), \mathrm{Cat})\simeq {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})(*).\]
<!-- end theorem-23 -->
<!-- proof-165: body_md -->
This is an immediate corollary of \crtCref{lem:extension_of_formalisms_to_presheaves,prop:2FF_are_E_mon}.
<!-- end proof-165 -->
<!-- proposition-105: body_md -->
\label{prop:adjointed_is_just_ambi}
    The equivalence of \crtCref{thm:equiv_between_2ff_and_E_monoidal} restricts to an equivalence \[\mathrm{Fun}^{({P},{I})\operatorname{-adjointed}}(\mathrm{Span}({C},{E}), \mathrm{Cat})\simeq {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E},(\mathsf{P},\mathsf{I})\text{-}\oplus}(\mathsf{Cat})(*).\]
<!-- end proposition-105 -->
<!-- proof-166: body_md -->
Unraveling the definitions, we can observe that the conditions are defined by the same inductive procedure.
<!-- end proof-166 -->
<!-- theorem-24: body_md -->
\label{thm:red_of_main_globally_trunc}
    Let ${C}$ be an $\infty$-category, and let ${E},{I},{P}\subset{C}$ be wide sub-$\infty$-categories that are stable under base change in ${C}$. Assume that ${I},{P}\subset{E}$ are left cancellable and that every morphism in ${I}$ and ${P}$ is $n$-truncated for some fixed $n\geq -2$. Let $a\in {C}$. Let $F\colon\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})\to\mathrm{Cat}$ denote the functor given by
    \[
    F(b):=\mathrm{Span}({E}[a](b),{P},{I}),
    \]
    obtained by composing the functor $b\mapsto({E}[a](b),{P},{I})$ with $\mathrm{Span}$. Then $F$ is the free $({P},{I})$-adjointed functor on $\mathrm{id}_a\in F(a)$.
<!-- end theorem-24 -->
<!-- proof-167: body_md -->
Let $A=\text{\usefont{U}{dmjhira}{m}{n}\symbol{"48}}(a)\in\mathcal{B}$ be the representable presheaf associated to $a$. By \crtCref{thm:generalized_main_C,prop:adjointed_is_just_ambi}, it remains to verify that ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})[A]$ corresponds to the functor $F\colon\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})\to\mathrm{Cat}$ given by $F(b):=\mathrm{Span}({E}[a](b),{P},{I})$. This follows by direct inspection, in the same way as in the proof of \cite[Theorem 4.20.]{CLLuniv}.
<!-- end proof-167 -->
<!-- proposition-106: body_md -->
\label{prop:main_thm_follows_from_truncated_case}
    Assume \crtCref{main_theorem:free_adjointed_2_cat} in the case where every morphism in ${I}$ and ${P}$ is $n$-truncated for some fixed $n$. Then \crtCref{main_theorem:free_adjointed_2_cat}   follows.
<!-- end proposition-106 -->
<!-- proof-168: body_md -->
Let ${P}_n\subset{P},{I}_n\subset{I}$ denote the wide sub-$\infty$-categories of morphisms which are $n$-truncated.
    
    By comparison of universal properties, it is enough to show that the following is a sequential colimit of $(\infty,2)$-categories:
    \begin{align*}
    \mathrm{Span}({C},{E})&=\mathbf{Span}^2({C},{E})^{{P}_{-2}}_{{I}_{-2}}\\
    &\to  \mathbf{Span}^2({C},{E})^{{P}_{-1}}_{{I}_{-1}}\\
    &\to \mathbf{Span}^2({C},{E})^{{P}_{0}}_{{I}_{0}} \to
    \hdots \\
    &\to \mathbf{Span}^2({C},{E})^{{P}_{n}}_{{I}_{n}}
    \to
    \hdots \\
    &\to \mathbf{Span}^2({C},{E})^{{P}}_{{I}}.
    \end{align*}

    This is a colimit diagram on the level of bisimplicial anima.
<!-- end proof-168 -->
<!-- definition-55: body_md -->
Let \[\widetilde{C}\to \mathrm{Span}(\mathrm{Fin})^{\mathrm{op}}\] denote the cartesian unstraightening of the functor 
    \[\mathrm{Span}(\mathrm{Fin})\xrightarrow{F_C}\mathrm{Cat}\]
    above. Let $\widetilde{E},\widetilde{P},\widetilde{I}\subset\widetilde{C}$ denote the wide sub-$\infty$-categories spanned by morphisms over isomorphisms in $\mathrm{Span}(\mathrm{Fin})^{\mathrm{op}}$ which are in $E,P,I$, respectively.
<!-- end definition-55 -->
<!-- lemma-17: body_md -->
$\widetilde{P},\widetilde{I}\subset \widetilde{E}\subset \widetilde{C}$ are wide sub-$\infty$-categories that are stable under base change in $\widetilde{C}$. Moreover, $\widetilde{P},\widetilde{I}$ are left cancellable, and every morphism in $\widetilde{P}$ and $\widetilde{I}$ is truncated.
<!-- end lemma-17 -->
<!-- proof-169: body_md -->
This follows by the same argument as in \cite[Lemma 5.5.]{CLLuniv}.
<!-- end proof-169 -->
<!-- proposition-107: body_md -->
\label{prop:span_commutes_with_tensor}
    We have an equivalence of $(\infty,2)$-categories 
    \[
    \mathbf{Span}^2(\widetilde{C},\widetilde{E})^{\widetilde{P}}_{\widetilde{I}}\simeq (\mathbf{Span}^2(C,E)^P_I)^\otimes.
    \]
<!-- end proposition-107 -->
<!-- proof-170: body_md -->
First, we know that $\mathrm{Span}(\widetilde{C},\widetilde{E}) \simeq \mathrm{Span}(C,E)^\otimes$ by \cite[Theorem 3.9]{haugseng2023twovariablefibrationsfactorisationsystems}. Thus, we get a functor 
    \[T:\mathrm{Span}(\widetilde{C},\widetilde{E})\to (\mathbf{Span}^2(C,E)^P_I)^\otimes.\]

    The rest of the proof follows the proof of \cite[Theorem 5.10.]{CLLuniv} closely. Namely, one shows that the functor $T$ satisfies the requirements of \crtCref{main_theorem:free_adjointed_2_cat} with respect to the quadruple $(\widetilde{C},\widetilde{E},\widetilde{P},
    \widetilde{I})$, gets a functor
    \[
        T':\mathbf{Span}^2(\widetilde{C},\widetilde{E})^{\widetilde{P}}_{\widetilde{I}}\to (\mathbf{Span}^2(C,E)^P_I)^\otimes
    \]
    and shows that $T'$ is an equivalence.
<!-- end proof-170 -->
<!-- lemma-18: body_md -->
\label{lemma:characterization_of_P_tensor_I_tenso_adjointed}
    Let $\mathbb{K}$ be a symmetric monoidal $(\infty,2)$-category. 
    Let
    \[f:\mathrm{Span}(C,E)\to \mathbb{K}\]
    be a lax symmetric monoidal functor. Then $f$ is $(P,I)$-adjointed if and only if the composition
    \[
    g:\mathrm{Span}(\widetilde{C},\widetilde{E})\simeq \mathrm{Span}(C,E)^\otimes\xrightarrow{f^\otimes} \mathbb{K}^\otimes
    \]
    is $(\widetilde{P},\widetilde{I})$-adjointed.
<!-- end lemma-18 -->
<!-- proof-171: body_md -->
Note that $\widetilde{P},\widetilde{I}\subset \mathrm{Span}(C,E)^\otimes\to \mathrm{Span}(\mathrm{Fin})$ live over the maximal subgroupoid $\mathrm{Fin}^\simeq\subset \mathrm{Span}(\mathrm{Fin})$. Thus, the lemma reduces to the following obvious claim:

    $f$ is $(P,I)$-adjointed if and only if, for any finite set $A$, $f^A:\mathrm{Span}(C,E)^A\to \mathbb{K}^A$ is $(P^A,I^A)$-adjointed.
<!-- end proof-171 -->
<!-- remark-22: body_md -->
In \cite{CLLuniv}, there is a requirement for the compatibility of the symmetric monoidal structure of $C$ with the adjointability condition (see \cite[Lemma 5.9.]{CLLuniv}). As the proof above suggests, in our case this additional condition is not needed.
<!-- end remark-22 -->
<!-- theorem-25: body_md -->
\label{thm:lax_monoidal_free_adjointed_2_cat}
    Let $(C,E,P,I)$ be as above and let $\mathbb{K}$ be a symmetric monoidal $(\infty,2)$-category. 
    We have a fully faithful embedding 
    \[\mathrm{Fun}^{\operatorname{lax}-\otimes}(\mathbf{Span}^2(C,E)^P_I,\mathbb{K})\hookrightarrow \mathrm{Fun}^{\operatorname{lax}-\otimes}(\mathrm{Span}(C,E),\mathbb{K}) 
    \]
    and the essential image is spanned by the lax symmetric monoidal functors whose underlying functors are $(P,I)$-adjointed.
<!-- end theorem-25 -->
<!-- proof-172: body_md -->
By \crtCref{prop:span_commutes_with_tensor} and \crtCref{main_theorem:free_adjointed_2_cat}, we have a fully faithful embedding
    \[\mathrm{Fun}_{/\mathrm{Span}(\mathrm{Fin})}((\mathbf{Span}^2(C,E)^P_I)^\otimes,\mathbb{K}^\otimes)\hookrightarrow \mathrm{Fun}_{/\mathrm{Span}(\mathrm{Fin})}(\mathrm{Span}(C,E)^\otimes,\mathbb{K}^\otimes) \]
    with essential image those functors that are $(\widetilde{P},\widetilde{I})$-adjointed.
    Restricting to functors that preserve $\mathrm{Fin}^{\mathrm{op}}$-cocartesian lifts, we get a fully faithful embedding
    \[\mathrm{Fun}^{\operatorname{lax}-\otimes}(\mathbf{Span}^2(C,E)^P_I,\mathbb{K})\hookrightarrow \mathrm{Fun}^{\operatorname{lax}-\otimes}(\mathrm{Span}(C,E),\mathbb{K}). 
    \]

    The characterization of the essential image follows from \crtCref{lemma:characterization_of_P_tensor_I_tenso_adjointed}.
<!-- end proof-172 -->
<!-- corollary-28: body_md -->
\label{cor:Mann_conj}
    Let $(C,E)$ be a geometric context and let 
    \[D:\mathrm{Span}(C,E)\to \mathrm{Cat}\]
    be a three-functor formalism. Let $P,I\subset E$ denote the wide sub-$\infty$-categories of $D$-proper and $D$-\'etale morphisms in $C$. Then $D$ extends uniquely to a lax symmetric monoidal $2$-functor
    \[D:\mathbf{Span}^2(C,E)^P_I\to {\mathbf{Cat}}.\]
<!-- end corollary-28 -->
<!-- proof-173: body_md -->
The fact that $P,I$ are stable under base change in $C$ and left cancellable, and that every morphism in $P$ and $I$ is truncated, was proved by Mann and Heyer (see \cite[Remark 4.6.5.]{just_6ff}). Thus this is a direct application of \crtCref{thm:lax_monoidal_free_adjointed_2_cat}.
<!-- end proof-173 -->
<!-- proposition-108: body_md -->
\label{prop:formalisms_equivalence_is_symmetric_monoidal}
    The equivalence of $\infty$-categories
    \[\mathrm{Fun}(\mathrm{Span}({C},{E}), \mathrm{Cat})\simeq {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})(*)\]
    established in \crtCref{thm:equiv_between_2ff_and_E_monoidal} lifts to a symmetric monoidal equivalence where the left-hand side is equipped with Day convolution and the right-hand side is equipped with the symmetric monoidal structure described in \crtCref{cor:E_monoidal_cats_are_symmetric_monoidal}.
<!-- end proposition-108 -->
<!-- proof-174: body_md -->
The equivalence
    \[\mathrm{Fun}(\mathrm{Span}({C},{E}), \mathrm{Cat})\simeq {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})(*)\]
    is given by the universal property of $\mathrm{Fun}(\mathrm{Span}({C},{E}), \mathrm{Cat})$ in the $\infty$-category of $\mathrm{Cat}$-modules in $\mathrm{Pr}^{\mathrm{L}}$ applied to the functor 
    \[i:\mathrm{Span}({C},{E})^{\mathrm{op}}\hookrightarrow {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})(*).\]
    The functor $i$ is clearly symmetric monoidal, since it identifies with a symmetric monoidal sub-$\infty$-category of the $\mathcal{B}$-Yoneda image of 
    \[\underline{\mathsf{Fun}}^{\mathsf{\Omega}-\sqcap}({\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{\Omega},\mathsf{\Omega}_{\mathsf{E}}), \mathsf{Cat})(*)\simeq {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})(*).\]
<!-- end proof-174 -->
<!-- proposition-109: body_md -->
\label{prop:adjointed_formalisms_as_modules}
    There are equivalences of $\infty$-categories
    \[\mathrm{Fun}^{(P,I)\operatorname{-adjointed}}(\mathrm{Span}({C},{E}), \mathrm{Cat})\simeq \operatorname{Mod}_{h_*}(\mathrm{Fun}(\mathrm{Span}({C},{E}), \mathrm{Cat}))\]
    and
    \[\mathrm{Fun}^{\operatorname{lax}-\otimes,(P,I)\operatorname{-adjointed}}(\mathrm{Span}({C},{E}), \mathrm{Cat})\simeq \operatorname{CAlg}_{h_*}(\mathrm{Fun}(\mathrm{Span}({C},{E}), \mathrm{Cat})).\]
<!-- end proposition-109 -->
<!-- proof-175: body_md -->
The first equivalence follows since $h_*$ corresponds to $L_{(\mathsf{P,I})-\oplus}(\mathsf{E}^{\simeq})$ which is an idempotent algebra in ${\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})(*)$ together with the identification of \crtCref{prop:adjointed_is_just_ambi}.

    The second equivalence follows from the first together with the identification of commutative algebras for Day convolution with lax symmetric monoidal functors, using \crtCref{thm:lax_monoidal_free_adjointed_2_cat}.
<!-- end proof-175 -->
<!-- remark-23: body_md -->
\label{remark:presheaf_case_without_uniform_truncation}
    On the other hand, direct comparison shows that $h_*$ corresponds to ${\mathsf{Span}}(\mathsf{E},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{P}},\mathsf{E}_{\mathsf{I}})\in {\mathsf{CMon}}^{\mathsf{E}}(\mathsf{Cat})(*)$. Thus, in this case, \crtCref{main_theorem:free_E_monoidal_semiadditive} holds without the additional uniform truncation bound of \crtCref{assumption:global_trunc_bound}.
<!-- end remark-23 -->
